Potential drift issue: if blog/posts/*.md changes, build_blog.dart syncs, then build_site --check in CI would fail (drift) unless the artifacts are committed. That's fine, by design.

Bug candidates I noticed in build_site.dart:

1. `renderBlogPostPage` cover figure: `${cover != null && (coverFromBody || !body.contains(']($cover)')) ? ...}` — after stripping the cover image from body, body no longer contains '](cover)'. Hmm, logic: if coverFromBody is true, show cover figure. If coverFromBody false but cover != null and body doesn't contain the image link, show cover figure. If the cover was NOT stripped (i.e., the body's cover line differs, e.g., extra whitespace/attributes in the markdown image), then the markdown renderer will inline the image and figure is omitted. Seems plausible. Edge: `body.contains(']($cover)')` would also be false if the cover image appears later in the body... then a duplicate cover would be rendered? If cover appears later in body, coverFromBody false (only first non-empty line matching), and body doesn't contain... wait it does contain. OK.

2. In `blogIndexBlock`, when a post has no cover, only h2; when cover, image + h2. Fine.

3. `_videoEmbed` youtube regex `[\w-]+` fine.

4. `loadPosts` reads file twice (readAsStringSync twice) — minor perf, trivial.

5. Escape issue in `_nav` prefix interpolation `${prefix}blog/` — fine.

6. In `docsLinkRewriter`, GitHub link: `'$repoUrl/blob/main/docs/${href...}'` — but href could be like `./redaction.md` — strips `./`. But if href is `../foo.md` it would produce wrong URL `docs/../foo.md`. Minor.

7. `buildLlmsFull` budget uses `text.length` — Dart string length is UTF-16 code units, not bytes. `llmsFullBudgetBytes` compared against char count, not bytes. If content has non-ASCII (em-dashes, emoji), actual bytes > chars, so the byte budget is not enforced correctly — file could exceed 150KB while passing. That's a real correctness issue (IMPORTANT or minor). The PR description says "87 KB, under the 150 KB budget, builder-enforced". File.writeAsStringSync writes UTF-8, so bytes on disk = UTF-8 byte count. Comparing `text.length` (code units) against byte budget overestimates capacity for ASCII (equal) but for non-ASCII text.length < byte count... actually for non-ASCII, UTF-8 bytes ≥ code units. So the check could pass while file exceeds budget. Severity: SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT. It's a claimed enforcement; use utf8.encode(text).length.

8. Check-mode `_generatedPageDirs` in main writes `entity.path.substring(root.length + 1)` — root may be absolute path; on check mode path comparisons use repo-relative dirs; expectedPaths are 'site/blog/slug/index.html' relative. OK.

# gh-1476: [GOAL] fa1.dev GEO/agent-optimization: be as legible to AI agents and search as marinamogilko.co

## Description

# [GOAL] fa1.dev GEO/agent-optimization: be as legible to AI agents and search as marinamogilko.co

## Product frame

One sentence: **fa1.dev stops being a JS-shell brochure and becomes a first-class citizen of the agent web — every meaningful page is crawlable without JavaScript, every AI crawler is explicitly welcomed, and llms.txt/llms-full.txt + structured data give LLMs citation-ready facts about Fa — modelled on marinamogilko.co, a reference-grade GEO/SEO site.**

Why it matters: users increasingly discover tools by asking ChatGPT/Claude/Perplexity "what's a good open-source coding agent for Flutter" — if agents can't READ the site, Fa doesn't exist in that answer. Our own product is an agent; our site being agent-illegible is both a marketing hole and a credibility joke.

## Reference analysis — what marinamogilko.co does (verified 2026-10-09)

1. **robots.txt explicitly welcomes AI crawlers by name**: `GPTBot`, `ChatGPT-User`, `Google-Extended`, `ClaudeBot`, `anthropic-ai`, `PerplexityBot`, `CCBot`, `Applebot-Extended` — each with `Allow: /`, plus a comment pointing to llms.txt. (fa1.dev: bare `User-agent: *` only.)
2. **llms.txt as a citation-ready fact sheet**: quotable blocks with hard numbers and named entities (subscribers, guests, awards), key pages, topic list — written so an LLM can lift answers verbatim. (fa1.dev HAS a decent 167-line llms.txt — keep and extend.)
3. **JSON-LD knowledge graph**: `@graph` with `Person` + `PodcastSeries` + `Organization` + `WebSite`; per-episode `PodcastEpisode` schema.
4. **Content moat, server-rendered**: every episode is a static page with the FULL TRANSCRIPT in raw HTML (84 KB, zero JS needed) — agents and search get the substance, not a shell.
5. **Living sitemap**: per-URL real `lastmod` (updated days ago), priorities.
6. Complete OG/Twitter card set with image dimensions and alt text.

## fa1.dev gap analysis (verified against live site + `site/` in this repo)

Already good (do not regress): meta description + robots meta, OG/Twitter with dims+alt, JSON-LD ×3 (`SoftwareApplication`, `FAQPage`, `HowTo`), 167-line llms.txt with quotable FAQ, sitemap.xml exists.

Gaps, ranked by impact:

- **G1 — the blog is invisible to agents.** `site/blog/` is a 3 KB JS shell + `posts.json`; post content renders client-side. Posts are absent from the sitemap. To a crawler/agent the blog is an empty page. (Marina's equivalent — episode transcripts — is her biggest GEO asset.)
- **G2 — robots.txt doesn't name AI crawlers** and doesn't point at llms.txt.
- **G3 — no `llms-full.txt`** (the emerging llms.txt companion: full documentation text for agents with big context windows).
- **G4 — JSON-LD misses the graph**: no `Organization`, no `WebSite`, `SoftwareApplication` lacks `sameAs` (GitHub repo, pub.dev), no `SoftwareSourceCode` with `codeRepository`. Knowledge-panel and entity-linking signals stay on the table.
- **G5 — sitemap is small and stale**: 5 URLs, `/app/` lastmod 2026-07-25; blog posts and any future pages never appear; `lastmod` is hand-maintained (drifts).
- **G6 — repo docs stay invisible**: `docs/*.md` (redaction, tool-availability, dap, …) never reach the site as crawlable HTML — exactly the deep content agents could quote.

## Design

### D1 — static pre-render build step (the core fix)

`site/` is framework-free static files; keep it that way — add a small build script (`site/build.sh` or Dart/make — pick what's already used for install.sh templating) that:
- renders every `blog/posts/*.md` to its own static HTML page (`/blog/<slug>/index.html`) with full content in raw HTML;
- emits `BlogPosting` JSON-LD per post (headline, datePublished/dateModified from file front-matter or git, author → Organization);
- regenerates `sitemap.xml` from the actual page inventory with real `lastmod` (file mtime / git log);
- assembles `llms-full.txt` = llms.txt header + concatenated curated docs (blog posts + selected `docs/*.md` pages), each section headed by its canonical URL.
The deploy pipeline runs the build; hand-editing generated files is forbidden (generated = rebuild in CI check).

### D2 — robots.txt AI welcome mat

Explicit per-bot `Allow: /` blocks for: `GPTBot`, `OAI-SearchBot`, `ChatGPT-User`, `Google-Extended`, `ClaudeBot`, `anthropic-ai`, `PerplexityBot`, `Perplexity-User`, `CCBot`, `Applebot-Extended`, `Meta-ExternalAgent` — plus the header comment pointing to `/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt`. (Keep `User-agent: * Allow: /` + sitemap line.)

### D3 — JSON-LD graph completion

Add `Organization` (author/maintainer entity with `url` + `sameAs` GitHub org), `WebSite` (name, url), `SoftwareSourceCode` (`codeRepository` → github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, `runtimePlatform` Dart), and `sameAs` on the existing `SoftwareApplication` → GitHub repo + pub.dev package page. One `@graph`, validated.

### D4 — sitemap as generated artifact

All indexable pages + every blog post, real `lastmod`, priorities sane (1.0 home, 0.8 posts). Generated by D1 — never hand-edited.

### D5 — docs surfacing (bounded)

Pick 3-5 agent-quotable docs pages (e.g. tool-availability, redaction, sessions/compaction overview) → static HTML under `/docs/`, `TechArticle` JSON-LD, in sitemap + llms-full.txt. Full docs-site publishing is a separate card.

## Threat model / risks

- **Stale generated artifacts** — CI check rebuilds and diffs (sitemap/llms-full/blog HTML must match sources; red = rebuild).
- **llms-full.txt bloat** — cap at ~100-150 KB of curated text; it's a context-window budget, not a dump of the repo.
- **Duplicate-content SEO** — canonical URLs on every page; blog markdown stays single-source, HTML is generated from it.
- **No secrets/PII** — static public content only; nothing from sessions/memory paths.

## Test matrix

- **No-JS crawl test (the GEO invariant)**: `curl` (no JS) of `/`, `/blog/`, every `/blog/<slug>/`, `/docs/<page>/` must contain the page's core text (assert on distinctive strings) — this test would have caught G1.
- **Schema validation**: every JSON-LD block parses and validates against schema.org types (scripted check in CI; Google Rich Results Test manually post-deploy).
- **robots.txt contract**: named AI bots each present with `Allow: /`; llms pointers present; sitemap line intact.
- **Sitemap integrity**: every `<loc>` returns 200; every indexable page is in the sitemap; `lastmod` ≤ source mtime.
- **llms.txt / llms-full.txt**: served 200, text/plain, llms-full contains each linked doc's canonical URL header.
- **REG**: existing OG/Twitter/FAQ/HowTo/SoftwareApplication blocks byte-stable (unless intentionally extended); lighthouse SEO score ≥ current (target 100).

## Acceptance

1. Blog posts crawlable without JS, each in sitemap with real lastmod + BlogPosting schema.
2. robots.txt names the AI crawlers + points at llms files.
3. `/llms-full.txt` live with curated full text.
4. JSON-LD graph: Organization + WebSite + SoftwareSourceCode + sameAs links; validators green.
5. CI fails on stale generated artifacts; no-JS crawl test green.
6. Post-deploy: Rich Results Test shows the new entities; site verified discoverable via an AI-agent query smoke ("what is Fa flutter agent harness" → fa1.dev facts quoted).

## Non-goals

- Full documentation site / docs framework (Docusaurus etc.) — D5 is deliberately 3-5 pages.
- Multilingual versions, hreflang.
- Search-ads/keyword campaigning — this card is machine-legibility, not SEM.
- Redesign/visual changes to the landing.

## References

- Reference site: https://marinamogilko.co/ (robots.txt, llms.txt, JSON-LD @graph, episode transcripts — all verified 2026-10-09)
- Site source: `site/` in this repo (blog shell: `site/blog/`, single post: `site/blog/posts/2026-09-20-we-burned-40-billion-tokens.md`)
- llms.txt spec: https://llmstxt.org/

Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # gh-1476: [GOAL] fa1.dev GEO/agent-optimization: be as legible to AI agents and search as marinamogilko.co

## Description

# [GOAL] fa1.dev GEO/agent-optimization: be as legible to AI agents and search as marinamogilko.co

## Product frame

One sentence: **fa1.dev stops being a JS-shell brochure and becomes a first-class citizen of the agent web — every meaningful page is crawlable without JavaScript, every AI crawler is explicitly welcomed, and llms.txt/llms-full.txt + structured data give LLMs citation-ready facts about Fa — modelled on marinamogilko.co, a reference-grade GEO/SEO site.**

Why it matters: users increasingly discover tools by asking ChatGPT/Claude/Perplexity "what's a good open-source coding agent for Flutter" — if agents can't READ the site, Fa doesn't exist in that answer. Our own product is an agent; our site being agent-illegible is both a marketing hole and a credibility joke.

## Reference analysis — what marinamogilko.co does (verified 2026-10-09)

1. **robots.txt explicitly welcomes AI crawlers by name**: `GPTBot`, `ChatGPT-User`, `Google-Extended`, `ClaudeBot`, `anthropic-ai`, `PerplexityBot`, `CCBot`, `Applebot-Extended` — each with `Allow: /`, plus a comment pointing to llms.txt. (fa1.dev: bare `User-agent: *` only.)
2. **llms.txt as a citation-ready fact sheet**: quotable blocks with hard numbers and named entities (subscribers, guests, awards), key pages, topic list — written so an LLM can lift answers verbatim. (fa1.dev HAS a decent 167-line llms.txt — keep and extend.)
3. **JSON-LD knowledge graph**: `@graph` with `Person` + `PodcastSeries` + `Organization` + `WebSite`; per-episode `PodcastEpisode` schema.
4. **Content moat, server-rendered**: every episode is a static page with the FULL TRANSCRIPT in raw HTML (84 KB, zero JS needed) — agents and search get the substance, not a shell.
5. **Living sitemap**: per-URL real `lastmod` (updated days ago), priorities.
6. Complete OG/Twitter card set with image dimensions and alt text.

## fa1.dev gap analysis (verified against live site + `site/` in this repo)

Already good (do not regress): meta description + robots meta, OG/Twitter with dims+alt, JSON-LD ×3 (`SoftwareApplication`, `FAQPage`, `HowTo`), 167-line llms.txt with quotable FAQ, sitemap.xml exists.

Gaps, ranked by impact:

- **G1 — the blog is invisible to agents.** `site/blog/` is a 3 KB JS shell + `posts.json`; post content renders client-side. Posts are absent from the sitemap. To a crawler/agent the blog is an empty page. (Marina's equivalent — episode transcripts — is her biggest GEO asset.)
- **G2 — robots.txt doesn't name AI crawlers** and doesn't point at llms.txt.
- **G3 — no `llms-full.txt`** (the emerging llms.txt companion: full documentation text for agents with big context windows).
- **G4 — JSON-LD misses the graph**: no `Organization`, no `WebSite`, `SoftwareApplication` lacks `sameAs` (GitHub repo, pub.dev), no `SoftwareSourceCode` with `codeRepository`. Knowledge-panel and entity-linking signals stay on the table.
- **G5 — sitemap is small and stale**: 5 URLs, `/app/` lastmod 2026-07-25; blog posts and any future pages never appear; `lastmod` is hand-maintained (drifts).
- **G6 — repo docs stay invisible**: `docs/*.md` (redaction, tool-availability, dap, …) never reach the site as crawlable HTML — exactly the deep content agents could quote.

## Design

### D1 — static pre-render build step (the core fix)

`site/` is framework-free static files; keep it that way — add a small build script (`site/build.sh` or Dart/make — pick what's already used for install.sh templating) that:
- renders every `blog/posts/*.md` to its own static HTML page (`/blog/<slug>/index.html`) with full content in raw HTML;
- emits `BlogPosting` JSON-LD per post (headline, datePublished/dateModified from file front-matter or git, author → Organization);
- regenerates `sitemap.xml` from the actual page inventory with real `lastmod` (file mtime / git log);
- assembles `llms-full.txt` = llms.txt header + concatenated curated docs (blog posts + selected `docs/*.md` pages), each section headed by its canonical URL.
The deploy pipeline runs the build; hand-editing generated files is forbidden (generated = rebuild in CI check).

### D2 — robots.txt AI welcome mat

Explicit per-bot `Allow: /` blocks for: `GPTBot`, `OAI-SearchBot`, `ChatGPT-User`, `Google-Extended`, `ClaudeBot`, `anthropic-ai`, `PerplexityBot`, `Perplexity-User`, `CCBot`, `Applebot-Extended`, `Meta-ExternalAgent` — plus the header comment pointing to `/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt`. (Keep `User-agent: * Allow: /` + sitemap line.)

### D3 — JSON-LD graph completion

Add `Organization` (author/maintainer entity with `url` + `sameAs` GitHub org), `WebSite` (name, url), `SoftwareSourceCode` (`codeRepository` → github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, `runtimePlatform` Dart), and `sameAs` on the existing `SoftwareApplication` → GitHub repo + pub.dev package page. One `@graph`, validated.

### D4 — sitemap as generated artifact

All indexable pages + every blog post, real `lastmod`, priorities sane (1.0 home, 0.8 posts). Generated by D1 — never hand-edited.

### D5 — docs surfacing (bounded)

Pick 3-5 agent-quotable docs pages (e.g. tool-availability, redaction, sessions/compaction overview) → static HTML under `/docs/`, `TechArticle` JSON-LD, in sitemap + llms-full.txt. Full docs-site publishing is a separate card.

## Threat model / risks

- **Stale generated artifacts** — CI check rebuilds and diffs (sitemap/llms-full/blog HTML must match sources; red = rebuild).
- **llms-full.txt bloat** — cap at ~100-150 KB of curated text; it's a context-window budget, not a dump of the repo.
- **Duplicate-content SEO** — canonical URLs on every page; blog markdown stays single-source, HTML is generated from it.
- **No secrets/PII** — static public content only; nothing from sessions/memory paths.

## Test matrix

- **No-JS crawl test (the GEO invariant)**: `curl` (no JS) of `/`, `/blog/`, every `/blog/<slug>/`, `/docs/<page>/` must contain the page's core text (assert on distinctive strings) — this test would have caught G1.
- **Schema validation**: every JSON-LD block parses and validates against schema.org types (scripted check in CI; Google Rich Results Test manually post-deploy).
- **robots.txt contract**: named AI bots each present with `Allow: /`; llms pointers present; sitemap line intact.
- **Sitemap integrity**: every `<loc>` returns 200; every indexable page is in the sitemap; `lastmod` ≤ source mtime.
- **llms.txt / llms-full.txt**: served 200, text/plain, llms-full contains each linked doc's canonical URL header.
- **REG**: existing OG/Twitter/FAQ/HowTo/SoftwareApplication blocks byte-stable (unless intentionally extended); lighthouse SEO score ≥ current (target 100).

## Acceptance

1. Blog posts crawlable without JS, each in sitemap with real lastmod + BlogPosting schema.
2. robots.txt names the AI crawlers + points at llms files.
3. `/llms-full.txt` live with curated full text.
4. JSON-LD graph: Organization + WebSite + SoftwareSourceCode + sameAs links; validators green.
5. CI fails on stale generated artifacts; no-JS crawl test green.
6. Post-deploy: Rich Results Test shows the new entities; site verified discoverable via an AI-agent query smoke ("what is Fa flutter agent harness" → fa1.dev facts quoted).

## Non-goals

- Full documentation site / docs framework (Docusaurus etc.) — D5 is deliberately 3-5 pages.
- Multilingual versions, hreflang.
- Search-ads/keyword campaigning — this card is machine-legibility, not SEM.
- Redesign/visual changes to the landing.

## References

- Reference site: https://marinamogilko.co/ (robots.txt, llms.txt, JSON-LD @graph, episode transcripts — all verified 2026-10-09)
- Site source: `site/` in this repo (blog shell: `site/blog/`, single post: `site/blog/posts/2026-09-20-we-burned-40-billion-tokens.md`)
- llms.txt spec: https://llmstxt.org/

Potential drift issue: if blog/posts/*.md changes, build_blog.dart syncs, then build_site --check in CI would fail (drift) unless the artifacts are committed. That's fine, by design.

Bug candidates I noticed in build_site.dart:

1. `renderBlogPostPage` cover figure: `${cover != null && (coverFromBody || !body.contains(']($cover)')) ? ...}` — after stripping the cover image from body, body no longer contains '](cover)'. Hmm, logic: if coverFromBody is true, show cover figure. If coverFromBody false but cover != null and body doesn't contain the image link, show cover figure. If the cover was NOT stripped (i.e., the body's cover line differs, e.g., extra whitespace/attributes in the markdown image), then the markdown renderer will inline the image and figure is omitted. Seems plausible. Edge: `body.contains(']($cover)')` would also be false if the cover image appears later in the body... then a duplicate cover would be rendered? If cover appears later in body, coverFromBody false (only first non-empty line matching), and body doesn't contain... wait it does contain. OK.

2. In `blogIndexBlock`, when a post has no cover, only h2; when cover, image + h2. Fine.

7. `buildLlmsFull` budget uses `text.length` — Dart string length is UTF-16 code units, not bytes. `llmsFullBudgetBytes` compared against char count, not bytes. If content has non-ASCII (em-dashes, emoji), actual bytes > chars, so the byte budget is not enforced correctly — file could exceed 150KB while passing. That's a real correctness issue (IMPORTANT or minor). The PR description says "87 KB, under the 150 KB budget, builder-enforced". File.writeAsStringSync writes UTF-8, so bytes on disk = UTF-8 byte count. Comparing `text.length` (code units) against byte budget overestimates capacity for ASCII (equal) but for non-ASCII text.length < byte count... actually for non-ASCII, UTF-8 bytes ≥ code units. So the check could pass while file exceeds budget. Severity: SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT. It's a claimed enforcement; use utf8.encode(text).length.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,

pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# gh-1476: [GOAL] fa1.dev GEO/agent-optimization: be as legible to AI agents and search as marinamogilko.co

## Description

# [GOAL] fa1.dev GEO/agent-optimization: be as legible to AI agents and search as marinamogilko.co

## Product frame

One sentence: **fa1.dev stops being a JS-shell brochure and becomes a first-class citizen of the agent web — every meaningful page is crawlable without JavaScript, every AI crawler is explicitly welcomed, and llms.txt/llms-full.txt + structured data give LLMs citation-ready facts about Fa — modelled on marinamogilko.co, a reference-grade GEO/SEO site.**

Why it matters: users increasingly discover tools by asking ChatGPT/Claude/Perplexity "what's a good open-source coding agent for Flutter" — if agents can't READ the site, Fa doesn't exist in that answer. Our own product is an agent; our site being agent-illegible is both a marketing hole and a credibility joke.

## Reference analysis — what marinamogilko.co does (verified 2026-10-09)

1. **robots.txt explicitly welcomes AI crawlers by name**: `GPTBot`, `ChatGPT-User`, `Google-Extended`, `ClaudeBot`, `anthropic-ai`, `PerplexityBot`, `CCBot`, `Applebot-Extended` — each with `Allow: /`, plus a comment pointing to llms.txt. (fa1.dev: bare `User-agent: *` only.)
2. **llms.txt as a citation-ready fact sheet**: quotable blocks with hard numbers and named entities (subscribers, guests, awards), key pages, topic list — written so an LLM can lift answers verbatim. (fa1.dev HAS a decent 167-line llms.txt — keep and extend.)
3. **JSON-LD knowledge graph**: `@graph` with `Person` + `PodcastSeries` + `Organization` + `WebSite`; per-episode `PodcastEpisode` schema.
4. **Content moat, server-rendered**: every episode is a static page with the FULL TRANSCRIPT in raw HTML (84 KB, zero JS needed) — agents and search get the substance, not a shell.
5. **Living sitemap**: per-URL real `lastmod` (updated days ago), priorities.
6. Complete OG/Twitter card set with image dimensions and alt text.

## fa1.dev gap analysis (verified against live site + `site/` in this repo)

Already good (do not regress): meta description + robots meta, OG/Twitter with dims+alt, JSON-LD ×3 (`SoftwareApplication`, `FAQPage`, `HowTo`), 167-line llms.txt with quotable FAQ, sitemap.xml exists.

Gaps, ranked by impact:

- **G1 — the blog is invisible to agents.** `site/blog/` is a 3 KB JS shell + `posts.json`; post content renders client-side. Posts are absent from the sitemap. To a crawler/agent the blog is an empty page. (Marina's equivalent — episode transcripts — is her biggest GEO asset.)
- **G2 — robots.txt doesn't name AI crawlers** and doesn't point at llms.txt.
- **G3 — no `llms-full.txt`** (the emerging llms.txt companion: full documentation text for agents with big context windows).
- **G4 — JSON-LD misses the graph**: no `Organization`, no `WebSite`, `SoftwareApplication` lacks `sameAs` (GitHub repo, pub.dev), no `SoftwareSourceCode` with `codeRepository`. Knowledge-panel and entity-linking signals stay on the table.
- **G5 — sitemap is small and stale**: 5 URLs, `/app/` lastmod 2026-07-25; blog posts and any future pages never appear; `lastmod` is hand-maintained (drifts).
- **G6 — repo docs stay invisible**: `docs/*.md` (redaction, tool-availability, dap, …) never reach the site as crawlable HTML — exactly the deep content agents could quote.

## Design

### D1 — static pre-render build step (the core fix)

`site/` is framework-free static files; keep it that way — add a small build script (`site/build.sh` or Dart/make — pick what's already used for install.sh templating) that:
- renders every `blog/posts/*.md` to its own static HTML page (`/blog/<slug>/index.html`) with full content in raw HTML;
- emits `BlogPosting` JSON-LD per post (headline, datePublished/dateModified from file front-matter or git, author → Organization);
- regenerates `sitemap.xml` from the actual page inventory with real `lastmod` (file mtime / git log);
- assembles `llms-full.txt` = llms.txt header + concatenated curated docs (blog posts + selected `docs/*.md` pages), each section headed by its canonical URL.
The deploy pipeline runs the build; hand-editing generated files is forbidden (generated = rebuild in CI check).

### D2 — robots.txt AI welcome mat

Explicit per-bot `Allow: /` blocks for: `GPTBot`, `OAI-SearchBot`, `ChatGPT-User`, `Google-Extended`, `ClaudeBot`, `anthropic-ai`, `PerplexityBot`, `Perplexity-User`, `CCBot`, `Applebot-Extended`, `Meta-ExternalAgent` — plus the header comment pointing to `/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt`. (Keep `User-agent: * Allow: /` + sitemap line.)

### D3 — JSON-LD graph completion

Add `Organization` (author/maintainer entity with `url` + `sameAs` GitHub org), `WebSite` (name, url), `SoftwareSourceCode` (`codeRepository` → github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, `runtimePlatform` Dart), and `sameAs` on the existing `SoftwareApplication` → GitHub repo + pub.dev package page. One `@graph`, validated.

### D4 — sitemap as generated artifact

All indexable pages + every blog post, real `lastmod`, priorities sane (1.0 home, 0.8 posts). Generated by D1 — never hand-edited.

### D5 — docs surfacing (bounded)

Pick 3-5 agent-quotable docs pages (e.g. tool-availability, redaction, sessions/compaction overview) → static HTML under `/docs/`, `TechArticle` JSON-LD, in sitemap + llms-full.txt. Full docs-site publishing is a separate card.

## Threat model / risks

- **Stale generated artifacts** — CI check rebuilds and diffs (sitemap/llms-full/blog HTML must match sources; red = rebuild).
- **llms-full.txt bloat** — cap at ~100-150 KB of curated text; it's a context-window budget, not a dump of the repo.
- **Duplicate-content SEO** — canonical URLs on every page; blog markdown stays single-source, HTML is generated from it.
- **No secrets/PII** — static public content only; nothing from sessions/memory paths.

## Test matrix

- **No-JS crawl test (the GEO invariant)**: `curl` (no JS) of `/`, `/blog/`, every `/blog/<slug>/`, `/docs/<page>/` must contain the page's core text (assert on distinctive strings) — this test would have caught G1.
- **Schema validation**: every JSON-LD block parses and validates against schema.org types (scripted check in CI; Google Rich Results Test manually post-deploy).
- **robots.txt contract**: named AI bots each present with `Allow: /`; llms pointers present; sitemap line intact.
- **Sitemap integrity**: every `<loc>` returns 200; every indexable page is in the sitemap; `lastmod` ≤ source mtime.
- **llms.txt / llms-full.txt**: served 200, text/plain, llms-full contains each linked doc's canonical URL header.
- **REG**: existing OG/Twitter/FAQ/HowTo/SoftwareApplication blocks byte-stable (unless intentionally extended); lighthouse SEO score ≥ current (target 100).

## Acceptance

1. Blog posts crawlable without JS, each in sitemap with real lastmod + BlogPosting schema.
2. robots.txt names the AI crawlers + points at llms files.
3. `/llms-full.txt` live with curated full text.
4. JSON-LD graph: Organization + WebSite + SoftwareSourceCode + sameAs links; validators green.
5. CI fails on stale generated artifacts; no-JS crawl test green.
6. Post-deploy: Rich Results Test shows the new entities; site verified discoverable via an AI-agent query smoke ("what is Fa flutter agent harness" → fa1.dev facts quoted).

## Non-goals

- Full documentation site / docs framework (Docusaurus etc.) — D5 is deliberately 3-5 pages.
- Multilingual versions, hreflang.
- Search-ads/keyword campaigning — this card is machine-legibility, not SEM.
- Redesign/visual changes to the landing.

## References

- Reference site: https://marinamogilko.co/ (robots.txt, llms.txt, JSON-LD @graph, episode transcripts — all verified 2026-10-09)
- Site source: `site/` in this repo (blog shell: `site/blog/`, single post: `site/blog/posts/2026-09-20-we-burned-40-billion-tokens.md`)
- llms.txt spec: https://llmstxt.org/

blocks.text:
Now let me look at site_markdown.dart. Also I noticed a potential bug: `blogIndexBlock` — the marker start string is `<!-- #blog-post-list:start` (without closing `-->`), and in the template the block start line becomes `$blogIndexStart — generated by ... -->`. Check mode: `blogIndex.indexOf(blogIndexStart)` — ok.

Also note in pages.yml deploy: runs `dart scripts/build_blog.dart` then `dart scripts/build_site.dart`. But CI check runs only `dart scripts/build_site.dart --check`. If build_blog.dart regenerates site/blog/posts from blog/posts, does the check gate cover that? The PR says "kept in sync with blog/posts/ by scripts/build_blog.dart". Potential drift issue: if blog/posts/*.md changes, build_blog.dart syncs, then build_site --check in CI would fail (drift) unless the artifacts are committed. That's fine, by design.

Bug candidates I noticed in build_site.dart:

1. `renderBlogPostPage` cover figure: `${cover != null && (coverFromBody || !body.contains(']($cover)')) ? ...}` — after stripping the cover image from body, body no longer contains '](cover)'. Hmm, logic: if coverFromBody is true, show cover figure. If coverFromBody false but cover != null and body doesn't contain the image link, show cover figure. If the cover was NOT stripped (i.e., the body's cover line differs, e.g., extra whitespace/attributes in the markdown image), then the markdown renderer will inline the image and figure is omitted. Seems plausible. Edge: `body.contains(']($cover)')` would also be false if the cover image appears later in the body... then a duplicate cover would be rendered? If cover appears later in body, coverFromBody false (only first non-empty line matching), and body doesn't contain... wait it does contain. OK.

2. In `blogIndexBlock`, when a post has no cover, only h2; when cover, image + h2. Fine.

3. `_videoEmbed` youtube regex `[\w-]+` fine.

4. `loadPosts` reads file twice (readAsStringSync twice) — minor perf, trivial.

5. Escape issue in `_nav` prefix interpolation `${prefix}blog/` — fine.

6. In `docsLinkRewriter`, GitHub link: `'$repoUrl/blob/main/docs/${href...}'` — but href could be like `./redaction.md` — strips `./`. But if href is `../foo.md` it would produce wrong URL `docs/../foo.md`. Minor.

7. `buildLlmsFull` budget uses `text.length` — Dart string length is UTF-16 code units, not bytes. `llmsFullBudgetBytes` compared against char count, not bytes. If content has non-ASCII (em-dashes, emoji), actual bytes > chars, so the byte budget is not enforced correctly — file could exceed 150KB while passing. Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# gh-1476: [GOAL] fa1.dev GEO/agent-optimization: be as legible to AI agents and search as marinamogilko.co

## Description

# [GOAL] fa1.dev GEO/agent-optimization: be as legible to AI agents and search as marinamogilko.co

## Product frame

One sentence: **fa1.dev stops being a JS-shell brochure and becomes a first-class citizen of the agent web — every meaningful page is crawlable without JavaScript, every AI crawler is explicitly welcomed, and llms.txt/llms-full.txt + structured data give LLMs citation-ready facts about Fa — modelled on marinamogilko.co, a reference-grade GEO/SEO site.**

Why it matters: users increasingly discover tools by asking ChatGPT/Claude/Perplexity "what's a good open-source coding agent for Flutter" — if agents can't READ the site, Fa doesn't exist in that answer. Our own product is an agent; our site being agent-illegible is both a marketing hole and a credibility joke.

## Reference analysis — what marinamogilko.co does (verified 2026-10-09)

1. **robots.txt explicitly welcomes AI crawlers by name**: `GPTBot`, `ChatGPT-User`, `Google-Extended`, `ClaudeBot`, `anthropic-ai`, `PerplexityBot`, `CCBot`, `Applebot-Extended` — each with `Allow: /`, plus a comment pointing to llms.txt. (fa1.dev: bare `User-agent: *` only.)
2. **llms.txt as a citation-ready fact sheet**: quotable blocks with hard numbers and named entities (subscribers, guests, awards), key pages, topic list — written so an LLM can lift answers verbatim. (fa1.dev HAS a decent 167-line llms.txt — keep and extend.)
3. **JSON-LD knowledge graph**: `@graph` with `Person` + `PodcastSeries` + `Organization` + `WebSite`; per-episode `PodcastEpisode` schema.
4. **Content moat, server-rendered**: every episode is a static page with the FULL TRANSCRIPT in raw HTML (84 KB, zero JS needed) — agents and search get the substance, not a shell.
5. **Living sitemap**: per-URL real `lastmod` (updated days ago), priorities.
6. Complete OG/Twitter card set with image dimensions and alt text.

## fa1.dev gap analysis (verified against live site + `site/` in this repo)

Already good (do not regress): meta description + robots meta, OG/Twitter with dims+alt, JSON-LD ×3 (`SoftwareApplication`, `FAQPage`, `HowTo`), 167-line llms.txt with quotable FAQ, sitemap.xml exists.

Gaps, ranked by impact:

- **G1 — the blog is invisible to agents.** `site/blog/` is a 3 KB JS shell + `posts.json`; post content renders client-side. Posts are absent from the sitemap. To a crawler/agent the blog is an empty page. (Marina's equivalent — episode transcripts — is her biggest GEO asset.)
- **G2 — robots.txt doesn't name AI crawlers** and doesn't point at llms.txt.
- **G3 — no `llms-full.txt`** (the emerging llms.txt companion: full documentation text for agents with big context windows).
- **G4 — JSON-LD misses the graph**: no `Organization`, no `WebSite`, `SoftwareApplication` lacks `sameAs` (GitHub repo, pub.dev), no `SoftwareSourceCode` with `codeRepository`. Knowledge-panel and entity-linking signals stay on the table.
- **G5 — sitemap is small and stale**: 5 URLs, `/app/` lastmod 2026-07-25; blog posts and any future pages never appear; `lastmod` is hand-maintained (drifts).
- **G6 — repo docs stay invisible**: `docs/*.md` (redaction, tool-availability, dap, …) never reach the site as crawlable HTML — exactly the deep content agents could quote.

## Design

### D1 — static pre-render build step (the core fix)

`site/` is framework-free static files; keep it that way — add a small build script (`site/build.sh` or Dart/make — pick what's already used for install.sh templating) that:
- renders every `blog/posts/*.md` to its own static HTML page (`/blog/<slug>/index.html`) with full content in raw HTML;
- emits `BlogPosting` JSON-LD per post (headline, datePublished/dateModified from file front-matter or git, author → Organization);
- regenerates `sitemap.xml` from the actual page inventory with real `lastmod` (file mtime / git log);
- assembles `llms-full.txt` = llms.txt header + concatenated curated docs (blog posts + selected `docs/*.md` pages), each section headed by its canonical URL.
The deploy pipeline runs the build; hand-editing generated files is forbidden (generated = rebuild in CI check).

### D2 — robots.txt AI welcome mat

Explicit per-bot `Allow: /` blocks for: `GPTBot`, `OAI-SearchBot`, `ChatGPT-User`, `Google-Extended`, `ClaudeBot`, `anthropic-ai`, `PerplexityBot`, `Perplexity-User`, `CCBot`, `Applebot-Extended`, `Meta-ExternalAgent` — plus the header comment pointing to `/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt`. (Keep `User-agent: * Allow: /` + sitemap line.)

### D3 — JSON-LD graph completion

Add `Organization` (author/maintainer entity with `url` + `sameAs` GitHub org), `WebSite` (name, url), `SoftwareSourceCode` (`codeRepository` → github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, `runtimePlatform` Dart), and `sameAs` on the existing `SoftwareApplication` → GitHub repo + pub.dev package page. One `@graph`, validated.

### D4 — sitemap as generated artifact

All indexable pages + every blog post, real `lastmod`, priorities sane (1.0 home, 0.8 posts). Generated by D1 — never hand-edited.

### D5 — docs surfacing (bounded)

Pick 3-5 agent-quotable docs pages (e.g. tool-availability, redaction, sessions/compaction overview) → static HTML under `/docs/`, `TechArticle` JSON-LD, in sitemap + llms-full.txt. Full docs-site publishing is a separate card.

## Threat model / risks

- **Stale generated artifacts** — CI check rebuilds and diffs (sitemap/llms-full/blog HTML must match sources; red = rebuild).
- **llms-full.txt bloat** — cap at ~100-150 KB of curated text; it's a context-window budget, not a dump of the repo.
- **Duplicate-content SEO** — canonical URLs on every page; blog markdown stays single-source, HTML is generated from it.
- **No secrets/PII** — static public content only; nothing from sessions/memory paths.

## Test matrix

- **No-JS crawl test (the GEO invariant)**: `curl` (no JS) of `/`, `/blog/`, every `/blog/<slug>/`, `/docs/<page>/` must contain the page's core text (assert on distinctive strings) — this test would have caught G1.
- **Schema validation**: every JSON-LD block parses and validates against schema.org types (scripted check in CI; Google Rich Results Test manually post-deploy).
- **robots.txt contract**: named AI bots each present with `Allow: /`; llms pointers present; sitemap line intact.
- **Sitemap integrity**: every `<loc>` returns 200; every indexable page is in the sitemap; `lastmod` ≤ source mtime.
- **llms.txt / llms-full.txt**: served 200, text/plain, llms-full contains each linked doc's canonical URL header.
- **REG**: existing OG/Twitter/FAQ/HowTo/SoftwareApplication blocks byte-stable (unless intentionally extended); lighthouse SEO score ≥ current (target 100).

## Acceptance

1. Blog posts crawlable without JS, each in sitemap with real lastmod + BlogPosting schema.
2. robots.txt names the AI crawlers + points at llms files.
3. `/llms-full.txt` live with curated full text.
4. JSON-LD graph: Organization + WebSite + SoftwareSourceCode + sameAs links; validators green.
5. CI fails on stale generated artifacts; no-JS crawl test green.
6. Post-deploy: Rich Results Test shows the new entities; site verified discoverable via an AI-agent query smoke ("what is Fa flutter agent harness" → fa1.dev facts quoted).

## Non-goals

- Full documentation site / docs framework (Docusaurus etc.) — D5 is deliberately 3-5 pages.
- Multilingual versions, hreflang.
- Search-ads/keyword campaigning — this card is machine-legibility, not SEM.
- Redesign/visual changes to the landing.

## References

- Reference site: https://marinamogilko.co/ (robots.txt, llms.txt, JSON-LD @graph, episode transcripts — all verified 2026-10-09)
- Site source: `site/` in this repo (blog shell: `site/blog/`, single post: `site/blog/posts/2026-09-20-we-burned-40-billion-tokens.md`)
- llms.txt spec: https://llmstxt.org/

# gh-1476: [GOAL] fa1.dev GEO/agent-optimization: be as legible to AI agents and search as marinamogilko.co

## Description

# [GOAL] fa1.dev GEO/agent-optimization: be as legible to AI agents and search as marinamogilko.co

## Product frame

One sentence: **fa1.dev stops being a JS-shell brochure and becomes a first-class citizen of the agent web — every meaningful page is crawlable without JavaScript, every AI crawler is explicitly welcomed, and llms.txt/llms-full.txt + structured data give LLMs citation-ready facts about Fa — modelled on marinamogilko.co, a reference-grade GEO/SEO site.**

Why it matters: users increasingly discover tools by asking ChatGPT/Claude/Perplexity "what's a good open-source coding agent for Flutter" — if agents can't READ the site, Fa doesn't exist in that answer. Our own product is an agent; our site being agent-illegible is both a marketing hole and a credibility joke.

## Reference analysis — what marinamogilko.co does (verified 2026-10-09)

1. **robots.txt explicitly welcomes AI crawlers by name**: `GPTBot`, `ChatGPT-User`, `Google-Extended`, `ClaudeBot`, `anthropic-ai`, `PerplexityBot`, `CCBot`, `Applebot-Extended` — each with `Allow: /`, plus a comment pointing to llms.txt. (fa1.dev: bare `User-agent: *` only.)
2. **llms.txt as a citation-ready fact sheet**: quotable blocks with hard numbers and named entities (subscribers, guests, awards), key pages, topic list — written so an LLM can lift answers verbatim. (fa1.dev HAS a decent 167-line llms.txt — keep and extend.)
3. **JSON-LD knowledge graph**: `@graph` with `Person` + `PodcastSeries` + `Organization` + `WebSite`; per-episode `PodcastEpisode` schema.
4. **Content moat, server-rendered**: every episode is a static page with the FULL TRANSCRIPT in raw HTML (84 KB, zero JS needed) — agents and search get the substance, not a shell.
5. **Living sitemap**: per-URL real `lastmod` (updated days ago), priorities.
6. Complete OG/Twitter card set with image dimensions and alt text.

## fa1.dev gap analysis (verified against live site + `site/` in this repo)

Already good (do not regress): meta description + robots meta, OG/Twitter with dims+alt, JSON-LD ×3 (`SoftwareApplication`, `FAQPage`, `HowTo`), 167-line llms.txt with quotable FAQ, sitemap.xml exists.

Gaps, ranked by impact:

- **G1 — the blog is invisible to agents.** `site/blog/` is a 3 KB JS shell + `posts.json`; post content renders client-side. Posts are absent from the sitemap. To a crawler/agent the blog is an empty page. (Marina's equivalent — episode transcripts — is her biggest GEO asset.)
- **G2 — robots.txt doesn't name AI crawlers** and doesn't point at llms.txt.
- **G3 — no `llms-full.txt`** (the emerging llms.txt companion: full documentation text for agents with big context windows).
- **G4 — JSON-LD misses the graph**: no `Organization`, no `WebSite`, `SoftwareApplication` lacks `sameAs` (GitHub repo, pub.dev), no `SoftwareSourceCode` with `codeRepository`. Knowledge-panel and entity-linking signals stay on the table.
- **G5 — sitemap is small and stale**: 5 URLs, `/app/` lastmod 2026-07-25; blog posts and any future pages never appear; `lastmod` is hand-maintained (drifts).
- **G6 — repo docs stay invisible**: `docs/*.md` (redaction, tool-availability, dap, …) never reach the site as crawlable HTML — exactly the deep content agents could quote.

## Design

### D1 — static pre-render build step (the core fix)

`site/` is framework-free static files; keep it that way — add a small build script (`site/build.sh` or Dart/make — pick what's already used for install.sh templating) that:
- renders every `blog/posts/*.md` to its own static HTML page (`/blog/<slug>/index.html`) with full content in raw HTML;
- emits `BlogPosting` JSON-LD per post (headline, datePublished/dateModified from file front-matter or git, author → Organization);
- regenerates `sitemap.xml` from the actual page inventory with real `lastmod` (file mtime / git log);
- assembles `llms-full.txt` = llms.txt header + concatenated curated docs (blog posts + selected `docs/*.md` pages), each section headed by its canonical URL.
The deploy pipeline runs the build; hand-editing generated files is forbidden (generated = rebuild in CI check).

### D2 — robots.txt AI welcome mat

Explicit per-bot `Allow: /` blocks for: `GPTBot`, `OAI-SearchBot`, `ChatGPT-User`, `Google-Extended`, `ClaudeBot`, `anthropic-ai`, `PerplexityBot`, `Perplexity-User`, `CCBot`, `Applebot-Extended`, `Meta-ExternalAgent` — plus the header comment pointing to `/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt`. (Keep `User-agent: * Allow: /` + sitemap line.)

### D3 — JSON-LD graph completion

Add `Organization` (author/maintainer entity with `url` + `sameAs` GitHub org), `WebSite` (name, url), `SoftwareSourceCode` (`codeRepository` → github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, `runtimePlatform` Dart), and `sameAs` on the existing `SoftwareApplication` → GitHub repo + pub.dev package page. One `@graph`, validated.

### D4 — sitemap as generated artifact

All indexable pages + every blog post, real `lastmod`, priorities sane (1.0 home, 0.8 posts). Generated by D1 — never hand-edited.

### D5 — docs surfacing (bounded)

Pick 3-5 agent-quotable docs pages (e.g. tool-availability, redaction, sessions/compaction overview) → static HTML under `/docs/`, `TechArticle` JSON-LD, in sitemap + llms-full.txt. Full docs-site publishing is a separate card.

## Threat model / risks

- **Stale generated artifacts** — CI check rebuilds and diffs (sitemap/llms-full/blog HTML must match sources; red = rebuild).
- **llms-full.txt bloat** — cap at ~100-150 KB of curated text; it's a context-window budget, not a dump of the repo.
- **Duplicate-content SEO** — canonical URLs on every page; blog markdown stays single-source, HTML is generated from it.
- **No secrets/PII** — static public content only; nothing from sessions/memory paths.

## Test matrix

- **No-JS crawl test (the GEO invariant)**: `curl` (no JS) of `/`, `/blog/`, every `/blog/<slug>/`, `/docs/<page>/` must contain the page's core text (assert on distinctive strings) — this test would have caught G1.
- **Schema validation**: every JSON-LD block parses and validates against schema.org types (scripted check in CI; Google Rich Results Test manually post-deploy).
- **robots.txt contract**: named AI bots each present with `Allow: /`; llms pointers present; sitemap line intact.
- **Sitemap integrity**: every `<loc>` returns 200; every indexable page is in the sitemap; `lastmod` ≤ source mtime.
- **llms.txt / llms-full.txt**: served 200, text/plain, llms-full contains each linked doc's canonical URL header.
- **REG**: existing OG/Twitter/FAQ/HowTo/SoftwareApplication blocks byte-stable (unless intentionally extended); lighthouse SEO score ≥ current (target 100).

## Acceptance

1. Blog posts crawlable without JS, each in sitemap with real lastmod + BlogPosting schema.
2. robots.txt names the AI crawlers + points at llms files.
3. `/llms-full.txt` live with curated full text.
4. JSON-LD graph: Organization + WebSite + SoftwareSourceCode + sameAs links; validators green.
5. CI fails on stale generated artifacts; no-JS crawl test green.
6. Post-deploy: Rich Results Test shows the new entities; site verified discoverable via an AI-agent query smoke ("what is Fa flutter agent harness" → fa1.dev facts quoted).

## Non-goals

- Full documentation site / docs framework (Docusaurus etc.) — D5 is deliberately 3-5 pages.
- Multilingual versions, hreflang.
- Search-ads/keyword campaigning — this card is machine-legibility, not SEM.
- Redesign/visual changes to the landing.

## References

- Reference site: https://marinamogilko.co/ (robots.txt, llms.txt, JSON-LD @graph, episode transcripts — all verified 2026-10-09)
- Site source: `site/` in this repo (blog shell: `site/blog/`, single post: `site/blog/posts/2026-09-20-we-burned-40-billion-tokens.md`)
- llms.txt spec: https://llmstxt.org/

# gh-1476: [GOAL] fa1.dev GEO/agent-optimization: be as legible to AI agents and search as marinamogilko.co

## Description

# [GOAL] fa1.dev GEO/agent-optimization: be as legible to AI agents and search as marinamogilko.co

## Product frame

One sentence: **fa1.dev stops being a JS-shell brochure and becomes a first-class citizen of the agent web — every meaningful page is crawlable without JavaScript, every AI crawler is explicitly welcomed, and llms.txt/llms-full.txt + structured data give LLMs citation-ready facts about Fa — modelled on marinamogilko.co, a reference-grade GEO/SEO site.**

Why it matters: users increasingly discover tools by asking ChatGPT/Claude/Perplexity "what's a good open-source coding agent for Flutter" — if agents can't READ the site, Fa doesn't exist in that answer. Our own product is an agent; our site being agent-illegible is both a marketing hole and a credibility joke.

## Reference analysis — what marinamogilko.co does (verified 2026-10-09)

1. **robots.txt explicitly welcomes AI crawlers by name**: `GPTBot`, `ChatGPT-User`, `Google-Extended`, `ClaudeBot`, `anthropic-ai`, `PerplexityBot`, `CCBot`, `Applebot-Extended` — each with `Allow: /`, plus a comment pointing to llms.txt. (fa1.dev: bare `User-agent: *` only.)
2. **llms.txt as a citation-ready fact sheet**: quotable blocks with hard numbers and named entities (subscribers, guests, awards), key pages, topic list — written so an LLM can lift answers verbatim. (fa1.dev HAS a decent 167-line llms.txt — keep and extend.)
3. **JSON-LD knowledge graph**: `@graph` with `Person` + `PodcastSeries` + `Organization` + `WebSite`; per-episode `PodcastEpisode` schema.
4. **Content moat, server-rendered**: every episode is a static page with the FULL TRANSCRIPT in raw HTML (84 KB, zero JS needed) — agents and search get the substance, not a shell.
5. **Living sitemap**: per-URL real `lastmod` (updated days ago), priorities.
6. Complete OG/Twitter card set with image dimensions and alt text.

## fa1.dev gap analysis (verified against live site + `site/` in this repo)

Already good (do not regress): meta description + robots meta, OG/Twitter with dims+alt, JSON-LD ×3 (`SoftwareApplication`, `FAQPage`, `HowTo`), 167-line llms.txt with quotable FAQ, sitemap.xml exists.

Gaps, ranked by impact:

- **G1 — the blog is invisible to agents.** `site/blog/` is a 3 KB JS shell + `posts.json`; post content renders client-side. Posts are absent from the sitemap. To a crawler/agent the blog is an empty page. (Marina's equivalent — episode transcripts — is her biggest GEO asset.)
- **G2 — robots.txt doesn't name AI crawlers** and doesn't point at llms.txt.
- **G3 — no `llms-full.txt`** (the emerging llms.txt companion: full documentation text for agents with big context windows).
- **G4 — JSON-LD misses the graph**: no `Organization`, no `WebSite`, `SoftwareApplication` lacks `sameAs` (GitHub repo, pub.dev), no `SoftwareSourceCode` with `codeRepository`. Knowledge-panel and entity-linking signals stay on the table.
- **G5 — sitemap is small and stale**: 5 URLs, `/app/` lastmod 2026-07-25; blog posts and any future pages never appear; `lastmod` is hand-maintained (drifts).
- **G6 — repo docs stay invisible**: `docs/*.md` (redaction, tool-availability, dap, …) never reach the site as crawlable HTML — exactly the deep content agents could quote.

## Design

### D1 — static pre-render build step (the core fix)

`site/` is framework-free static files; keep it that way — add a small build script (`site/build.sh` or Dart/make — pick what's already used for install.sh templating) that:
- renders every `blog/posts/*.md` to its own static HTML page (`/blog/<slug>/index.html`) with full content in raw HTML;
- emits `BlogPosting` JSON-LD per post (headline, datePublished/dateModified from file front-matter or git, author → Organization);
- regenerates `sitemap.xml` from the actual page inventory with real `lastmod` (file mtime / git log);
- assembles `llms-full.txt` = llms.txt header + concatenated curated docs (blog posts + selected `docs/*.md` pages), each section headed by its canonical URL.
The deploy pipeline runs the build; hand-editing generated files is forbidden (generated = rebuild in CI check).

### D2 — robots.txt AI welcome mat

Explicit per-bot `Allow: /` blocks for: `GPTBot`, `OAI-SearchBot`, `ChatGPT-User`, `Google-Extended`, `ClaudeBot`, `anthropic-ai`, `PerplexityBot`, `Perplexity-User`, `CCBot`, `Applebot-Extended`, `Meta-ExternalAgent` — plus the header comment pointing to `/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt`. (Keep `User-agent: * Allow: /` + sitemap line.)

### D3 — JSON-LD graph completion

Add `Organization` (author/maintainer entity with `url` + `sameAs` GitHub org), `WebSite` (name, url), `SoftwareSourceCode` (`codeRepository` → github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, `runtimePlatform` Dart), and `sameAs` on the existing `SoftwareApplication` → GitHub repo + pub.dev package page. One `@graph`, validated.

### D4 — sitemap as generated artifact

All indexable pages + every blog post, real `lastmod`, priorities sane (1.0 home, 0.8 posts). Generated by D1 — never hand-edited.

### D5 — docs surfacing (bounded)

Pick 3-5 agent-quotable docs pages (e.g. tool-availability, redaction, sessions/compaction overview) → static HTML under `/docs/`, `TechArticle` JSON-LD, in sitemap + llms-full.txt. Full docs-site publishing is a separate card.

## Threat model / risks

- **Stale generated artifacts** — CI check rebuilds and diffs (sitemap/llms-full/blog HTML must match sources; red = rebuild).
- **llms-full.txt bloat** — cap at ~100-150 KB of curated text; it's a context-window budget, not a dump of the repo.
- **Duplicate-content SEO** — canonical URLs on every page; blog markdown stays single-source, HTML is generated from it.
- **No secrets/PII** — static public content only; nothing from sessions/memory paths.

## Test matrix

- **No-JS crawl test (the GEO invariant)**: `curl` (no JS) of `/`, `/blog/`, every `/blog/<slug>/`, `/docs/<page>/` must contain the page's core text (assert on distinctive strings) — this test would have caught G1.
- **Schema validation**: every JSON-LD block parses and validates against schema.org types (scripted check in CI; Google Rich Results Test manually post-deploy).
- **robots.txt contract**: named AI bots each present with `Allow: /`; llms pointers present; sitemap line intact.
- **Sitemap integrity**: every `<loc>` returns 200; every indexable page is in the sitemap; `lastmod` ≤ source mtime.
- **llms.txt / llms-full.txt**: served 200, text/plain, llms-full contains each linked doc's canonical URL header.
- **REG**: existing OG/Twitter/FAQ/HowTo/SoftwareApplication blocks byte-stable (unless intentionally extended); lighthouse SEO score ≥ current (target 100).

## Acceptance

1. Blog posts crawlable without JS, each in sitemap with real lastmod + BlogPosting schema.
2. robots.txt names the AI crawlers + points at llms files.
3. `/llms-full.txt` live with curated full text.
4. JSON-LD graph: Organization + WebSite + SoftwareSourceCode + sameAs links; validators green.
5. CI fails on stale generated artifacts; no-JS crawl test green.
6. Post-deploy: Rich Results Test shows the new entities; site verified discoverable via an AI-agent query smoke ("what is Fa flutter agent harness" → fa1.dev facts quoted).

## Non-goals

- Full documentation site / docs framework (Docusaurus etc.) — D5 is deliberately 3-5 pages.
- Multilingual versions, hreflang.
- Search-ads/keyword campaigning — this card is machine-legibility, not SEM.
- Redesign/visual changes to the landing.

## References

- Reference site: https://marinamogilko.co/ (robots.txt, llms.txt, JSON-LD @graph, episode transcripts — all verified 2026-10-09)
- Site source: `site/` in this repo (blog shell: `site/blog/`, single post: `site/blog/posts/2026-09-20-we-burned-40-billion-tokens.md`)
- llms.txt spec: https://llmstxt.org/

      # find-exec guard (gh-1232 AC2) is gone: one enforcement point, no

      # Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +
      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed a build containing /app/ (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 2: no base tag to patch.
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          echo '<html></html>' > "$d/build/index.html"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad2.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an unpatchable base tag (AC1 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 3: a missing touchpoint file.
          rm "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad3.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an incomplete build (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # fa1.dev parity pin: both web builds must keep the identical
          # release flags AND the same pinned SDK — the bundle's only edit
          # stays the base tag.
          for wf in .github/workflows/pages.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml; do
            grep -q -- '--release' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost the --release web flag (#1100 parity)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q -- '--base-href /app/' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost --base-href /app/ (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q "flutter-version: '3.47.x'" "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf unpinned Flutter SDK (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }

      - name: CRAP badge/config sync guard
