# find-exec guard (gh-1232 AC2) is gone: one enforcement point, no
      # drifted exclusions.

      # Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +
      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed a build containing /app/ (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 2: no base tag to patch.
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          echo '<html></html>' > "$d/build/index.html"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad2.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an unpatchable base tag (AC1 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 3: a missing touchpoint file.
          rm "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad3.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an incomplete build (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # fa1.dev parity pin: both web builds must keep the identical
          # release flags AND the same pinned SDK — the bundle's only edit
          # stays the base tag.
          for wf in .github/workflows/pages.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml; do
            grep -q -- '--release' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost the --release web flag (#1100 parity)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q -- '--base-href /app/' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost --base-href /app/ (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q "flutter-version: '3.47.x'" "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf unpinned Flutter SDK (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
          done

      # Issue #433 AC1: README CRAP badge must equal the crap4dart.yaml
      # threshold (they drifted to 8.0-vs-12.0 once). Pure python — runs on
      # every PR, including docs-only ones (a README edit is exactly the
      # drift vector).
      - name: CRAP badge/config sync guard
        run: python3 scripts/check_crap_guards.py

      # gh-1476 AC5 (PR #1479 owner directive): the GEO layer is built at
      # deploy time — gitignored, never committed, nothing to drift
      # against. So the gate builds to a temp dir and validates the
      # OUTPUT: test/site/* (no-JS crawl, robots contract, sitemap

# gh-1476: [GOAL] fa1.dev GEO/agent-optimization: be as legible to AI agents and search as marinamogilko.co

## Description

# [GOAL] fa1.dev GEO/agent-optimization: be as legible to AI agents and search as marinamogilko.co

## Product frame

One sentence: **fa1.dev stops being a JS-shell brochure and becomes a first-class citizen of the agent web — every meaningful page is crawlable without JavaScript, every AI crawler is explicitly welcomed, and llms.txt/llms-full.txt + structured data give LLMs citation-ready facts about Fa — modelled on marinamogilko.co, a reference-grade GEO/SEO site.**

Why it matters: users increasingly discover tools by asking ChatGPT/Claude/Perplexity "what's a good open-source coding agent for Flutter" — if agents can't READ the site, Fa doesn't exist in that answer. Our own product is an agent; our site being agent-illegible is both a marketing hole and a credibility joke.

## Reference analysis — what marinamogilko.co does (verified 2026-10-09)

1. **robots.txt explicitly welcomes AI crawlers by name**: `GPTBot`, `ChatGPT-User`, `Google-Extended`, `ClaudeBot`, `anthropic-ai`, `PerplexityBot`, `CCBot`, `Applebot-Extended` — each with `Allow: /`, plus a comment pointing to llms.txt. (fa1.dev: bare `User-agent: *` only.)
2. **llms.txt as a citation-ready fact sheet**: quotable blocks with hard numbers and named entities (subscribers, guests, awards), key pages, topic list — written so an LLM can lift answers verbatim. (fa1.dev HAS a decent 167-line llms.txt — keep and extend.)
3. **JSON-LD knowledge graph**: `@graph` with `Person` + `PodcastSeries` + `Organization` + `WebSite`; per-episode `PodcastEpisode` schema.
4. **Content moat, server-rendered**: every episode is a static page with the FULL TRANSCRIPT in raw HTML (84 KB, zero JS needed) — agents and search get the substance, not a shell.
5. **Living sitemap**: per-URL real `lastmod` (updated days ago), priorities.
6. Complete OG/Twitter card set with image dimensions and alt text.

## fa1.dev gap analysis (verified against live site + `site/` in this repo)

Already good (do not regress): meta description + robots meta, OG/Twitter with dims+alt, JSON-LD ×3 (`SoftwareApplication`, `FAQPage`, `HowTo`), 167-line llms.txt with quotable FAQ, sitemap.xml exists.

Gaps, ranked by impact:

- **G1 — the blog is invisible to agents.** `site/blog/` is a 3 KB JS shell + `posts.json`; post content renders client-side. Posts are absent from the sitemap. To a crawler/agent the blog is an empty page. (Marina's equivalent — episode transcripts — is her biggest GEO asset.)
- **G2 — robots.txt doesn't name AI crawlers** and doesn't point at llms.txt.
- **G3 — no `llms-full.txt`** (the emerging llms.txt companion: full documentation text for agents with big context windows).
- **G4 — JSON-LD misses the graph**: no `Organization`, no `WebSite`, `SoftwareApplication` lacks `sameAs` (GitHub repo, pub.dev), no `SoftwareSourceCode` with `codeRepository`. Knowledge-panel and entity-linking signals stay on the table.
- **G5 — sitemap is small and stale**: 5 URLs, `/app/` lastmod 2026-07-25; blog posts and any future pages never appear; `lastmod` is hand-maintained (drifts).
- **G6 — repo docs stay invisible**: `docs/*.md` (redaction, tool-availability, dap, …) never reach the site as crawlable HTML — exactly the deep content agents could quote.

## Design

### D1 — static pre-render build step (the core fix)

`site/` is framework-free static files; keep it that way — add a small build script (`site/build.sh` or Dart/make — pick what's already used for install.sh templating) that:
- renders every `blog/posts/*.md` to its own static HTML page (`/blog/<slug>/index.html`) with full content in raw HTML;
- emits `BlogPosting` JSON-LD per post (headline, datePublished/dateModified from file front-matter or git, author → Organization);
- regenerates `sitemap.xml` from the actual page inventory with real `lastmod` (file mtime / git log);
- assembles `llms-full.txt` = llms.txt header + concatenated curated docs (blog posts + selected `docs/*.md` pages), each section headed by its canonical URL.
The deploy pipeline runs the build; hand-editing generated files is forbidden (generated = rebuild in CI check).

### D2 — robots.txt AI welcome mat

Explicit per-bot `Allow: /` blocks for: `GPTBot`, `OAI-SearchBot`, `ChatGPT-User`, `Google-Extended`, `ClaudeBot`, `anthropic-ai`, `PerplexityBot`, `Perplexity-User`, `CCBot`, `Applebot-Extended`, `Meta-ExternalAgent` — plus the header comment pointing to `/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt`. (Keep `User-agent: * Allow: /` + sitemap line.)

### D3 — JSON-LD graph completion

Add `Organization` (author/maintainer entity with `url` + `sameAs` GitHub org), `WebSite` (name, url), `SoftwareSourceCode` (`codeRepository` → github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, `runtimePlatform` Dart), and `sameAs` on the existing `SoftwareApplication` → GitHub repo + pub.dev package page. One `@graph`, validated.

### D4 — sitemap as generated artifact

All indexable pages + every blog post, real `lastmod`, priorities sane (1.0 home, 0.8 posts). Generated by D1 — never hand-edited.

### D5 — docs surfacing (bounded)

Pick 3-5 agent-quotable docs pages (e.g. tool-availability, redaction, sessions/compaction overview) → static HTML under `/docs/`, `TechArticle` JSON-LD, in sitemap + llms-full.txt. Full docs-site publishing is a separate card.

## Threat model / risks

- **Stale generated artifacts** — CI check rebuilds and diffs (sitemap/llms-full/blog HTML must match sources; red = rebuild).
- **llms-full.txt bloat** — cap at ~100-150 KB of curated text; it's a context-window budget, not a dump of the repo.
- **Duplicate-content SEO** — canonical URLs on every page; blog markdown stays single-source, HTML is generated from it.
- **No secrets/PII** — static public content only; nothing from sessions/memory paths.

## Test matrix

- **No-JS crawl test (the GEO invariant)**: `curl` (no JS) of `/`, `/blog/`, every `/blog/<slug>/`, `/docs/<page>/` must contain the page's core text (assert on distinctive strings) — this test would have caught G1.
- **Schema validation**: every JSON-LD block parses and validates against schema.org types (scripted check in CI; Google Rich Results Test manually post-deploy).
- **robots.txt contract**: named AI bots each present with `Allow: /`; llms pointers present; sitemap line intact.
- **Sitemap integrity**: every `<loc>` returns 200; every indexable page is in the sitemap; `lastmod` ≤ source mtime.
- **llms.txt / llms-full.txt**: served 200, text/plain, llms-full contains each linked doc's canonical URL header.
- **REG**: existing OG/Twitter/FAQ/HowTo/SoftwareApplication blocks byte-stable (unless intentionally extended); lighthouse SEO score ≥ current (target 100).

## Acceptance

1. Blog posts crawlable without JS, each in sitemap with real lastmod + BlogPosting schema.
2. robots.txt names the AI crawlers + points at llms files.
3. `/llms-full.txt` live with curated full text.
4. JSON-LD graph: Organization + WebSite + SoftwareSourceCode + sameAs links; validators green.
5. CI fails on stale generated artifacts; no-JS crawl test green.
6. Post-deploy: Rich Results Test shows the new entities; site verified discoverable via an AI-agent query smoke ("what is Fa flutter agent harness" → fa1.dev facts quoted).

## Non-goals

- Full documentation site / docs framework (Docusaurus etc.) — D5 is deliberately 3-5 pages.
- Multilingual versions, hreflang.
- Search-ads/keyword campaigning — this card is machine-legibility, not SEM.
- Redesign/visual changes to the landing.

## References

- Reference site: https://marinamogilko.co/ (robots.txt, llms.txt, JSON-LD @graph, episode transcripts — all verified 2026-10-09)
- Site source: `site/` in this repo (blog shell: `site/blog/`, single post: `site/blog/posts/2026-09-20-we-burned-40-billion-tokens.md`)
- llms.txt spec: https://llmstxt.org/

name: Pages

# Builds the Flutter web demo (flutter_app) into site/app and
# deploys the static landing (site/) to GitHub Pages. Pages source must be
# set to "GitHub Actions" in the repo settings.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'site/**'
      - 'blog/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'flutter_app/**'
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'lib/**'
      - 'vendor/**'
      - 'browser_ext/**'
      - 'scripts/build_browser_ext.sh'
      - 'office_addin/**'
      - 'scripts/build_office_addin.sh'
      - 'scripts/build_site.dart'
      - 'scripts/site_markdown.dart'
      - '.github/workflows/pages.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# One deploy at a time; queued runs must not be cancelled mid-deploy.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build landing + web demo
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily website watcher's budget arithmetic (#351):
    # flutter web build + extension dart2js + add-in build + a Playwright
    # chromium boot smoke; historically ~15m, 45m is the slow-day bound.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          # Same pinned SDK as ci.yml web-spa (#1100): fa1.dev and
          # fa-web-spa.zip must never drift onto different Flutter stables
          # (resolves to the same SDK the floating channel picked today).
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable

      # gh-1275 AC3 (web leg): fail fast before the web build — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      - name: Example app pub get
        # gh-1265 AC2: resolve against the committed lockfile.
=====
          cd office_addin/dart && dart pub get && cd ../..
          bash scripts/build_office_addin.sh

      # gh-1476 (PR #1479 owner directive): the static GEO layer is
      # generated ONLY here, straight into build/pages — the artifacts
      # (blog/docs pages, sitemap.xml, llms-full.txt) are gitignored
      # deploy-time products and never exist in the repo tree; sources
      # (blog/posts, docs/*.md, site/*.html|txt|css) are the single
      # source of truth. `--out` copies the static tree and overlays the
      # generated layer, so the Assemble step below picks up the freshly
      # built files, not repo paths. Dep-free pure Dart scripts — no
      # `dart pub get` needed.
      - name: Build the static GEO layer (gh-1476)
        run: |
          dart scripts/build_blog.dart
          dart scripts/build_site.dart --out build/pages/root

      - name: Assemble Pages artifact
        run: |
          # build/pages/root already holds the complete site: the GEO
          # step above built the generated layer AND the static tree
          # into it. Only the deploy-specific additions land here.
          mkdir -p build/pages/root
          # The App Store frames page (issue #691): the images are the
          # COMMITTED GOLDENS, copied at deploy — never hand-copied PNGs,
          # so the site assets cannot drift from the store assets (the
          # page↔golden set is pinned by test/site/appstore_assets_test.dart).
          mkdir -p build/pages/root/app-store/img
          cp flutter_app/test/goldens/store/en/ios/*.png build/pages/root/app-store/img/
          # Only copy the web app if it built successfully.
          if [ -d build/pages/app ]; then
            cp -R build/pages/app build/pages/root/app
          fi
          # The extension zip lives under /extension/ on fa1.dev.
          if [ -f build/fa-extension.zip ]; then
            mkdir -p build/pages/root/extension
            cp build/fa-extension.zip build/pages/root/extension/fa-extension.zip
          fi

      - name: Cache-bust static assets
        if: steps.web_build.outcome == 'success'
        env:
          BUILD_ID: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          # Bust the Flutter demo app's entry scripts so browsers never load a
          # stale flutter_bootstrap.js / helper bundle after a new deploy.
          sed -i -E 's|src="([^\"]+)"|src="\1?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/app/index.html
          # Bust the landing page's own CSS/JS and the demo-app iframe/link.
          sed -i -E 's|href="styles\.css"|href="styles.css?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="main\.js" defer|src="main.js?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" defer|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="\./app/"|src="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|href="\./app/" target="_blank"|href="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" target="_blank"|g' build/pages/root/index.html

      - name: Size manifest + budget gate (#1096 AC1)
        run: |
          # Per-entry uncompressed size table + +5% budget per line (issue
          # inventory format). First run seeds web-app.tsv/outlook-app.tsv
          # in the workspace (--init-if-missing) — the step below uploads
          # them as a ride-along artifact; commit them to arm the web
          # gates. The extension zip is gated against the committed
          # cut-shape baseline (same file the release gate in
          # build-macos.yml uses).
          python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/pages/app \
            --baseline scripts/size_budget/web-app.tsv --init-if-missing
          if [ -d build/pages/root/outlook/app ]; then
            python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/pages/root/outlook/app \
              --baseline scripts/size_budget/outlook-app.tsv --init-if-missing
          fi
          if [ -f build/fa-extension.zip ]; then
            python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/fa-extension.zip \
              --baseline scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv
          fi

      # The self-seeded baselines live only in this runner's workspace —
      # upload them so "commit it to arm the gate" is actually recoverable
      # (grab the artifact, commit the two TSVs).
      - name: Upload seeded size baselines (#1096 ratchet)
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:

      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed a build containing /app/ (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 2: no base tag to patch.
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          echo '<html></html>' > "$d/build/index.html"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad2.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an unpatchable base tag (AC1 #1100)"

          # Red exit 3: a missing touchpoint file.

the byte count beyond the code-unit count — today the file is 88,350
chars but 89,026 bytes, so the guard already under-reports by ~0.8%.

promises (and a wrong date is worse for search than none).

dates are already required convention — make the gate enforce it), or
omitting `datePublished`/`lastmod` for that entry instead of inventing
one.

This validates the builder itself, not just drift, and nothing generated is ever committable. Hand-edited-HTML accidents become impossible by construction. 4. Keep everything else: D2 robots welcome-mat, D3 JSON-LD graph, deterministic lastmod (front-matter/registry — still the right call for reproducible builds), no-JS crawl tests. Note: the committed-artifact + drift-gate pattern has precedent in this repo (install.sh via gen_installers.dart), but that one is a *signed release artifact* where the bytes are the contract — blog HTML is pure render output, so the deploy-time model fits it better. --- ## General PR Comments **ai-teammate** (2026-10-10): ⚠️ **IMPORTANT: every /docs/ page ships with no visible `

`** `loadDocs` strips the leading H1 from each source doc with the comment "the page template renders it as the headline" — but `renderDocsPage` never renders any headline. The article opens with only the `post-meta` div followed by the body HTML, so the doc title appears in ``/OG/JSON-LD but not on the page itself. That hurts the GEO goal of this PR (headings are exactly what agents and crawlers index), and it's untested: the "exactly one h1" test in `test/scripts/build_site_test.dart:151` only exercises `renderBlogPostPage`. Fix — add the headline to the docs template: ```dart <article class="post-body" id="doc"> <h1>$title</h1> <div class="post-meta">Updated ${d.updated} · ${escapeHtml(orgName)}</div> ``` and add a matching "exactly one h1" assertion for the docs pages. --- **ai-teammate** (2026-10-10): ⚠️ **IMPORTANT: llms-full budget guard compares UTF-16 code units against a byte budget** The guard says "bytes" in both the constant docs and the error message: ```dart if (text.length > llmsFullBudgetBytes) { ``` but `String.length` in Dart is UTF-16 code units, while the file is written as UTF-8. Non-ASCII content (em-dashes, arrows, "—") inflates the byte count beyond the code-unit count — today the file is 88,350 chars but 89,026 bytes, so the guard already under-reports by ~0.8%. As more curated content lands, the guard can pass while the real file exceeds the 150 KB context-window budget it exists to enforce. Fix: ```dart if (utf8.encode(text).length > llmsFullBudgetBytes) { ``` (`dart:convert` is already imported.) --- **ai-teammate** (2026-10-10): 💡 **SUGGESTION: fabricated `lastmod` fallback leaks into JSON-LD and sitemap** When a post has neither `updated:`/`date:` front-matter nor a `YYYY-MM-DD-` filename prefix, `lastmod` falls back to `blogIndexFloor` ('2026-09-20') — a date unrelated to the post's actual publication. name: Pages

# Builds the Flutter web demo (flutter_app) into site/app and
# deploys the static landing (site/) to GitHub Pages. Pages source must be
# set to "GitHub Actions" in the repo settings.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'site/**'
      - 'blog/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'flutter_app/**'
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'lib/**'
      - 'vendor/**'
      - 'browser_ext/**'
      - 'scripts/build_browser_ext.sh'
      - 'office_addin/**'
      - 'scripts/build_office_addin.sh'
      - 'scripts/build_site.dart'
      - 'scripts/site_markdown.dart'
      - '.github/workflows/pages.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# One deploy at a time; queued runs must not be cancelled mid-deploy.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build landing + web demo
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily website watcher's budget arithmetic (#351):
    # flutter web build + extension dart2js + add-in build + a Playwright
    # chromium boot smoke; historically ~15m, 45m is the slow-day bound.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          # Same pinned SDK as ci.yml web-spa (#1100): fa1.dev and
          # fa-web-spa.zip must never drift onto different Flutter stables
          # (resolves to the same SDK the floating channel picked today).
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable

      # gh-1275 AC3 (web leg): fail fast before the web build — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      - name: Example app pub get
        # gh-1265 AC2: resolve against the committed lockfile.
=====
          cd office_addin/dart && dart pub get && cd ../..
          bash scripts/build_office_addin.sh

      # gh-1476 (PR #1479 owner directive): the static GEO layer is
      # generated ONLY here, straight into build/pages — the artifacts
      # (blog/docs pages, sitemap.xml, llms-full.txt) are gitignored
      # deploy-time products and never exist in the repo tree; sources
      # (blog/posts, docs/*.md, site/*.html|txt|css) are the single
      # source of truth. `--out` copies the static tree and overlays the
      # generated layer, so the Assemble step below picks up the freshly
      # built files, not repo paths. Dep-free pure Dart scripts — no
      # `dart pub get` needed.
      - name: Build the static GEO layer (gh-1476)
        run: |
          dart scripts/build_blog.dart
          dart scripts/build_site.dart --out build/pages/root

      - name: Assemble Pages artifact
        run: |
          # build/pages/root already holds the complete site: the GEO
          # step above built the generated layer AND the static tree
          # into it. Only the deploy-specific additions land here.
          mkdir -p build/pages/root
          # The App Store frames page (issue #691): the images are the
          # COMMITTED GOLDENS, copied at deploy — never hand-copied PNGs,
          # so the site assets cannot drift from the store assets (the
          # page↔golden set is pinned by test/site/appstore_assets_test.dart).
          mkdir -p build/pages/root/app-store/img
          cp flutter_app/test/goldens/store/en/ios/*.png build/pages/root/app-store/img/
          # Only copy the web app if it built successfully.
          if [ -d build/pages/app ]; then
            cp -R build/pages/app build/pages/root/app
          fi
          # The extension zip lives under /extension/ on fa1.dev.
          if [ -f build/fa-extension.zip ]; then
            mkdir -p build/pages/root/extension
            cp build/fa-extension.zip build/pages/root/extension/fa-extension.zip
          fi

      - name: Cache-bust static assets
        if: steps.web_build.outcome == 'success'
        env:
          BUILD_ID: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          # Bust the Flutter demo app's entry scripts so browsers never load a
          # stale flutter_bootstrap.js / helper bundle after a new deploy.
          sed -i -E 's|src="([^\"]+)"|src="\1?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/app/index.html
          # Bust the landing page's own CSS/JS and the demo-app iframe/link.
          sed -i -E 's|href="styles\.css"|href="styles.css?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="main\.js" defer|src="main.js?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" defer|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="\./app/"|src="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|href="\./app/" target="_blank"|href="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" target="_blank"|g' build/pages/root/index.html

      - name: Size manifest + budget gate (#1096 AC1)
        run: |
          # Per-entry uncompressed size table + +5% budget per line (issue
          # inventory format). First run seeds web-app.tsv/outlook-app.tsv
          # in the workspace (--init-if-missing) — the step below uploads
          # them as a ride-along artifact; commit them to arm the web
          # gates. The extension zip is gated against the committed
          # cut-shape baseline (same file the release gate in
          # build-macos.yml uses).
          python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/pages/app \
            --baseline scripts/size_budget/web-app.tsv --init-if-missing
          if [ -d build/pages/root/outlook/app ]; then
            python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/pages/root/outlook/app \
              --baseline scripts/size_budget/outlook-app.tsv --init-if-missing
          fi
          if [ -f build/fa-extension.zip ]; then
            python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/fa-extension.zip \
              --baseline scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv
          fi

      # The self-seeded baselines live only in this runner's workspace —
      # upload them so "commit it to arm the gate" is actually recoverable
      # (grab the artifact, commit the two TSVs).

      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed a build containing /app/ (AC3 #1100)"

          # Red exit 2: no base tag to patch.
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          echo '<html></html>' > "$d/build/index.html"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad2.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an unpatchable base tag (AC1 #1100)"

Add them to `.gitignore`. 2. **pages.yml already rebuilds** (`build_blog.dart` + `build_site.dart` before Assemble) — keep that; it becomes the ONLY place artifacts exist, inside `build/pages`. 3. **Replace the `--check` drift gate** (CI ci.yml:344) with **build-to-temp + validate**: `dart scripts/build_site.dart --out `, then run the crawl/schema/llms guard tests (`test/site/*`) against the temp output. Keep everything else: D2 robots welcome-mat, D3 JSON-LD graph, deterministic lastmod (front-matter/registry — still the right call for reproducible builds), no-JS crawl tests. Note: the committed-artifact + drift-gate pattern has precedent in this repo (install.sh via gen_installers.dart), but that one is a *signed release artifact* where the bytes are the contract — blog HTML is pure render output, so the deploy-time model fits it better. --- ## General PR Comments **ai-teammate** (2026-10-10): ⚠️ **IMPORTANT: every /docs/ page ships with no visible `

`** `loadDocs` strips the leading H1 from each source doc with the comment "the page template renders it as the headline" — but `renderDocsPage` never renders any headline. The article opens with only the `post-meta` div followed by the body HTML, so the doc title appears in ``/OG/JSON-LD but not on the page itself. That hurts the GEO goal of this PR (headings are exactly what agents and crawlers index), and it's untested: the "exactly one h1" test in `test/scripts/build_site_test.dart:151` only exercises `renderBlogPostPage`. Fix — add the headline to the docs template: ```dart <article class="post-body" id="doc"> <h1>$title</h1> <div class="post-meta">Updated ${d.updated} · ${escapeHtml(orgName)}</div> ``` and add a matching "exactly one h1" assertion for the docs pages. --- **ai-teammate** (2026-10-10): ⚠️ **IMPORTANT: llms-full budget guard compares UTF-16 code units against a byte budget** The guard says "bytes" in both the constant docs and the error message: ```dart if (text.length > llmsFullBudgetBytes) { ``` but `String.length` in Dart is UTF-16 code units, while the file is written as UTF-8. Non-ASCII content (em-dashes, arrows, "—") inflates the byte count beyond the code-unit count — today the file is 88,350 chars but 89,026 bytes, so the guard already under-reports by ~0.8%. As more curated content lands, the guard can pass while the real file exceeds the 150 KB context-window budget it exists to enforce. Fix: ```dart if (utf8.encode(text).length > llmsFullBudgetBytes) { ``` (`dart:convert` is already imported.) --- **ai-teammate** (2026-10-10): 💡 **SUGGESTION: fabricated `lastmod` fallback leaks into JSON-LD and sitemap** When a post has neither `updated:`/`date:` front-matter nor a `YYYY-MM-DD-` filename prefix, `lastmod` falls back to `blogIndexFloor` ('2026-09-20') — a date unrelated to the post's actual publication. That fabricated date then becomes `datePublished` / `dateModified` in the BlogPosting JSON-LD and the sitemap `<lastmod>`, which is exactly the "real lastmod" discipline this PR's design section promises (and a wrong date is worse for search than none). Consider either failing the build for a dateless post (front-matter dates are already required convention — make the gate enforce it), or omitting `datePublished`/`lastmod` for that entry instead of inventing one. --- **ai-teammate** (2026-10-10): 💡 **SUGGESTION: `docsLinkRewriter` mangles parent-relative links** For a doc-internal relative link like `../foo.md` (or `../../x.md`) that isn't in the curated registry, the fallback builds: ```dart '$repoUrl/blob/main/docs/${href.replaceAll(RegExp(r'^\./'), '')}' ``` → `https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/blob/main/docs/../foo.md` — the `..` survives into the published URL, producing a broken or unexpected GitHub link. None of the current 5 curated docs hit this today, so it's latent, but it's cheap to normalize: ```dart final cleaned = href.replaceAll(RegExp(r'^\./'), ''); // resolve '.'/'..' segments before embedding, e.g. via Uri resolution return '$repoUrl/blob/main/docs/$cleaned'; ``` --- **ai-teammate** (2026-10-10): 💡 **SUGGESTION: front-matter `cover` interpolated unescaped into HTML attributes** Every other user-facing value in the templates goes through `escapeHtml` (title, description, author, meta), but the raw front-matter `cover` path is interpolated verbatim: ```dart '<img src="posts/$cover" alt="" loading="lazy">' ``` (and the same pattern in the OG/Twitter `og:image`/`twitter:image` meta and the `.post-cover` figure). Risk is low — the source is repo-controlled blog front-matter, not user input — but for consistency with the rest of the template (and defense if front-matter is ever sourced elsewhere), run it through `escapeHtml`/`Uri`-safe encoding like the sibling fields. --- **ai-teammate** (2026-10-10): Fixed. `renderDocsPage` now emits the headline as the first element of the article, exactly as proposed: ```dart <article class="post-body" id="doc"> <h1>$title</h1> <div class="post-meta">Updated ${d.updated} · ${escapeHtml(orgName)}</div> ``` New regression test `docs page renders exactly one visible h1 with the doc title` asserts a single `<h1>` (matching the blog-post coverage at `test/scripts/build_site_test.dart`) and that it opens the article ahead of the `post-meta` line. # Builds the Flutter web demo (flutter_app) into site/app and
# deploys the static landing (site/) to GitHub Pages. Pages source must be
# set to "GitHub Actions" in the repo settings.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'site/**'
      - 'blog/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'flutter_app/**'
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'lib/**'
      - 'vendor/**'
      - 'browser_ext/**'
      - 'scripts/build_browser_ext.sh'
      - 'office_addin/**'
      - 'scripts/build_office_addin.sh'
      - 'scripts/build_site.dart'
      - 'scripts/site_markdown.dart'
      - '.github/workflows/pages.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# One deploy at a time; queued runs must not be cancelled mid-deploy.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build landing + web demo
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily website watcher's budget arithmetic (#351):

      # Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +
      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed a build containing /app/ (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 2: no base tag to patch.
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          echo '<html></html>' > "$d/build/index.html"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad2.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an unpatchable base tag (AC1 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 3: a missing touchpoint file.
          rm "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad3.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an incomplete build (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # fa1.dev parity pin: both web builds must keep the identical
          # release flags AND the same pinned SDK — the bundle's only edit
          # stays the base tag.
          for wf in .github/workflows/pages.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml; do
            grep -q -- '--release' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost the --release web flag (#1100 parity)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q -- '--base-href /app/' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost --base-href /app/ (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q "flutter-version: '3.47.x'" "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf unpinned Flutter SDK (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
          done

      # Issue #433 AC1: README CRAP badge must equal the crap4dart.yaml
      # threshold (they drifted to 8.0-vs-12.0 once). Pure python — runs on
      # every PR, including docs-only ones (a README edit is exactly the
      # drift vector).
      - name: CRAP badge/config sync guard
        run: python3 scripts/check_crap_guards.py

      # gh-1476 AC5 (PR #1479 owner directive): the GEO layer is built at
      # deploy time — gitignored, never committed, nothing to drift
      # against. So the gate builds to a temp dir and validates the
      # OUTPUT: test/site/* (no-JS crawl, robots contract, sitemap

      - name: GEO site build + validation (gh-1476 AC5)

name: Pages

# Builds the Flutter web demo (flutter_app) into site/app and
# deploys the static landing (site/) to GitHub Pages. Pages source must be
# set to "GitHub Actions" in the repo settings.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'site/**'
      - 'blog/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'flutter_app/**'
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'lib/**'
      - 'vendor/**'
      - 'browser_ext/**'
      - 'scripts/build_browser_ext.sh'
      - 'office_addin/**'
      - 'scripts/build_office_addin.sh'
      - 'scripts/build_site.dart'
      - 'scripts/site_markdown.dart'
      - '.github/workflows/pages.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# One deploy at a time; queued runs must not be cancelled mid-deploy.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build landing + web demo
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily website watcher's budget arithmetic (#351):
    # flutter web build + extension dart2js + add-in build + a Playwright
    # chromium boot smoke; historically ~15m, 45m is the slow-day bound.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          # Same pinned SDK as ci.yml web-spa (#1100): fa1.dev and
          # fa-web-spa.zip must never drift onto different Flutter stables
          # (resolves to the same SDK the floating channel picked today).
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable

      # gh-1275 AC3 (web leg): fail fast before the web build — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      - name: Example app pub get
        # gh-1265 AC2: resolve against the committed lockfile.
=====
          cd office_addin/dart && dart pub get && cd ../..
          bash scripts/build_office_addin.sh

      # gh-1476 (PR #1479 owner directive): the static GEO layer is
      # generated ONLY here, straight into build/pages — the artifacts
      # (blog/docs pages, sitemap.xml, llms-full.txt) are gitignored
      # deploy-time products and never exist in the repo tree; sources
      # (blog/posts, docs/*.md, site/*.html|txt|css) are the single
      # source of truth. `--out` copies the static tree and overlays the
      # generated layer, so the Assemble step below picks up the freshly
      # built files, not repo paths. Dep-free pure Dart scripts — no
      # `dart pub get` needed.
      - name: Build the static GEO layer (gh-1476)
        run: |
          dart scripts/build_blog.dart
          dart scripts/build_site.dart --out build/pages/root

      - name: Assemble Pages artifact
        run: |
          # build/pages/root already holds the complete site: the GEO
          # step above built the generated layer AND the static tree
          # into it. Only the deploy-specific additions land here.
          mkdir -p build/pages/root
          # The App Store frames page (issue #691): the images are the
          # COMMITTED GOLDENS, copied at deploy — never hand-copied PNGs,
          # so the site assets cannot drift from the store assets (the
          # page↔golden set is pinned by test/site/appstore_assets_test.dart).
          mkdir -p build/pages/root/app-store/img
          cp flutter_app/test/goldens/store/en/ios/*.png build/pages/root/app-store/img/
          # Only copy the web app if it built successfully.
          if [ -d build/pages/app ]; then
            cp -R build/pages/app build/pages/root/app
          fi
          # The extension zip lives under /extension/ on fa1.dev.
          if [ -f build/fa-extension.zip ]; then
            mkdir -p build/pages/root/extension
            cp build/fa-extension.zip build/pages/root/extension/fa-extension.zip
          fi

      - name: Cache-bust static assets
        if: steps.web_build.outcome == 'success'
        env:
          BUILD_ID: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          # Bust the Flutter demo app's entry scripts so browsers never load a
          # stale flutter_bootstrap.js / helper bundle after a new deploy.
          sed -i -E 's|src="([^\"]+)"|src="\1?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/app/index.html
          # Bust the landing page's own CSS/JS and the demo-app iframe/link.
          sed -i -E 's|href="styles\.css"|href="styles.css?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="main\.js" defer|src="main.js?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" defer|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="\./app/"|src="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|href="\./app/" target="_blank"|href="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" target="_blank"|g' build/pages/root/index.html

      - name: Size manifest + budget gate (#1096 AC1)
        run: |
          # Per-entry uncompressed size table + +5% budget per line (issue
          # inventory format). First run seeds web-app.tsv/outlook-app.tsv
          # in the workspace (--init-if-missing) — the step below uploads
          # them as a ride-along artifact; commit them to arm the web
          # gates. The extension zip is gated against the committed
          # cut-shape baseline (same file the release gate in
          # build-macos.yml uses).
          python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/pages/app \
            --baseline scripts/size_budget/web-app.tsv --init-if-missing
          if [ -d build/pages/root/outlook/app ]; then
            python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/pages/root/outlook/app \
              --baseline scripts/size_budget/outlook-app.tsv --init-if-missing
          fi
          if [ -f build/fa-extension.zip ]; then
            python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/fa-extension.zip \
              --baseline scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv
          fi

      # The self-seeded baselines live only in this runner's workspace —
      # upload them so "commit it to arm the gate" is actually recoverable
      # (grab the artifact, commit the two TSVs).
      - name: Upload seeded size baselines (#1096 ratchet)
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: size-baselines

      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |

          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"

          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null

          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's

          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: llms-full budget guard compares UTF-16 code units against a byte budget**

The guard says "bytes" in both the constant docs and the error message:

```dart
if (text.length > llmsFullBudgetBytes) {
```

but `String.length` in Dart is UTF-16 code units, while the file is
written as UTF-8. Non-ASCII content (em-dashes, arrows, "—") inflates
the byte count beyond the code-unit count — today the file is 88,350
chars but 89,026 bytes, so the guard already under-reports by ~0.8%.
As more curated content lands, the guard can pass while the real file
exceeds the 150 KB context-window budget it exists to enforce.

```dart

```

","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: fabricated `lastmod` fallback leaks into JSON-LD and sitemap**

When a post has neither `updated:`/`date:` front-matter nor a
`YYYY-MM-DD-` filename prefix, `lastmod` falls back to
`blogIndexFloor` ('2026-09-20') — a date unrelated to the post's actual
publication. That fabricated date then becomes `datePublished` /
`dateModified` in the BlogPosting JSON-LD and the sitemap `<lastmod>`,
which is exactly the "real lastmod" discipline this PR's design section
promises (and a wrong date is worse for search than none).

Consider either failing the build for a dateless post (front-matter
dates are already required convention — make the gate enforce it), or
omitting `datePublished`/`lastmod` for that entry instead of inventing
one.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `docsLinkRewriter` mangles parent-relative links**

For a doc-internal relative link like `../foo.md` (or `../../x.md`)
that isn't in the curated registry, the fallback builds:

```dart
'$repoUrl/blob/main/docs/${href.replaceAll(RegExp(r'^\./'), '')}'
```

→ `https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/blob/main/docs/../foo.md`
— the `..` survives into the published URL, producing a broken or
unexpected GitHub link. None of the current 5 curated docs hit this
today, so it's latent, but it's cheap to normalize:

```dart
final cleaned = href.replaceAll(RegExp(r'^\./'), '');
// resolve '.'/'..' segments before embedding, e.g. via Uri resolution
return '$repoUrl/blob/main/docs/$cleaned';
```
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment4.md"}

name: Pages

# Builds the Flutter web demo (flutter_app) into site/app and
# deploys the static landing (site/) to GitHub Pages. Pages source must be
# set to "GitHub Actions" in the repo settings.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'site/**'
      - 'blog/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'flutter_app/**'
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'lib/**'
      - 'vendor/**'
      - 'browser_ext/**'
      - 'scripts/build_browser_ext.sh'
      - 'office_addin/**'
      - 'scripts/build_office_addin.sh'
      - 'scripts/build_site.dart'
      - 'scripts/site_markdown.dart'
      - '.github/workflows/pages.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# One deploy at a time; queued runs must not be cancelled mid-deploy.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build landing + web demo
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily website watcher's budget arithmetic (#351):
    # flutter web build + extension dart2js + add-in build + a Playwright
    # chromium boot smoke; historically ~15m, 45m is the slow-day bound.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          # Same pinned SDK as ci.yml web-spa (#1100): fa1.dev and
          # fa-web-spa.zip must never drift onto different Flutter stables
          # (resolves to the same SDK the floating channel picked today).
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable

      # gh-1275 AC3 (web leg): fail fast before the web build — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      - name: Example app pub get
        # gh-1265 AC2: resolve against the committed lockfile.
=====
          cd office_addin/dart && dart pub get && cd ../..
          bash scripts/build_office_addin.sh

      # gh-1476 (PR #1479 owner directive): the static GEO layer is
      # generated ONLY here, straight into build/pages — the artifacts
      # (blog/docs pages, sitemap.xml, llms-full.txt) are gitignored
      # deploy-time products and never exist in the repo tree; sources
      # (blog/posts, docs/*.md, site/*.html|txt|css) are the single
      # source of truth. `--out` copies the static tree and overlays the
      # generated layer, so the Assemble step below picks up the freshly
      # built files, not repo paths. Dep-free pure Dart scripts — no
      # `dart pub get` needed.
      - name: Build the static GEO layer (gh-1476)
        run: |
          dart scripts/build_blog.dart
          dart scripts/build_site.dart --out build/pages/root

      - name: Assemble Pages artifact
        run: |
          # build/pages/root already holds the complete site: the GEO
          # step above built the generated layer AND the static tree
          # into it. Only the deploy-specific additions land here.
          mkdir -p build/pages/root
          # The App Store frames page (issue #691): the images are the
          # COMMITTED GOLDENS, copied at deploy — never hand-copied PNGs,
          # so the site assets cannot drift from the store assets (the
          # page↔golden set is pinned by test/site/appstore_assets_test.dart).
          mkdir -p build/pages/root/app-store/img
          cp flutter_app/test/goldens/store/en/ios/*.png build/pages/root/app-store/img/
          # Only copy the web app if it built successfully.
          if [ -d build/pages/app ]; then
            cp -R build/pages/app build/pages/root/app
          fi
          # The extension zip lives under /extension/ on fa1.dev.
          if [ -f build/fa-extension.zip ]; then
            mkdir -p build/pages/root/extension
            cp build/fa-extension.zip build/pages/root/extension/fa-extension.zip
          fi

      - name: Cache-bust static assets
        if: steps.web_build.outcome == 'success'
        env:
          BUILD_ID: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          # Bust the Flutter demo app's entry scripts so browsers never load a
          # stale flutter_bootstrap.js / helper bundle after a new deploy.
          sed -i -E 's|src="([^\"]+)"|src="\1?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/app/index.html
          # Bust the landing page's own CSS/JS and the demo-app iframe/link.
          sed -i -E 's|href="styles\.css"|href="styles.css?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="main\.js" defer|src="main.js?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" defer|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="\./app/"|src="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|href="\./app/" target="_blank"|href="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" target="_blank"|g' build/pages/root/index.html

      - name: Size manifest + budget gate (#1096 AC1)
        run: |
          # Per-entry uncompressed size table + +5% budget per line (issue
          # inventory format). First run seeds web-app.tsv/outlook-app.tsv
          # in the workspace (--init-if-missing) — the step below uploads
          # them as a ride-along artifact; commit them to arm the web
          # gates. The extension zip is gated against the committed
          # cut-shape baseline (same file the release gate in
          # build-macos.yml uses).
          python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/pages/app \
            --baseline scripts/size_budget/web-app.tsv --init-if-missing
          if [ -d build/pages/root/outlook/app ]; then
            python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/pages/root/outlook/app \
              --baseline scripts/size_budget/outlook-app.tsv --init-if-missing
          fi
          if [ -f build/fa-extension.zip ]; then
            python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/fa-extension.zip \
              --baseline scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv
          fi

      # The self-seeded baselines live only in this runner's workspace —
      # upload them so "commit it to arm the gate" is actually recoverable
      # (grab the artifact, commit the two TSVs).
      - name: Upload seeded size baselines (#1096 ratchet)
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: size-baselines

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: every /docs/ page ships with no visible `

`** `loadDocs` strips the leading H1 from each source doc with the comment "the page template renders it as the headline" — but `renderDocsPage` never renders any headline. The article opens with only the `post-meta` div followed by the body HTML, so the doc title appears in ``/OG/JSON-LD but not on the page itself. That hurts the GEO goal of this PR (headings are exactly what agents and crawlers index), and it's untested: the "exactly one h1" test in `test/scripts/build_site_test.dart:151` only exercises `renderBlogPostPage`. Fix — add the headline to the docs template: ```dart <article class="post-body" id="doc"> <h1>$title</h1> <div class="post-meta">Updated ${d.updated} · ${escapeHtml(orgName)}</div> ``` and add a matching "exactly one h1" assertion for the docs pages. ","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: llms-full budget guard compares UTF-16 code units against a byte budget**

The guard says "bytes" in both the constant docs and the error message:

```dart
if (text.length > llmsFullBudgetBytes) {
```

but `String.length` in Dart is UTF-16 code units, while the file is
written as UTF-8. Non-ASCII content (em-dashes, arrows, "—") inflates
the byte count beyond the code-unit count — today the file is 88,350
chars but 89,026 bytes, so the guard already under-reports by ~0.8%.
As more curated content lands, the guard can pass while the real file
exceeds the 150 KB context-window budget it exists to enforce.

Fix:

```dart
if (utf8.encode(text).length > llmsFullBudgetBytes) {
```

(`dart:convert` is already imported.)
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: fabricated `lastmod` fallback leaks into JSON-LD and sitemap**

When a post has neither `updated:`/`date:` front-matter nor a
`YYYY-MM-DD-` filename prefix, `lastmod` falls back to
`blogIndexFloor` ('2026-09-20') — a date unrelated to the post's actual
publication. That fabricated date then becomes `datePublished` /
`dateModified` in the BlogPosting JSON-LD and the sitemap `<lastmod>`,
which is exactly the "real lastmod" discipline this PR's design section
promises (and a wrong date is worse for search than none).

Consider either failing the build for a dateless post (front-matter
dates are already required convention — make the gate enforce it), or
omitting `datePublished`/`lastmod` for that entry instead of inventing
one.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `docsLinkRewriter` mangles parent-relative links**

For a doc-internal relative link like `../foo.md` (or `../../x.md`)
that isn't in the curated registry, the fallback builds:

```dart
'$repoUrl/blob/main/docs/${href.replaceAll(RegExp(r'^\./'), '')}'
```

→ `https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/blob/main/docs/../foo.md`
— the `..` survives into the published URL, producing a broken or
unexpected GitHub link. None of the current 5 curated docs hit this
today, so it's latent, but it's cheap to normalize:

```dart
final cleaned = href.replaceAll(RegExp(r'^\./'), '');
// resolve '.'/'..' segments before embedding, e.g. via Uri resolution
return '$repoUrl/blob/main/docs/$cleaned';
```
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment4.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: front-matter `cover` interpolated unescaped into HTML attributes** Every other user-facing value in the templates goes through `escapeHtml` (title, description, author, meta), but the raw front-matter `cover` path is interpolated verbatim: ```dart '' ``` (and the same pattern in the OG/Twitter `og:image`/`twitter:image` meta and the `.post-cover` figure). Risk is low — the source is repo-controlled blog front-matter, not user input — but for consistency with the rest of the template (and defense if front-matter is ever sourced elsewhere), run it through `escapeHtml`/`Uri`-safe encoding like the sibling fields. name: Pages

# Builds the Flutter web demo (flutter_app) into site/app and
# deploys the static landing (site/) to GitHub Pages. Pages source must be
# set to "GitHub Actions" in the repo settings.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'site/**'
      - 'blog/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'flutter_app/**'
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'lib/**'
      - 'vendor/**'
      - 'browser_ext/**'
      - 'scripts/build_browser_ext.sh'
      - 'office_addin/**'
      - 'scripts/build_office_addin.sh'
      - 'scripts/build_site.dart'
      - 'scripts/site_markdown.dart'
      - '.github/workflows/pages.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# One deploy at a time; queued runs must not be cancelled mid-deploy.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build landing + web demo
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily website watcher's budget arithmetic (#351):
    # flutter web build + extension dart2js + add-in build + a Playwright
    # chromium boot smoke; historically ~15m, 45m is the slow-day bound.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          # Same pinned SDK as ci.yml web-spa (#1100): fa1.dev and
          # fa-web-spa.zip must never drift onto different Flutter stables
          # (resolves to the same SDK the floating channel picked today).
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable

      # gh-1275 AC3 (web leg): fail fast before the web build — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      - name: Example app pub get
        # gh-1265 AC2: resolve against the committed lockfile.
=====
          cd office_addin/dart && dart pub get && cd ../..
          bash scripts/build_office_addin.sh

      # gh-1476 (PR #1479 owner directive): the static GEO layer is
      # generated ONLY here, straight into build/pages — the artifacts
      # (blog/docs pages, sitemap.xml, llms-full.txt) are gitignored
      # deploy-time products and never exist in the repo tree; sources
      # (blog/posts, docs/*.md, site/*.html|txt|css) are the single
      # source of truth. `--out` copies the static tree and overlays the
      # generated layer, so the Assemble step below picks up the freshly
      # built files, not repo paths. Dep-free pure Dart scripts — no
      # `dart pub get` needed.
      - name: Build the static GEO layer (gh-1476)
        run: |
          dart scripts/build_blog.dart
          dart scripts/build_site.dart --out build/pages/root

      - name: Assemble Pages artifact
        run: |
          # build/pages/root already holds the complete site: the GEO
          # step above built the generated layer AND the static tree
          # into it. Only the deploy-specific additions land here.
          mkdir -p build/pages/root
          # The App Store frames page (issue #691): the images are the
          # COMMITTED GOLDENS, copied at deploy — never hand-copied PNGs,
          # so the site assets cannot drift from the store assets (the
          # page↔golden set is pinned by test/site/appstore_assets_test.dart).
          mkdir -p build/pages/root/app-store/img
          cp flutter_app/test/goldens/store/en/ios/*.png build/pages/root/app-store/img/
          # Only copy the web app if it built successfully.
          if [ -d build/pages/app ]; then
            cp -R build/pages/app build/pages/root/app
          fi
          # The extension zip lives under /extension/ on fa1.dev.
          if [ -f build/fa-extension.zip ]; then
            mkdir -p build/pages/root/extension
            cp build/fa-extension.zip build/pages/root/extension/fa-extension.zip
          fi

      - name: Cache-bust static assets
        if: steps.web_build.outcome == 'success'
        env:
          BUILD_ID: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          # Bust the Flutter demo app's entry scripts so browsers never load a
          # stale flutter_bootstrap.js / helper bundle after a new deploy.
          sed -i -E 's|src="([^\"]+)"|src="\1?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/app/index.html
          # Bust the landing page's own CSS/JS and the demo-app iframe/link.
          sed -i -E 's|href="styles\.css"|href="styles.css?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="main\.js" defer|src="main.js?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" defer|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="\./app/"|src="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|href="\./app/" target="_blank"|href="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" target="_blank"|g' build/pages/root/index.html

      - name: Size manifest + budget gate (#1096 AC1)
        run: |
          # Per-entry uncompressed size table + +5% budget per line (issue
          # inventory format). First run seeds web-app.tsv/outlook-app.tsv
          # in the workspace (--init-if-missing) — the step below uploads
          # them as a ride-along artifact; commit them to arm the web
          # gates. The extension zip is gated against the committed
          # cut-shape baseline (same file the release gate in
          # build-macos.yml uses).
          python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/pages/app \
            --baseline scripts/size_budget/web-app.tsv --init-if-missing
          if [ -d build/pages/root/outlook/app ]; then
            python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/pages/root/outlook/app \
              --baseline scripts/size_budget/outlook-app.tsv --init-if-missing
          fi
          if [ -f build/fa-extension.zip ]; then
            python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/fa-extension.zip \
              --baseline scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv
          fi

      # The self-seeded baselines live only in this runner's workspace —
      # upload them so "commit it to arm the gate" is actually recoverable
      # (grab the artifact, commit the two TSVs).
      - name: Upload seeded size baselines (#1096 ratchet)
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: size-baselines

name: Pages

# Builds the Flutter web demo (flutter_app) into site/app and
# deploys the static landing (site/) to GitHub Pages. Pages source must be
# set to "GitHub Actions" in the repo settings.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'site/**'
      - 'blog/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'flutter_app/**'
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'lib/**'
      - 'vendor/**'
      - 'browser_ext/**'
      - 'scripts/build_browser_ext.sh'
      - 'office_addin/**'
      - 'scripts/build_office_addin.sh'
      - 'scripts/build_site.dart'
      - 'scripts/site_markdown.dart'
      - '.github/workflows/pages.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# One deploy at a time; queued runs must not be cancelled mid-deploy.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build landing + web demo
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily website watcher's budget arithmetic (#351):
    # flutter web build + extension dart2js + add-in build + a Playwright
    # chromium boot smoke; historically ~15m, 45m is the slow-day bound.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          # Same pinned SDK as ci.yml web-spa (#1100): fa1.dev and
          # fa-web-spa.zip must never drift onto different Flutter stables
          # (resolves to the same SDK the floating channel picked today).
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable

      # gh-1275 AC3 (web leg): fail fast before the web build — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      - name: Example app pub get
        # gh-1265 AC2: resolve against the committed lockfile.
=====
          cd office_addin/dart && dart pub get && cd ../..
          bash scripts/build_office_addin.sh

      # gh-1476 (PR #1479 owner directive): the static GEO layer is
      # generated ONLY here, straight into build/pages — the artifacts
      # (blog/docs pages, sitemap.xml, llms-full.txt) are gitignored
      # deploy-time products and never exist in the repo tree; sources
      # (blog/posts, docs/*.md, site/*.html|txt|css) are the single
      # source of truth. `--out` copies the static tree and overlays the
      # generated layer, so the Assemble step below picks up the freshly
      # built files, not repo paths. Dep-free pure Dart scripts — no
      # `dart pub get` needed.
      - name: Build the static GEO layer (gh-1476)
        run: |
          dart scripts/build_blog.dart
          dart scripts/build_site.dart --out build/pages/root

      - name: Assemble Pages artifact
        run: |
          # build/pages/root already holds the complete site: the GEO
          # step above built the generated layer AND the static tree
          # into it. Only the deploy-specific additions land here.
          mkdir -p build/pages/root
          # The App Store frames page (issue #691): the images are the
          # COMMITTED GOLDENS, copied at deploy — never hand-copied PNGs,
          # so the site assets cannot drift from the store assets (the
          # page↔golden set is pinned by test/site/appstore_assets_test.dart).
          mkdir -p build/pages/root/app-store/img
          cp flutter_app/test/goldens/store/en/ios/*.png build/pages/root/app-store/img/
          # Only copy the web app if it built successfully.
          if [ -d build/pages/app ]; then
            cp -R build/pages/app build/pages/root/app
          fi
          # The extension zip lives under /extension/ on fa1.dev.
          if [ -f build/fa-extension.zip ]; then
            mkdir -p build/pages/root/extension
            cp build/fa-extension.zip build/pages/root/extension/fa-extension.zip
          fi

      - name: Cache-bust static assets
        if: steps.web_build.outcome == 'success'
        env:
          BUILD_ID: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          # Bust the Flutter demo app's entry scripts so browsers never load a
          # stale flutter_bootstrap.js / helper bundle after a new deploy.
          sed -i -E 's|src="([^\"]+)"|src="\1?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/app/index.html
          # Bust the landing page's own CSS/JS and the demo-app iframe/link.
          sed -i -E 's|href="styles\.css"|href="styles.css?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="main\.js" defer|src="main.js?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" defer|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="\./app/"|src="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|href="\./app/" target="_blank"|href="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" target="_blank"|g' build/pages/root/index.html

      - name: Size manifest + budget gate (#1096 AC1)
        run: |
          # Per-entry uncompressed size table + +5% budget per line (issue
          # inventory format). First run seeds web-app.tsv/outlook-app.tsv
          # in the workspace (--init-if-missing) — the step below uploads
          # them as a ride-along artifact; commit them to arm the web
          # gates. The extension zip is gated against the committed
          # cut-shape baseline (same file the release gate in
          # build-macos.yml uses).
          python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/pages/app \
            --baseline scripts/size_budget/web-app.tsv --init-if-missing
          if [ -d build/pages/root/outlook/app ]; then
            python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/pages/root/outlook/app \
              --baseline scripts/size_budget/outlook-app.tsv --init-if-missing
          fi
          if [ -f build/fa-extension.zip ]; then
            python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/fa-extension.zip \
              --baseline scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv
          fi

      # The self-seeded baselines live only in this runner's workspace —
      # upload them so "commit it to arm the gate" is actually recoverable
      # (grab the artifact, commit the two TSVs).
      - name: Upload seeded size baselines (#1096 ratchet)
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: size-baselines

      # Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +
      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed a build containing /app/ (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 2: no base tag to patch.
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          echo '<html></html>' > "$d/build/index.html"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad2.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an unpatchable base tag (AC1 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 3: a missing touchpoint file.
          rm "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad3.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an incomplete build (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # fa1.dev parity pin: both web builds must keep the identical
          # release flags AND the same pinned SDK — the bundle's only edit
          # stays the base tag.
          for wf in .github/workflows/pages.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml; do
            grep -q -- '--release' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost the --release web flag (#1100 parity)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q -- '--base-href /app/' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost --base-href /app/ (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }

          done

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: llms-full budget guard compares UTF-16 code units against a byte budget**

The guard says "bytes" in both the constant docs and the error message:

```dart
if (text.length > llmsFullBudgetBytes) {
```

but `String.length` in Dart is UTF-16 code units, while the file is
written as UTF-8. Non-ASCII content (em-dashes, arrows, "—") inflates
the byte count beyond the code-unit count — today the file is 88,350
chars but 89,026 bytes, so the guard already under-reports by ~0.8%.
As more curated content lands, the guard can pass while the real file
exceeds the 150 KB context-window budget it exists to enforce.

Fix:

```dart

```

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: fabricated `lastmod` fallback leaks into JSON-LD and sitemap**

When a post has neither `updated:`/`date:` front-matter nor a
`YYYY-MM-DD-` filename prefix, `lastmod` falls back to
`blogIndexFloor` ('2026-09-20') — a date unrelated to the post's actual
publication. That fabricated date then becomes `datePublished` /
`dateModified` in the BlogPosting JSON-LD and the sitemap `<lastmod>`,
which is exactly the "real lastmod" discipline this PR's design section
promises (and a wrong date is worse for search than none).

Consider either failing the build for a dateless post (front-matter
dates are already required convention — make the gate enforce it), or
omitting `datePublished`/`lastmod` for that entry instead of inventing
one.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `docsLinkRewriter` mangles parent-relative links**

For a doc-internal relative link like `../foo.md` (or `../../x.md`)
that isn't in the curated registry, the fallback builds:

```dart
'$repoUrl/blob/main/docs/${href.replaceAll(RegExp(r'^\./'), '')}'
```

→ `https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/blob/main/docs/../foo.md`
— the `..` survives into the published URL, producing a broken or
unexpected GitHub link. None of the current 5 curated docs hit this
today, so it's latent, but it's cheap to normalize:

```dart
final cleaned = href.replaceAll(RegExp(r'^\./'), '');
// resolve '.'/'..' segments before embedding, e.g. via Uri resolution
return '$repoUrl/blob/main/docs/$cleaned';
```
