name: Pages

# Builds the Flutter web demo (flutter_app) into site/app and
# deploys the static landing (site/) to GitHub Pages. Pages source must be
# set to "GitHub Actions" in the repo settings.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'site/**'
      - 'blog/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'flutter_app/**'
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'lib/**'
      - 'vendor/**'
      - 'browser_ext/**'
      - 'scripts/build_browser_ext.sh'
      - 'office_addin/**'
      - 'scripts/build_office_addin.sh'
      - 'scripts/build_site.dart'
      - 'scripts/site_markdown.dart'
      - '.github/workflows/pages.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# One deploy at a time; queued runs must not be cancelled mid-deploy.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build landing + web demo
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily website watcher's budget arithmetic (#351):
    # flutter web build + extension dart2js + add-in build + a Playwright
    # chromium boot smoke; historically ~15m, 45m is the slow-day bound.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          # Same pinned SDK as ci.yml web-spa (#1100): fa1.dev and
          # fa-web-spa.zip must never drift onto different Flutter stables
          # (resolves to the same SDK the floating channel picked today).
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable

      # gh-1275 AC3 (web leg): fail fast before the web build — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      - name: Example app pub get
        # gh-1265 AC2: resolve against the committed lockfile.
=====
          cd office_addin/dart && dart pub get && cd ../..
          bash scripts/build_office_addin.sh

      # gh-1476 (PR #1479 owner directive): the static GEO layer is
      # generated ONLY here, straight into build/pages — the artifacts
      # (blog/docs pages, sitemap.xml, llms-full.txt) are gitignored
      # deploy-time products and never exist in the repo tree; sources
      # (blog/posts, docs/*.md, site/*.html|txt|css) are the single
      # source of truth. `--out` copies the static tree and overlays the
      # generated layer, so the Assemble step below picks up the freshly
      # built files, not repo paths. Dep-free pure Dart scripts — no
      # `dart pub get` needed.
      - name: Build the static GEO layer (gh-1476)
        run: |
          dart scripts/build_blog.dart
          dart scripts/build_site.dart --out build/pages/root

      - name: Assemble Pages artifact
        run: |
          # build/pages/root already holds the complete site: the GEO
          # step above built the generated layer AND the static tree
          # into it. Only the deploy-specific additions land here.
          mkdir -p build/pages/root
          # The App Store frames page (issue #691): the images are the
          # COMMITTED GOLDENS, copied at deploy — never hand-copied PNGs,
          # so the site assets cannot drift from the store assets (the
          # page↔golden set is pinned by test/site/appstore_assets_test.dart).
          mkdir -p build/pages/root/app-store/img
          cp flutter_app/test/goldens/store/en/ios/*.png build/pages/root/app-store/img/
          # Only copy the web app if it built successfully.
          if [ -d build/pages/app ]; then
            cp -R build/pages/app build/pages/root/app
          fi
          # The extension zip lives under /extension/ on fa1.dev.
          if [ -f build/fa-extension.zip ]; then
            mkdir -p build/pages/root/extension
            cp build/fa-extension.zip build/pages/root/extension/fa-extension.zip
          fi

      - name: Cache-bust static assets
        if: steps.web_build.outcome == 'success'
        env:
          BUILD_ID: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          # Bust the Flutter demo app's entry scripts so browsers never load a
          # stale flutter_bootstrap.js / helper bundle after a new deploy.
          sed -i -E 's|src="([^\"]+)"|src="\1?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/app/index.html
          # Bust the landing page's own CSS/JS and the demo-app iframe/link.
          sed -i -E 's|href="styles\.css"|href="styles.css?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="main\.js" defer|src="main.js?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" defer|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="\./app/"|src="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|href="\./app/" target="_blank"|href="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" target="_blank"|g' build/pages/root/index.html

      - name: Size manifest + budget gate (#1096 AC1)
        run: |
          # Per-entry uncompressed size table + +5% budget per line (issue
          # inventory format). First run seeds web-app.tsv/outlook-app.tsv
          # in the workspace (--init-if-missing) — the step below uploads
          # them as a ride-along artifact; commit them to arm the web
          # gates. The extension zip is gated against the committed
          # cut-shape baseline (same file the release gate in
          # build-macos.yml uses).
          python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/pages/app \
            --baseline scripts/size_budget/web-app.tsv --init-if-missing
          if [ -d build/pages/root/outlook/app ]; then
            python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/pages/root/outlook/app \
              --baseline scripts/size_budget/outlook-app.tsv --init-if-missing
          fi
          if [ -f build/fa-extension.zip ]; then
            python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/fa-extension.zip \
              --baseline scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv
          fi

      # The self-seeded baselines live only in this runner's workspace —
      # upload them so "commit it to arm the gate" is actually recoverable
      # (grab the artifact, commit the two TSVs).
      - name: Upload seeded size baselines (#1096 ratchet)
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: size-baselines

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: llms-full budget guard compares UTF-16 code units against a byte budget**

The guard says "bytes" in both the constant docs and the error message:

```dart
if (text.length > llmsFullBudgetBytes) {
```

but `String.length` in Dart is UTF-16 code units, while the file is
written as UTF-8. Non-ASCII content (em-dashes, arrows, "—") inflates
the byte count beyond the code-unit count — today the file is 88,350
chars but 89,026 bytes, so the guard already under-reports by ~0.8%.
As more curated content lands, the guard can pass while the real file
exceeds the 150 KB context-window budget it exists to enforce.

Fix:

```dart
if (utf8.encode(text).length > llmsFullBudgetBytes) {
```

(`dart:convert` is already imported.)
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: fabricated `lastmod` fallback leaks into JSON-LD and sitemap**

When a post has neither `updated:`/`date:` front-matter nor a
`YYYY-MM-DD-` filename prefix, `lastmod` falls back to
`blogIndexFloor` ('2026-09-20') — a date unrelated to the post's actual
publication. That fabricated date then becomes `datePublished` /
`dateModified` in the BlogPosting JSON-LD and the sitemap `<lastmod>`,
which is exactly the "real lastmod" discipline this PR's design section
promises (and a wrong date is worse for search than none).

Consider either failing the build for a dateless post (front-matter
dates are already required convention — make the gate enforce it), or
omitting `datePublished`/`lastmod` for that entry instead of inventing
one.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `docsLinkRewriter` mangles parent-relative links**

For a doc-internal relative link like `../foo.md` (or `../../x.md`)
that isn't in the curated registry, the fallback builds:

```dart
'$repoUrl/blob/main/docs/${href.replaceAll(RegExp(r'^\./'), '')}'
```

→ `https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/blob/main/docs/../foo.md`
— the `..` survives into the published URL, producing a broken or
unexpected GitHub link. None of the current 5 curated docs hit this
today, so it's latent, but it's cheap to normalize:

```dart
final cleaned = href.replaceAll(RegExp(r'^\./'), '');
// resolve '.'/'..' segments before embedding, e.g. via Uri resolution
return '$repoUrl/blob/main/docs/$cleaned';
```

`User-agent: *` + sitemap line kept. - **llms-full.txt** (87 KB, under the 150 KB budget, builder-enforced) = llms.txt verbatim + every post and doc in full, each section headed by its canonical URL; llms.txt extended with Blog/Docs sections. - Blog body markdown stays single-source (site/blog/posts/*.md); HTML is generated, cover/H1 lifted into the template (`post.html` parity); legacy `post.html` still serves old links. - CI: `static` job runs `dart scripts/build_site.dart --check` (fails on any hand-edit/stale artifact); pages.yml rebuilds the layer at deploy and now triggers on `blog/**` + `docs/**` changes. ### How to verify ```bash dart scripts/build_site.dart --check # freshness gate (also in CI static job) dart test test/site/ test/scripts/ # 96 tests: no-JS crawl over loopback HTTP, # robots contract, sitemap integrity, # JSON-LD validation, builder units ```
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD MD[blog/posts/*.md + docs/*.md] --> B[scripts/build_site.dart] REG[date registries
front-matter / updated / static table] --> B B --> BP[/blog/slug/ index.html
BlogPosting JSON-LD/] B --> DP[/docs/slug/ index.html
TechArticle JSON-LD/] B --> SM[sitemap.xml
real lastmod] B --> LF[llms-full.txt
≤150 KB budget] B --> BI[blog index post list
generated markers block] CI[CI static gate
--check byte-diff] -.fails on drift.-> B PGH[pages.yml deploy] --> B ```

Do not edit or reply. --- ### Thread 19 **ai-teammate** (2026-10-10): ## Owner directive: sources-only, generate at deploy — drop the committed artifacts The implementation is solid, but the content-duplication model is rejected: right now every article lives 3× in the tree (markdown source + committed HTML + llms-full.txt excerpt). The repo should hold **sources only**; generated HTML/llms-full/sitemap get built **at deploy time**. Rework: 1. **Remove committed generated artifacts** from the tree: `site/blog//index.html`, `site/docs/*/index.html`, `site/llms-full.txt`, generated `sitemap.xml`, and the rendered blog-index list (keep a template/marker if the index needs one). Add them to `.gitignore`. 2. **pages.yml already rebuilds** (`build_blog.dart` + `build_site.dart` before Assemble) — keep that; it becomes the ONLY place artifacts exist, inside `build/pages`. 3. **Replace the `--check` drift gate** (CI ci.yml:344) with **build-to-temp + validate**: `dart scripts/build_site.dart --out `, then run the crawl/schema/llms guard tests (`test/site/*`) against the temp output. This validates the builder itself, not just drift, and nothing generated is ever committable. Hand-edited-HTML accidents become impossible by construction. 4. Keep everything else: D2 robots welcome-mat, D3 JSON-LD graph, deterministic lastmod (front-matter/registry — still the right call for reproducible builds), no-JS crawl tests. Note: the committed-artifact + drift-gate pattern has precedent in this repo (install.sh via gen_installers.dart), but that one is a *signed release artifact* where the bytes are the contract — blog HTML is pure render output, so the deploy-time model fits it better. --- ## General PR Comments **ai-teammate** (2026-10-10): ⚠️ **IMPORTANT: every /docs/ page ships with no visible `

`** `loadDocs` strips the leading H1 from each source doc with the comment "the page template renders it as the headline" — but `renderDocsPage` never renders any headline. The article opens with only the `post-meta` div followed by the body HTML, so the doc title appears in ``/OG/JSON-LD but not on the page itself. That hurts the GEO goal of this PR (headings are exactly what agents and crawlers index), and it's untested: the "exactly one h1" test in `test/scripts/build_site_test.dart:151` only exercises `renderBlogPostPage`. Fix — add the headline to the docs template: ```dart <article class="post-body" id="doc"> <h1>$title</h1> <div class="post-meta">Updated ${d.updated} · ${escapeHtml(orgName)}</div> ``` and add a matching "exactly one h1" assertion for the docs pages. --- **ai-teammate** (2026-10-10): ⚠️ **IMPORTANT: llms-full budget guard compares UTF-16 code units against a byte budget** The guard says "bytes" in both the constant docs and the error message: ```dart if (text.length > llmsFullBudgetBytes) { ``` but `String.length` in Dart is UTF-16 code units, while the file is written as UTF-8. Non-ASCII content (em-dashes, arrows, "—") inflates the byte count beyond the code-unit count — today the file is 88,350 chars but 89,026 bytes, so the guard already under-reports by ~0.8%. As more curated content lands, the guard can pass while the real file exceeds the 150 KB context-window budget it exists to enforce. Fix: ```dart if (utf8.encode(text).length > llmsFullBudgetBytes) { ``` (`dart:convert` is already imported.) --- **ai-teammate** (2026-10-10): 💡 **SUGGESTION: fabricated `lastmod` fallback leaks into JSON-LD and sitemap** When a post has neither `updated:`/`date:` front-matter nor a `YYYY-MM-DD-` filename prefix, `lastmod` falls back to `blogIndexFloor` ('2026-09-20') — a date unrelated to the post's actual publication. That fabricated date then becomes `datePublished` / `dateModified` in the BlogPosting JSON-LD and the sitemap `<lastmod>`, which is exactly the "real lastmod" discipline this PR's design section promises (and a wrong date is worse for search than none). Consider either failing the build for a dateless post (front-matter dates are already required convention — make the gate enforce it), or omitting `datePublished`/`lastmod` for that entry instead of inventing one. --- **ai-teammate** (2026-10-10): 💡 **SUGGESTION: `docsLinkRewriter` mangles parent-relative links** For a doc-internal relative link like `../foo.md` (or `../../x.md`) that isn't in the curated registry, the fallback builds: ```dart '$repoUrl/blob/main/docs/${href.replaceAll(RegExp(r'^\./'), '')}' ``` → `https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/blob/main/docs/../foo.md` — the `..` survives into the published URL, producing a broken or unexpected GitHub link. None of the current 5 curated docs hit this today, so it's latent, but it's cheap to normalize: ```dart final cleaned = href.replaceAll(RegExp(r'^\./'), ''); // resolve '.'/'..' segments before embedding, e.g. via Uri resolution return '$repoUrl/blob/main/docs/$cleaned'; ``` --- **ai-teammate** (2026-10-10): 💡 **SUGGESTION: front-matter `cover` interpolated unescaped into HTML attributes** Every other user-facing value in the templates goes through `escapeHtml` (title, description, author, meta), but the raw front-matter `cover` path is interpolated verbatim: ```dart '<img src="posts/$cover" alt="" loading="lazy">' ``` (and the same pattern in the OG/Twitter `og:image`/`twitter:image` meta and the `.post-cover` figure). Risk is low — the source is repo-controlled blog front-matter, not user input — but for consistency with the rest of the template (and defense if front-matter is ever sourced elsewhere), run it through `escapeHtml`/`Uri`-safe encoding like the sibling fields. --- **ai-teammate** (2026-10-10): Fixed. `renderDocsPage` now emits the headline as the first element of the article, exactly as proposed: ```dart <article class="post-body" id="doc"> <h1>$title</h1> <div class="post-meta">Updated ${d.updated} · ${escapeHtml(orgName)}</div> ``` New regression test `docs page renders exactly one visible h1 with the doc title` asserts a single `<h1>` (matching the blog-post coverage at `test/scripts/build_site_test.dart`) and that it opens the article ahead of the `post-meta` line. All 5 committed docs pages were regenerated — `dart scripts/build_site.dart --check` reports `site build fresh: …

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build landing + web demo
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    # chromium boot smoke; historically ~15m, 45m is the slow-day bound.
    timeout-minutes: 45

        # gh-1265 AC2: resolve against the committed lockfile.
=====

      # generated ONLY here, straight into build/pages — the artifacts

      # deploy-time products and never exist in the repo tree; sources
      # (blog/posts, docs/*.md, site/*.html|txt|css) are the single
      # source of truth. `--out` copies the static tree and overlays the
      # generated layer, so the Assemble step below picks up the freshly
      # built files, not repo paths. Dep-free pure Dart scripts — no
      # `dart pub get` needed.
      - name: Build the static GEO layer (gh-1476)
        run: |
          dart scripts/build_blog.dart
          dart scripts/build_site.dart --out build/pages/root

      - name: Assemble Pages artifact
        run: |
          # build/pages/root already holds the complete site: the GEO
          # step above built the generated layer AND the static tree
          # into it. Only the deploy-specific additions land here.
          mkdir -p build/pages/root
          # The App Store frames page (issue #691): the images are the
          # COMMITTED GOLDENS, copied at deploy — never hand-copied PNGs,
          # so the site assets cannot drift from the store assets (the
          # page↔golden set is pinned by test/site/appstore_assets_test.dart).
          mkdir -p build/pages/root/app-store/img

          if [ -f build/fa-extension.zip ]; then
            mkdir -p build/pages/root/extension
            cp build/fa-extension.zip build/pages/root/extension/fa-extension.zip
          fi

      - name: Cache-bust static assets
        if: steps.web_build.outcome == 'success'
        env:
          BUILD_ID: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          # Bust the Flutter demo app's entry scripts so browsers never load a
          # stale flutter_bootstrap.js / helper bundle after a new deploy.
          sed -i -E 's|src="([^\"]+)"|src="\1?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/app/index.html
          # Bust the landing page's own CSS/JS and the demo-app iframe/link.
          sed -i -E 's|href="styles\.css"|href="styles.css?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="main\.js" defer|src="main.js?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" defer|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="\./app/"|src="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|href="\./app/" target="_blank"|href="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" target="_blank"|g' build/pages/root/index.html

      - name: Size manifest + budget gate (#1096 AC1)
        run: |
          # Per-entry uncompressed size table + +5% budget per line (issue
          # inventory format). First run seeds web-app.tsv/outlook-app.tsv
          # in the workspace (--init-if-missing) — the step below uploads
          # them as a ride-along artifact; commit them to arm the web
          # gates. The extension zip is gated against the committed
          # cut-shape baseline (same file the release gate in
          # build-macos.yml uses).
          python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/pages/app \
            --baseline scripts/size_budget/web-app.tsv --init-if-missing
          if [ -d build/pages/root/outlook/app ]; then
            python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/pages/root/outlook/app \
              --baseline scripts/size_budget/outlook-app.tsv --init-if-missing
          fi
          if [ -f build/fa-extension.zip ]; then

              --baseline scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv
          fi

      # upload them so "commit it to arm the gate" is actually recoverable
      # (grab the artifact, commit the two TSVs).
      - name: Upload seeded size baselines (#1096 ratchet)
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:

      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done

          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.

      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

name: Pages

# Builds the Flutter web demo (flutter_app) into site/app and
# deploys the static landing (site/) to GitHub Pages. Pages source must be
# set to "GitHub Actions" in the repo settings.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'site/**'
      - 'blog/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'flutter_app/**'
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'lib/**'
      - 'vendor/**'
      - 'browser_ext/**'
      - 'scripts/build_browser_ext.sh'
      - 'office_addin/**'
      - 'scripts/build_office_addin.sh'
      - 'scripts/build_site.dart'
      - 'scripts/site_markdown.dart'
      - '.github/workflows/pages.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# One deploy at a time; queued runs must not be cancelled mid-deploy.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build landing + web demo
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily website watcher's budget arithmetic (#351):
    # flutter web build + extension dart2js + add-in build + a Playwright
    # chromium boot smoke; historically ~15m, 45m is the slow-day bound.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          # Same pinned SDK as ci.yml web-spa (#1100): fa1.dev and
          # fa-web-spa.zip must never drift onto different Flutter stables
          # (resolves to the same SDK the floating channel picked today).
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable

      # gh-1275 AC3 (web leg): fail fast before the web build — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      - name: Example app pub get
        # gh-1265 AC2: resolve against the committed lockfile.
=====
          cd office_addin/dart && dart pub get && cd ../..
          bash scripts/build_office_addin.sh

      # gh-1476 (PR #1479 owner directive): the static GEO layer is
      # generated ONLY here, straight into build/pages — the artifacts
      # (blog/docs pages, sitemap.xml, llms-full.txt) are gitignored
      # deploy-time products and never exist in the repo tree; sources
      # (blog/posts, docs/*.md, site/*.html|txt|css) are the single
      # source of truth. `--out` copies the static tree and overlays the
      # generated layer, so the Assemble step below picks up the freshly
      # built files, not repo paths. Dep-free pure Dart scripts — no
      # `dart pub get` needed.
      - name: Build the static GEO layer (gh-1476)
        run: |
          dart scripts/build_blog.dart
          dart scripts/build_site.dart --out build/pages/root

      - name: Assemble Pages artifact
        run: |
          # build/pages/root already holds the complete site: the GEO
          # step above built the generated layer AND the static tree
          # into it. Only the deploy-specific additions land here.
          mkdir -p build/pages/root
          # The App Store frames page (issue #691): the images are the
          # COMMITTED GOLDENS, copied at deploy — never hand-copied PNGs,
          # so the site assets cannot drift from the store assets (the
          # page↔golden set is pinned by test/site/appstore_assets_test.dart).
          mkdir -p build/pages/root/app-store/img
          cp flutter_app/test/goldens/store/en/ios/*.png build/pages/root/app-store/img/
          # Only copy the web app if it built successfully.
          if [ -d build/pages/app ]; then
            cp -R build/pages/app build/pages/root/app
          fi
          # The extension zip lives under /extension/ on fa1.dev.
          if [ -f build/fa-extension.zip ]; then
            mkdir -p build/pages/root/extension
            cp build/fa-extension.zip build/pages/root/extension/fa-extension.zip
          fi

      - name: Cache-bust static assets
        if: steps.web_build.outcome == 'success'
        env:
          BUILD_ID: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          # Bust the Flutter demo app's entry scripts so browsers never load a
          # stale flutter_bootstrap.js / helper bundle after a new deploy.
          sed -i -E 's|src="([^\"]+)"|src="\1?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/app/index.html
          # Bust the landing page's own CSS/JS and the demo-app iframe/link.
          sed -i -E 's|href="styles\.css"|href="styles.css?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="main\.js" defer|src="main.js?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" defer|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="\./app/"|src="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|href="\./app/" target="_blank"|href="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" target="_blank"|g' build/pages/root/index.html

      - name: Size manifest + budget gate (#1096 AC1)
        run: |
          # Per-entry uncompressed size table + +5% budget per line (issue
          # inventory format). First run seeds web-app.tsv/outlook-app.tsv
          # in the workspace (--init-if-missing) — the step below uploads
          # them as a ride-along artifact; commit them to arm the web
          # gates. The extension zip is gated against the committed
          # cut-shape baseline (same file the release gate in
          # build-macos.yml uses).
          python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/pages/app \
            --baseline scripts/size_budget/web-app.tsv --init-if-missing
          if [ -d build/pages/root/outlook/app ]; then
            python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/pages/root/outlook/app \
              --baseline scripts/size_budget/outlook-app.tsv --init-if-missing
          fi
          if [ -f build/fa-extension.zip ]; then
            python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/fa-extension.zip \
              --baseline scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv
          fi

      # The self-seeded baselines live only in this runner's workspace —
      # upload them so "commit it to arm the gate" is actually recoverable
      # (grab the artifact, commit the two TSVs).
      - name: Upload seeded size baselines (#1096 ratchet)
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: size-baselines

# find-exec guard (gh-1232 AC2) is gone: one enforcement point, no
      # drifted exclusions.

      # Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +
      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed a build containing /app/ (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 2: no base tag to patch.
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          echo '<html></html>' > "$d/build/index.html"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad2.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an unpatchable base tag (AC1 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 3: a missing touchpoint file.
          rm "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad3.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an incomplete build (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # fa1.dev parity pin: both web builds must keep the identical
          # release flags AND the same pinned SDK — the bundle's only edit
          # stays the base tag.
          for wf in .github/workflows/pages.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml; do
            grep -q -- '--release' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost the --release web flag (#1100 parity)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q -- '--base-href /app/' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost --base-href /app/ (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q "flutter-version: '3.47.x'" "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf unpinned Flutter SDK (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
          done

      # Issue #433 AC1: README CRAP badge must equal the crap4dart.yaml
      # threshold (they drifted to 8.0-vs-12.0 once). Pure python — runs on
      # every PR, including docs-only ones (a README edit is exactly the
      # drift vector).
      - name: CRAP badge/config sync guard
        run: python3 scripts/check_crap_guards.py

      # gh-1476 AC5 (PR #1479 owner directive): the GEO layer is built at
      # deploy time — gitignored, never committed, nothing to drift
      # against. So the gate builds to a temp dir and validates the
      # OUTPUT: test/site/* (no-JS crawl, robots contract, sitemap
      # integrity, JSON-LD, llms guards) serve the temp tree over loopback
      # HTTP via FA_SITE_ROOT. Stronger than the old `--check` drift gate:
      # it tests the builder itself, and hand-edited generated HTML is
      # uncommittable by construction.
      - name: GEO site build + validation (gh-1476 AC5)
        run: |
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          dart scripts/build_site.dart --out "$d/site"
          FA_SITE_ROOT="$d/site" dart test/site/

blocks.text:
67/67 pass. Now remaining verification:

1. `--check` exits 2 with guidance.
2. In-tree default build keeps git tree clean (gitignored paths).
3. Look for NEW issues in the rework — this is the key value-add of re-review. Areas:

a) **pages.yml ordering issue**: "Build the static GEO layer" runs `dart scripts/build_blog.dart` which writes into `site/blog/posts/` in-tree — that's fine (committed sources). But then `build_site --out build/pages/root` copies statics. Wait — does the pages checkout have site/blog/posts committed? Yes. OK.

b) **The Assemble step no longer copies `site/`** — previously `cp -R site/. build/pages/root/` copied everything committed including e.g. `site/app-store/`, `site/widgets/`, `site/oauth/` — verified present in out tree above. Good. But what about files that are in site/ but skipped by _copyStaticSite incorrectly? The skip list: app/, generated page dirs (dirs under blog/ or docs/ containing index.html), sitemap.xml, llms-full.txt, blog/index.template.html. What about `site/blog/index.html` if present in-tree (from a local preview build committed accidentally)? It's gitignored so won't be in a fresh checkout. In the deploy checkout it won't exist. OK.

c) **The blog post legacy `post.html`** — committed, copied. Good.

d) **Concern: `dart scripts/build_site.dart --out build/pages/root` in pages.yml runs BEFORE "Assemble Pages artifact" mkdir** — emitSite creates dirs recursively, so build/pages/root exists. Fine.

e) **Cache-bust step** mutates `build/pages/root/index.html` and expects `href="styles.css"` and `src="main.js" defer` patterns — those are in the copied index.html, unaffected.

f) **`resolveSiteFile`** in the crawl test blocks paths containing '..' — fine for tests.

g) **test/site_test_support.dart `_repoRoot`** walks up from Directory.current — under `dart test`, cwd is the package root, fine.

h) **Potential issue — `_copyStaticSite` and stale generated dirs in-tree at deploy**: In the pages.yml deploy, checkout is clean (no in-tree generated), skipDirs empty. Fine.

i) **Potential issue — emitSite prune with `--out` when a generated dir contains extra files**: deletes whole dir recursively. In-tree, `site/blog/posts` — wait! `_generatedPageDirs` scans `site/blog` subdirs for dirs containing index.html. `site/blog/posts` has no index.html. But what about... `site/blog/2026-09-20-...` in-tree after preview build gets pruned correctly. OK.

But careful: **the in-tree default mode writes into gitignored paths, but does it also regenerate `site/blog/posts.json`?** No — build_blog does that. Fine.

j) **A subtle one**: In `_copyStaticSite`, `site/blog/index.template.html` is skipped, and the output writes `blog/index.html`. But in-tree mode, `index.template.html` stays. Good.

k) **`--out` to a dir inside repo? e.g. build/pages/root — `_repoRoot()` walks from cwd; pages.yml runs from repo root. Fine.

l) **Check `--check` exit code and stale references**: grep for `--check` across repo.

m) **The ci.yml GEO step**: `dart test/site/` runs the crawl tests which bind a loopback HttpServer — fine on ubuntu runner. Also note test/site has other tests (appstore_assets, asset_version_guard) that read committed site/ files directly — they run in the static job too (previously did they run there? They exist on main already, presumably run in test-core or somewhere; now they also run in static job — duplicate but harmless).

Wait — one thing: `dart test/site/` in the GEO step runs ALL test/site tests including appstore_assets_test, which reads `site/index.html` from the repo. That's fine.

n) **Duration**: static job timeout 8 min; building + 34 tests is fast. Fine.

o) **Edge: `resolveSiteRoot` fallback temp build inside tests** — builds on the fly when no FA_SITE_ROOT and no in-tree layer. In the static CI job, FA_SITE_ROOT is set. For local dev running `dart test/site/`, it builds to temp — good.

p) **The `--check` removal — is there any other caller?** grep.

q) **AGENTS.md references to build_site --check or committed artifacts?** grep AGENTS.md.

r) One more architectural check — the owner directive said "Add them to .gitignore". Done. But `site/blog/posts.json` is generated by build_blog.dart and still committed — pre-existing pattern, not in scope.

s) **blog/index.template.html rename** — old links to site/blog/index.html in tests/docs? The deployed URL /blog/ serves index.html which is generated. Fine.

t) Potential issue: **pages.yml builds `build_blog.dart` into `site/blog/posts` in-tree** — in the deploy runner that's a git checkout, writes fine.

u) **What about `widgets/`, `oauth/`, `app-store/` pages** — copied. Confirmed in ls output.

Now check for NEW bugs in emitSite/_copyStaticSite:

- `skipDirs` computed on the SOURCE site dir (`src.path`). In a fresh checkout, no generated dirs → nothing skipped except explicit rules. In `--out` from a dirty local tree (in-tree preview built), skipDirs includes generated page dirs so they're not copied stale. Good.
- BUT: `_generatedPageDirs(src.path)` returns paths relative like `blog/2026-09-20-...`. skip checks `rel == d || rel.startsWith('$d/')`. Files directly like `blog/2026-.../index.html` → rel = `blog/2026-.../index.html`, startsWith d+'/' → skipped. Good.
- In the OUT dir, after writing outputs, prune scans `_generatedPageDirs(siteDir)` where siteDir=outDir. It deletes dirs not in expectedPaths. But note: the prune runs on every emit — including in-tree local preview. If a user has `site/blog/posts` — no index.html, not touched. OK.

- **A real edge**: in `_copyStaticSite`, file skip of `sitemap.xml`/`llms-full.txt` uses exact rel match — but those files are gitignored; only exist if local in-tree build ran. Skip them either way; output overwrites. Fine.

- **Windows path**: rel replaceAll('\\','/') handled.

- **Symlinks**: listSync follows links? Entity types could be Link — `entity is Directory` false for Link. Edge, ignore.

- **empty --out**: `--out` requires arg, exits 2. What if `--out` dir exists with content (e.g. redeploy)? Overwrites files; stale generated pruned. Good.

- **What if outDir is inside site/?** Not a case.

Now, `--check` grep and AGENTS.md references. Also verify exit code 2.

4. **CI GEO step does not run `dart scripts/build_blog.dart`** — the builder reads committed `site/blog/posts`. But wait: is there a drift risk between `blog/posts/` and `site/blog/posts/`? If someone edits blog/posts but not the copy, CI passes but deploy... build_blog.dart runs at deploy and syncs. And pages.yml triggers on `blog/**` changes. There might be an existing guard checking blog/posts ↔ site/blog/posts sync. Not this PR's scope, but the new builder made site/blog/posts a build INPUT for sitemap/JSON-LD — is there a CI check that site/blog/posts is in sync with blog/posts? Let me check quickly. Actually this matters: the freshness gate was removed. If a post is added to blog/posts/ without running build_blog.dart, then site/blog/posts lacks it → builder doesn't see it → no page, no sitemap entry, and CI green. Previously --check would... no, --check only checked generated artifacts, not the posts copy. Let me check if there's a sync guard elsewhere.

5. **The llms-full budget guard error message says bytes** — fixed.

6. **`emitSite` stdout writes** — fine.

7. **`_copyStaticSite` copies `install.sh`, `setup.sh` etc. templates and generated install scripts** — those are committed generated (signed release artifacts per owner note). Fine.

8. **`CNAME` copied** — good, needed for Pages.

9. **`.gitignore` patterns**: `site/blog/*/index.html` — this also matches... site/blog/posts/index.html? doesn't exist. But `site/blog/*/index.html` would match `site/blog/posts/index.html` if it existed — harmless. Does it match anything committed that shouldn't be ignored? `site/blog/post.html` is not matched (no slash). `site/app-store/`? Not under blog. OK. What about `site/docs/*/index.html` — matches generated docs pages. But wait: does `site/blog/*/index.html` accidentally ignore a legit committed file? git ls-files showed committed: blog.css, index.template.html, post.html, posts.json, posts/. None match. Good.

10. **Deeper issue — `_generatedPageDirs` heuristic during `--out` static copy**: it detects generated dirs by the presence of `index.html`. Consider the out-dir static copy when the SOURCE tree has a stale in-tree generated page dir, e.g. `site/blog/old-post/index.html` from a local preview, whose source post was deleted. skipDirs includes it → not copied → good. And prune also handles out dir. Good.

11. **Race/idempotency**: emitSite with --out to an existing build/pages/root (redeploy same workspace?) — GitHub runners are fresh. Fine.

12. **`main()` arg parsing**: unknown args silently ignored, e.g. typo `--ou t`? If user passes `--out` without value → exit 2. OK. What if both `--check` and `--out`? --check wins, exits 2. Fine.

13. **The `dart test/site/` in CI runs from repo root; tests bind loopback** — integration-tagged? The ticket gh-1199 deterministic-gate: tests that look live need mocks. These tests serve local files over loopback with no credentials — compliant. There's a guard that detects integration-looking tests; test/site presumably tagged appropriately. Check dart_test.yaml tags for test/site? The CI step runs `dart test/site/` directly without --tags exclude... In ci.yml other jobs exclude integration tags. Does `dart test/site/` run integration-tagged tests? Let me check dart_test.yaml and whether site tests carry tags.

14. **`resolveSiteRoot` fallback temp build in tests runs `builder.buildSite(root:)` then `emitSite(..., outDir: tmp.path)`** — emitSite with outDir copies statics → tmp is the site root; correct.

15. **Potential issue: `FA_SITE_ROOT` handling in `site_llms_guard_test`** — setUpAll resolves. Tests previously read files directly at main() time; now in setUpAll. Fine.

16. **`test/scripts/build_site_test.dart:538`** — asserts in-tree emit doesn't write sitemap... wait: "in-tree emit writes artifacts next to the sources (local preview)" — and line 538 checks `File('${root.path}/site/sitemap.xml').existsSync(), isFalse` in the --out test. Good coverage.

17. One more: **pages.yml — removing `cp -R site/.` also removed copying of any files that are NOT under site/ ... no, it only copied site/. Everything committed under site/ is handled: statics copied by builder, generated written by builder, app excluded and separately assembled. What about `site/app/` if web build FAILED? Previously cp -R would copy stale committed... site/app is gitignored, never committed — so previously on web-build failure there was no app either (unless leftover). Now `if [ -d build/pages/app ]` — same behavior. Good.

18. **The `widgets/`, `oauth/` pages in sitemap staticPages** — registry lists landing, app, app-store, blog, widgets, privacy. OK.

19. **blog index template markers**: blogIndexStart constant is `<!-- #blog-post-list:start` — indexOf finds it; template contains the full marker line. Regenerated from template. Good.

20. Check dart_test.yaml tags for the site tests to ensure CI `dart test/site/` doesn't trip the gh-1199 deterministic-gate or integration-tag policies. The geo crawl test binds loopback — the gh-1199 gate scans for tests that look live; loopback is allowed. But does `dart test/site/` by default exclude tags? dart_test.yaml may define presets. Let me check.

Also item 4 — blog/posts ↔ site/blog/posts sync guard. Let me grep for an existing guard.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: llms-full budget guard compares UTF-16 code units against a byte budget**

The guard says "bytes" in both the constant docs and the error message:

```dart
if (text.length > llmsFullBudgetBytes) {
```

but `String.length` in Dart is UTF-16 code units, while the file is
written as UTF-8. Non-ASCII content (em-dashes, arrows, "—") inflates
the byte count beyond the code-unit count — today the file is 88,350
chars but 89,026 bytes, so the guard already under-reports by ~0.8%.
As more curated content lands, the guard can pass while the real file
exceeds the 150 KB context-window budget it exists to enforce.

Fix:

```dart
if (utf8.encode(text).length > llmsFullBudgetBytes) {
```

(`dart:convert` is already imported.)
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: fabricated `lastmod` fallback leaks into JSON-LD and sitemap**

When a post has neither `updated:`/`date:` front-matter nor a
`YYYY-MM-DD-` filename prefix, `lastmod` falls back to
`blogIndexFloor` ('2026-09-20') — a date unrelated to the post's actual
publication. That fabricated date then becomes `datePublished` /
`dateModified` in the BlogPosting JSON-LD and the sitemap `<lastmod>`,
which is exactly the "real lastmod" discipline this PR's design section
promises (and a wrong date is worse for search than none).

Consider either failing the build for a dateless post (front-matter
dates are already required convention — make the gate enforce it), or
omitting `datePublished`/`lastmod` for that entry instead of inventing
one.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `docsLinkRewriter` mangles parent-relative links**

For a doc-internal relative link like `../foo.md` (or `../../x.md`)
that isn't in the curated registry, the fallback builds:

```dart
'$repoUrl/blob/main/docs/${href.replaceAll(RegExp(r'^\./'), '')}'
```

→ `https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/blob/main/docs/../foo.md`
— the `..` survives into the published URL, producing a broken or
unexpected GitHub link. None of the current 5 curated docs hit this
today, so it's latent, but it's cheap to normalize:

```dart
final cleaned = href.replaceAll(RegExp(r'^\./'), '');
// resolve '.'/'..' segments before embedding, e.g. via Uri resolution
return '$repoUrl/blob/main/docs/$cleaned';
```
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment4.md"}

name: Pages

# Builds the Flutter web demo (flutter_app) into site/app and
# deploys the static landing (site/) to GitHub Pages. Pages source must be
# set to "GitHub Actions" in the repo settings.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'site/**'
      - 'blog/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'flutter_app/**'
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'lib/**'
      - 'vendor/**'
      - 'browser_ext/**'
      - 'scripts/build_browser_ext.sh'
      - 'office_addin/**'
      - 'scripts/build_office_addin.sh'
      - 'scripts/build_site.dart'
      - 'scripts/site_markdown.dart'
      - '.github/workflows/pages.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# One deploy at a time; queued runs must not be cancelled mid-deploy.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build landing + web demo
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily website watcher's budget arithmetic (#351):
    # flutter web build + extension dart2js + add-in build + a Playwright
    # chromium boot smoke; historically ~15m, 45m is the slow-day bound.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          # Same pinned SDK as ci.yml web-spa (#1100): fa1.dev and
          # fa-web-spa.zip must never drift onto different Flutter stables
          # (resolves to the same SDK the floating channel picked today).
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable

      # gh-1275 AC3 (web leg): fail fast before the web build — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      - name: Example app pub get
        # gh-1265 AC2: resolve against the committed lockfile.
=====
          cd office_addin/dart && dart pub get && cd ../..
          bash scripts/build_office_addin.sh

      # gh-1476 (PR #1479 owner directive): the static GEO layer is
      # generated ONLY here, straight into build/pages — the artifacts
      # (blog/docs pages, sitemap.xml, llms-full.txt) are gitignored
      # deploy-time products and never exist in the repo tree; sources
      # (blog/posts, docs/*.md, site/*.html|txt|css) are the single
      # source of truth. `--out` copies the static tree and overlays the
      # generated layer, so the Assemble step below picks up the freshly
      # built files, not repo paths. Dep-free pure Dart scripts — no
      # `dart pub get` needed.
      - name: Build the static GEO layer (gh-1476)
        run: |
          dart scripts/build_blog.dart
          dart scripts/build_site.dart --out build/pages/root

      - name: Assemble Pages artifact
        run: |
          # build/pages/root already holds the complete site: the GEO
          # step above built the generated layer AND the static tree
          # into it. Only the deploy-specific additions land here.
          mkdir -p build/pages/root
          # The App Store frames page (issue #691): the images are the
          # COMMITTED GOLDENS, copied at deploy — never hand-copied PNGs,
          # so the site assets cannot drift from the store assets (the
          # page↔golden set is pinned by test/site/appstore_assets_test.dart).
          mkdir -p build/pages/root/app-store/img
          cp flutter_app/test/goldens/store/en/ios/*.png build/pages/root/app-store/img/
          # Only copy the web app if it built successfully.
          if [ -d build/pages/app ]; then
            cp -R build/pages/app build/pages/root/app
          fi
          # The extension zip lives under /extension/ on fa1.dev.
          if [ -f build/fa-extension.zip ]; then
            mkdir -p build/pages/root/extension
            cp build/fa-extension.zip build/pages/root/extension/fa-extension.zip
          fi

      - name: Cache-bust static assets
        if: steps.web_build.outcome == 'success'
        env:
          BUILD_ID: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          # Bust the Flutter demo app's entry scripts so browsers never load a
          # stale flutter_bootstrap.js / helper bundle after a new deploy.
          sed -i -E 's|src="([^\"]+)"|src="\1?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/app/index.html
          # Bust the landing page's own CSS/JS and the demo-app iframe/link.
          sed -i -E 's|href="styles\.css"|href="styles.css?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="main\.js" defer|src="main.js?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" defer|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="\./app/"|src="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|href="\./app/" target="_blank"|href="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" target="_blank"|g' build/pages/root/index.html

      - name: Size manifest + budget gate (#1096 AC1)
        run: |
          # Per-entry uncompressed size table + +5% budget per line (issue
          # inventory format). First run seeds web-app.tsv/outlook-app.tsv
          # in the workspace (--init-if-missing) — the step below uploads
          # them as a ride-along artifact; commit them to arm the web
          # gates. The extension zip is gated against the committed
          # cut-shape baseline (same file the release gate in
          # build-macos.yml uses).
          python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/pages/app \

      # Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +
      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed a build containing /app/ (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 2: no base tag to patch.
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          echo '<html></html>' > "$d/build/index.html"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad2.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an unpatchable base tag (AC1 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 3: a missing touchpoint file.
          rm "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad3.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an incomplete build (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # fa1.dev parity pin: both web builds must keep the identical
          # release flags AND the same pinned SDK — the bundle's only edit
          # stays the base tag.
          for wf in .github/workflows/pages.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml; do
            grep -q -- '--release' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost the --release web flag (#1100 parity)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q -- '--base-href /app/' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost --base-href /app/ (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }

blocks.text:
67/67 pass. Now remaining verification:

1. `--check` exits 2 with guidance.
2. In-tree default build keeps git tree clean (gitignored paths).
3. Look for NEW issues in the rework — this is the key value-add of re-review. Areas:

a) **pages.yml ordering issue**: "Build the static GEO layer" runs `dart scripts/build_blog.dart` which writes into `site/blog/posts/` in-tree — that's fine (committed sources). But then `build_site --out build/pages/root` copies statics. Wait — does the pages checkout have site/blog/posts committed? Yes. OK.

b) **The Assemble step no longer copies `site/`** — previously `cp -R site/. build/pages/root/` copied everything committed including e.g. `site/app-store/`, `site/widgets/`, `site/oauth/` — verified present in out tree above. Good. But what about files that are in site/ but skipped by _copyStaticSite incorrectly? The skip list: app/, generated page dirs (dirs under blog/ or docs/ containing index.html), sitemap.xml, llms-full.txt, blog/index.template.html. What about `site/blog/index.html` if present in-tree (from a local preview build committed accidentally)? It's gitignored so won't be in a fresh checkout. In the deploy checkout it won't exist. OK.

c) **The blog post legacy `post.html`** — committed, copied. Good.

d) **Concern: `dart scripts/build_site.dart --out build/pages/root` in pages.yml runs BEFORE "Assemble Pages artifact" mkdir** — emitSite creates dirs recursively, so build/pages/root exists. Fine.

e) **Cache-bust step** mutates `build/pages/root/index.html` and expects `href="styles.css"` and `src="main.js" defer` patterns — those are in the copied index.html, unaffected.

f) **`resolveSiteFile`** in the crawl test blocks paths containing '..' — fine for tests.

g) **test/site_test_support.dart `_repoRoot`** walks up from Directory.current — under `dart test`, cwd is the package root, fine.

h) **Potential issue — `_copyStaticSite` and stale generated dirs in-tree at deploy**: In the pages.yml deploy, checkout is clean (no in-tree generated), skipDirs empty. Fine.

i) **Potential issue — emitSite prune with `--out` when a generated dir contains extra files**: deletes whole dir recursively. In-tree, `site/blog/posts` — wait! `_generatedPageDirs` scans `site/blog` subdirs for dirs containing index.html. `site/blog/posts` has no index.html. But what about... `site/blog/2026-09-20-...` in-tree after preview build gets pruned correctly. OK.

But careful: **the in-tree default mode writes into gitignored paths, but does it also regenerate `site/blog/posts.json`?** No — build_blog does that. Fine.

j) **A subtle one**: In `_copyStaticSite`, `site/blog/index.template.html` is skipped, and the output writes `blog/index.html`. But in-tree mode, `index.template.html` stays. Good.

k) **`--out` to a dir inside repo? e.g. build/pages/root — `_repoRoot()` walks from cwd; pages.yml runs from repo root. Fine.

l) **Check `--check` exit code and stale references**: grep for `--check` across repo.

m) **The ci.yml GEO step**: `dart test/site/` runs the crawl tests which bind a loopback HttpServer — fine on ubuntu runner. Also note test/site has other tests (appstore_assets, asset_version_guard) that read committed site/ files directly — they run in the static job too (previously did they run there? They exist on main already, presumably run in test-core or somewhere; now they also run in static job — duplicate but harmless).

Wait — one thing: `dart test/site/` in the GEO step runs ALL test/site tests including appstore_assets_test, which reads `site/index.html` from the repo. That's fine.

n) **Duration**: static job timeout 8 min; building + 34 tests is fast. Fine.

o) **Edge: `resolveSiteRoot` fallback temp build inside tests** — builds on the fly when no FA_SITE_ROOT and no in-tree layer. In the static CI job, FA_SITE_ROOT is set. For local dev running `dart test/site/`, it builds to temp — good.

p) **The `--check` removal — is there any other caller?** grep.

q) **AGENTS.md references to build_site --check or committed artifacts?** grep AGENTS.md.

r) One more architectural check — the owner directive said "Add them to .gitignore". Done. But `site/blog/posts.json` is generated by build_blog.dart and still committed — pre-existing pattern, not in scope.

s) **blog/index.template.html rename** — old links to site/blog/index.html in tests/docs? The deployed URL /blog/ serves index.html which is generated. Fine.

t) Potential issue: **pages.yml builds `build_blog.dart` into `site/blog/posts` in-tree** — in the deploy runner that's a git checkout, writes fine.

u) **What about `widgets/`, `oauth/`, `app-store/` pages** — copied. Confirmed in ls output.

Now check for NEW bugs in emitSite/_copyStaticSite:

- `skipDirs` computed on the SOURCE site dir (`src.path`). In a fresh checkout, no generated dirs → nothing skipped except explicit rules. In `--out` from a dirty local tree (in-tree preview built), skipDirs includes generated page dirs so they're not copied stale. Good.
- BUT: `_generatedPageDirs(src.path)` returns paths relative like `blog/2026-09-20-...`. skip checks `rel == d || rel.startsWith('$d/')`. Files directly like `blog/2026-.../index.html` → rel = `blog/2026-.../index.html`, startsWith d+'/' → skipped. Good.
- In the OUT dir, after writing outputs, prune scans `_generatedPageDirs(siteDir)` where siteDir=outDir. It deletes dirs not in expectedPaths. But note: the prune runs on every emit — including in-tree local preview. If a user has `site/blog/posts` — no index.html, not touched. OK.

- **A real edge**: in `_copyStaticSite`, file skip of `sitemap.xml`/`llms-full.txt` uses exact rel match — but those files are gitignored; only exist if local in-tree build ran. Skip them either way; output overwrites. Fine.

- **Windows path**: rel replaceAll('\\','/') handled.

- **Symlinks**: listSync follows links? Entity types could be Link — `entity is Directory` false for Link. Edge, ignore.

- **empty --out**: `--out` requires arg, exits 2. What if `--out` dir exists with content (e.g. redeploy)? Overwrites files; stale generated pruned. Good.

- **What if outDir is inside site/?** Not a case.

Now, `--check` grep and AGENTS.md references. Also verify exit code 2.

blocks.text:
In-tree build leaves the tree clean (all generated paths gitignored). 

Now the exhaustive hunt for new issues in the rework. Let me think hard about what's actually questionable:

1. **`site/blog/posts.json` still committed + `build_blog.dart` copies in-tree** — pre-existing pattern, out of scope. But note: in pages.yml, `build_blog.dart` runs at deploy and writes into the checkout's site/blog/posts — but the checkout already has committed copies, so it's a no-op refresh. And `_copyStaticSite` copies posts.json + posts/. Fine.

2. **`test/site_test_support.dart` imports `../scripts/build_site.dart`** — build_site.dart has a `main()` and calls exit() only within main; importing is safe. But `_repoRoot()` in build_site exits the process if not found — only called from main, not from buildSite. Fine.

3. **The crawl test's `resolveSiteFile` traversal guard**: `if (path.contains('..'))` — fine for tests.

4. **CI GEO step does not run `dart scripts/build_blog.dart`** — the builder reads committed `site/blog/posts`. But wait: is there a drift risk between `blog/posts/` and `site/blog/posts/`? If someone edits blog/posts but not the copy, CI passes but deploy... build_blog.dart runs at deploy and syncs. And pages.yml triggers on `blog/**` changes. There might be an existing guard checking blog/posts ↔ site/blog/posts sync. Not this PR's scope, but the new builder made site/blog/posts a build INPUT for sitemap/JSON-LD — is there a CI check that site/blog/posts is in sync with blog/posts? Let me check quickly. Actually this matters: the freshness gate was removed. If a post is added to blog/posts/ without running build_blog.dart, then site/blog/posts lacks it → builder doesn't see it → no page, no sitemap entry, and CI green. Previously --check would... no, --check only checked generated artifacts, not the posts copy. Let me check if there's a sync guard elsewhere.

5. **The llms-full budget guard error message says bytes** — fixed.

6. **`emitSite` stdout writes** — fine.

7. **`_copyStaticSite` copies `install.sh`, `setup.sh` etc. templates and generated install scripts** — those are committed generated (signed release artifacts per owner note). Fine.

8. **`CNAME` copied** — good, needed for Pages.

9. **`.gitignore` patterns**: `site/blog/*/index.html` — this also matches... site/blog/posts/index.html? doesn't exist. But `site/blog/*/index.html` would match `site/blog/posts/index.html` if it existed — harmless. Does it match anything committed that shouldn't be ignored? `site/blog/post.html` is not matched (no slash). `site/app-store/`? Not under blog. OK. What about `site/docs/*/index.html` — matches generated docs pages. But wait: does `site/blog/*/index.html` accidentally ignore a legit committed file? git ls-files showed committed: blog.css, index.template.html, post.html, posts.json, posts/. None match. Good.

10. **Deeper issue — `_generatedPageDirs` heuristic during `--out` static copy**: it detects generated dirs by the presence of `index.html`. Consider the out-dir static copy when the SOURCE tree has a stale in-tree generated page dir, e.g. `site/blog/old-post/index.html` from a local preview, whose source post was deleted. skipDirs includes it → not copied → good. And prune also handles out dir. Good.

11. **Race/idempotency**: emitSite with --out to an existing build/pages/root (redeploy same workspace?) — GitHub runners are fresh. Fine.

12. **`main()` arg parsing**: unknown args silently ignored, e.g. typo `--ou t`? If user passes `--out` without value → exit 2. OK. What if both `--check` and `--out`? --check wins, exits 2. Fine.

13. **The `dart test/site/` in CI runs from repo root; tests bind loopback** — integration-tagged? The ticket gh-1199 deterministic-gate: tests that look live need mocks. These tests serve local files over loopback with no credentials — compliant. There's a guard that detects integration-looking tests; test/site presumably tagged appropriately. Check dart_test.yaml tags for test/site? The CI step runs `dart test/site/` directly without --tags exclude... In ci.yml other jobs exclude integration tags. Does `dart test/site/` run integration-tagged tests? Let me check dart_test.yaml and whether site tests carry tags.

14. **`resolveSiteRoot` fallback temp build in tests runs `builder.buildSite(root:)` then `emitSite(..., outDir: tmp.path)`** — emitSite with outDir copies statics → tmp is the site root; correct.

15. **Potential issue: `FA_SITE_ROOT` handling in `site_llms_guard_test`** — setUpAll resolves. Tests previously read files directly at main() time; now in setUpAll. Fine.

16. **`test/scripts/build_site_test.dart:538`** — asserts in-tree emit doesn't write sitemap... wait: "in-tree emit writes artifacts next to the sources (local preview)" — and line 538 checks `File('${root.path}/site/sitemap.xml').existsSync(), isFalse` in the --out test. Good coverage.

17. One more: **pages.yml — removing `cp -R site/.` also removed copying of any files that are NOT under site/ ... no, it only copied site/. Everything committed under site/ is handled: statics copied by builder, generated written by builder, app excluded and separately assembled. What about `site/app/` if web build FAILED? Previously cp -R would copy stale committed... site/app is gitignored, never committed — so previously on web-build failure there was no app either (unless leftover). Now `if [ -d build/pages/app ]` — same behavior. Good.

18. **The `widgets/`, `oauth/` pages in sitemap staticPages** — registry lists landing, app, app-store, blog, widgets, privacy. OK.

19. **blog index template markers**: blogIndexStart constant is `<!-- #blog-post-list:start` — indexOf finds it; template contains the full marker line. Regenerated from template. Good.

20. Check dart_test.yaml tags for the site tests to ensure CI `dart test/site/` doesn't trip the gh-1199 deterministic-gate or integration-tag policies. The geo crawl test binds loopback — the gh-1199 gate scans for tests that look live; loopback is allowed. But does `dart test/site/` by default exclude tags? dart_test.yaml may define presets. Let me check.

Also item 4 — blog/posts ↔ site/blog/posts sync guard. Let me grep for an existing guard.
Two final checks: test tagging policy (gh-1199 deterministic gate) and the `blog/posts` → `site/blog/posts` sync guard.

That hurts the GEO goal of this PR (headings are exactly what agents and crawlers index), and it's untested: the "exactly one h1" test in `test/scripts/build_site_test.dart:151` only exercises `renderBlogPostPage`. {"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: llms-full budget guard compares UTF-16 code units against a byte budget**

The guard says "bytes" in both the constant docs and the error message:

```dart
if (text.length > llmsFullBudgetBytes) {
```

but `String.length` in Dart is UTF-16 code units, while the file is
written as UTF-8. Non-ASCII content (em-dashes, arrows, "—") inflates
the byte count beyond the code-unit count — today the file is 88,350
chars but 89,026 bytes, so the guard already under-reports by ~0.8%.
As more curated content lands, the guard can pass while the real file
exceeds the 150 KB context-window budget it exists to enforce.

Fix:

```dart
if (utf8.encode(text).length > llmsFullBudgetBytes) {
```

(`dart:convert` is already imported.)
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: fabricated `lastmod` fallback leaks into JSON-LD and sitemap**

When a post has neither `updated:`/`date:` front-matter nor a
`YYYY-MM-DD-` filename prefix, `lastmod` falls back to
`blogIndexFloor` ('2026-09-20') — a date unrelated to the post's actual
publication. That fabricated date then becomes `datePublished` /
`dateModified` in the BlogPosting JSON-LD and the sitemap `<lastmod>`,
which is exactly the "real lastmod" discipline this PR's design section
promises (and a wrong date is worse for search than none).

Consider either failing the build for a dateless post (front-matter
dates are already required convention — make the gate enforce it), or
omitting `datePublished`/`lastmod` for that entry instead of inventing
one.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `docsLinkRewriter` mangles parent-relative links**

For a doc-internal relative link like `../foo.md` (or `../../x.md`)
that isn't in the curated registry, the fallback builds:

```dart
'$repoUrl/blob/main/docs/${href.replaceAll(RegExp(r'^\./'), '')}'
```

→ `https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/blob/main/docs/../foo.md`
— the `..` survives into the published URL, producing a broken or
unexpected GitHub link. None of the current 5 curated docs hit this
today, so it's latent, but it's cheap to normalize:

```dart
final cleaned = href.replaceAll(RegExp(r'^\./'), '');
// resolve '.'/'..' segments before embedding, e.g. via Uri resolution
return '$repoUrl/blob/main/docs/$cleaned';
```
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment4.md"}

Rework: 1. **Remove committed generated artifacts** from the tree: `site/blog//index.html`, `site/docs/*/index.html`, `site/llms-full.txt`, generated `sitemap.xml`, and the rendered blog-index list (keep a template/marker if the index needs one). Add them to `.gitignore`. 2. **pages.yml already rebuilds** (`build_blog.dart` + `build_site.dart` before Assemble) — keep that; it becomes the ONLY place artifacts exist, inside `build/pages`. 3. **Replace the `--check` drift gate** (CI ci.yml:344) with **build-to-temp + validate**: `dart scripts/build_site.dart --out `, then run the crawl/schema/llms guard tests (`test/site/*`) against the temp output. This validates the builder itself, not just drift, and nothing generated is ever committable. Hand-edited-HTML accidents become impossible by construction. 4. Keep everything else: D2 robots welcome-mat, D3 JSON-LD graph, deterministic lastmod (front-matter/registry — still the right call for reproducible builds), no-JS crawl tests. Note: the committed-artifact + drift-gate pattern has precedent in this repo (install.sh via gen_installers.dart), but that one is a *signed release artifact* where the bytes are the contract — blog HTML is pure render output, so the deploy-time model fits it better. --- ## General PR Comments **ai-teammate** (2026-10-10): ⚠️ **IMPORTANT: every /docs/ page ships with no visible `

`** `loadDocs` strips the leading H1 from each source doc with the comment "the page template renders it as the headline" — but `renderDocsPage` never renders any headline. The article opens with only the `post-meta` div followed by the body HTML, so the doc title appears in ``/OG/JSON-LD but not on the page itself. That hurts the GEO goal of this PR (headings are exactly what agents and crawlers index), and it's untested: the "exactly one h1" test in `test/scripts/build_site_test.dart:151` only exercises `renderBlogPostPage`. Fix — add the headline to the docs template: ```dart <article class="post-body" id="doc"> <h1>$title</h1> <div class="post-meta">Updated ${d.updated} · ${escapeHtml(orgName)}</div> ``` and add a matching "exactly one h1" assertion for the docs pages. --- **ai-teammate** (2026-10-10): ⚠️ **IMPORTANT: llms-full budget guard compares UTF-16 code units against a byte budget** The guard says "bytes" in both the constant docs and the error message: ```dart if (text.length > llmsFullBudgetBytes) { ``` but `String.length` in Dart is UTF-16 code units, while the file is written as UTF-8. Non-ASCII content (em-dashes, arrows, "—") inflates the byte count beyond the code-unit count — today the file is 88,350 chars but 89,026 bytes, so the guard already under-reports by ~0.8%. As more curated content lands, the guard can pass while the real file exceeds the 150 KB context-window budget it exists to enforce. Fix: ```dart if (utf8.encode(text).length > llmsFullBudgetBytes) { ``` (`dart:convert` is already imported.) --- **ai-teammate** (2026-10-10): 💡 **SUGGESTION: fabricated `lastmod` fallback leaks into JSON-LD and sitemap** When a post has neither `updated:`/`date:` front-matter nor a `YYYY-MM-DD-` filename prefix, `lastmod` falls back to `blogIndexFloor` ('2026-09-20') — a date unrelated to the post's actual publication. That fabricated date then becomes `datePublished` / `dateModified` in the BlogPosting JSON-LD and the sitemap `<lastmod>`, which is exactly the "real lastmod" discipline this PR's design section promises (and a wrong date is worse for search than none). Consider either failing the build for a dateless post (front-matter dates are already required convention — make the gate enforce it), or omitting `datePublished`/`lastmod` for that entry instead of inventing one. --- **ai-teammate** (2026-10-10): 💡 **SUGGESTION: `docsLinkRewriter` mangles parent-relative links** For a doc-internal relative link like `../foo.md` (or `../../x.md`) that isn't in the curated registry, the fallback builds: ```dart '$repoUrl/blob/main/docs/${href.replaceAll(RegExp(r'^\./'), '')}' ``` → `https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/blob/main/docs/../foo.md` — the `..` survives into the published URL, producing a broken or unexpected GitHub link. None of the current 5 curated docs hit this today, so it's latent, but it's cheap to normalize: ```dart final cleaned = href.replaceAll(RegExp(r'^\./'), ''); // resolve '.'/'..' segments before embedding, e.g. via Uri resolution return '$repoUrl/blob/main/docs/$cleaned'; ``` --- **ai-teammate** (2026-10-10): 💡 **SUGGESTION: front-matter `cover` interpolated unescaped into HTML attributes** Every other user-facing value in the templates goes through `escapeHtml` (title, description, author, meta), but the raw front-matter `cover` path is interpolated verbatim: ```dart '<img src="posts/$cover" alt="" loading="lazy">' ``` (and the same pattern in the OG/Twitter `og:image`/`twitter:image` meta and the `.post-cover` figure). Risk is low — the source is repo-controlled blog front-matter, not user input — but for consistency with the rest of the template (and defense if front-matter is ever sourced elsewhere), run it through `escapeHtml`/`Uri`-safe encoding like the sibling fields. --- **ai-teammate** (2026-10-10): Fixed. `renderDocsPage` now emits the headline as the first element of the article, exactly as proposed: ```dart <article class="post-body" id="doc"> <h1>$title</h1> <div class="post-meta">Updated ${d.updated} · ${escapeHtml(orgName)}</div> ``` New regression test `docs page renders exactly one visible h1 with the doc title` asserts a single `<h1>` (matching the blog-post coverage at `test/scripts/build_site_test.dart`) and that it opens the article ahead of the `post-meta` line. name: Pages

# Builds the Flutter web demo (flutter_app) into site/app and
# deploys the static landing (site/) to GitHub Pages. Pages source must be
# set to "GitHub Actions" in the repo settings.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'site/**'
      - 'blog/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'flutter_app/**'
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'lib/**'
      - 'vendor/**'
      - 'browser_ext/**'
      - 'scripts/build_browser_ext.sh'
      - 'office_addin/**'
      - 'scripts/build_office_addin.sh'
      - 'scripts/build_site.dart'
      - 'scripts/site_markdown.dart'
      - '.github/workflows/pages.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# One deploy at a time; queued runs must not be cancelled mid-deploy.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build landing + web demo
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily website watcher's budget arithmetic (#351):
    # flutter web build + extension dart2js + add-in build + a Playwright
    # chromium boot smoke; historically ~15m, 45m is the slow-day bound.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"

Not this PR's scope, but the new builder made site/blog/posts a build INPUT for sitemap/JSON-LD — is there a CI check that site/blog/posts is in sync with blog/posts? Let me check quickly. Actually this matters: the freshness gate was removed. Previously --check would... no, --check only checked generated artifacts, not the posts copy. Let me check if there's a sync guard elsewhere.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: llms-full budget guard compares UTF-16 code units against a byte budget**

The guard says "bytes" in both the constant docs and the error message:

```dart
if (text.length > llmsFullBudgetBytes) {
```

but `String.length` in Dart is UTF-16 code units, while the file is
written as UTF-8. Non-ASCII content (em-dashes, arrows, "—") inflates
the byte count beyond the code-unit count — today the file is 88,350
chars but 89,026 bytes, so the guard already under-reports by ~0.8%.
As more curated content lands, the guard can pass while the real file
exceeds the 150 KB context-window budget it exists to enforce.

Fix:

```dart
if (utf8.encode(text).length > llmsFullBudgetBytes) {
```

(`dart:convert` is already imported.)
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: fabricated `lastmod` fallback leaks into JSON-LD and sitemap**

When a post has neither `updated:`/`date:` front-matter nor a
`YYYY-MM-DD-` filename prefix, `lastmod` falls back to
`blogIndexFloor` ('2026-09-20') — a date unrelated to the post's actual
publication. That fabricated date then becomes `datePublished` /
`dateModified` in the BlogPosting JSON-LD and the sitemap `<lastmod>`,
which is exactly the "real lastmod" discipline this PR's design section
promises (and a wrong date is worse for search than none).

Consider either failing the build for a dateless post (front-matter
dates are already required convention — make the gate enforce it), or
omitting `datePublished`/`lastmod` for that entry instead of inventing
one.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `docsLinkRewriter` mangles parent-relative links**

For a doc-internal relative link like `../foo.md` (or `../../x.md`)
that isn't in the curated registry, the fallback builds:

```dart
'$repoUrl/blob/main/docs/${href.replaceAll(RegExp(r'^\./'), '')}'
```

→ `https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/blob/main/docs/../foo.md`
— the `..` survives into the published URL, producing a broken or
unexpected GitHub link. None of the current 5 curated docs hit this
today, so it's latent, but it's cheap to normalize:

```dart
final cleaned = href.replaceAll(RegExp(r'^\./'), '');
// resolve '.'/'..' segments before embedding, e.g. via Uri resolution
return '$repoUrl/blob/main/docs/$cleaned';
```
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment4.md"}
