Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. name: Pages

# Builds the Flutter web demo (flutter_app) into site/app and
# deploys the static landing (site/) to GitHub Pages. Pages source must be
# set to "GitHub Actions" in the repo settings.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'site/**'
      - 'blog/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'flutter_app/**'
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'lib/**'
      - 'vendor/**'
      - 'browser_ext/**'
      - 'scripts/build_browser_ext.sh'
      - 'office_addin/**'
      - 'scripts/build_office_addin.sh'
      - 'scripts/build_site.dart'
      - 'scripts/site_markdown.dart'
      - '.github/workflows/pages.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# One deploy at a time; queued runs must not be cancelled mid-deploy.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build landing + web demo
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily website watcher's budget arithmetic (#351):
    # flutter web build + extension dart2js + add-in build + a Playwright
    # chromium boot smoke; historically ~15m, 45m is the slow-day bound.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          # Same pinned SDK as ci.yml web-spa (#1100): fa1.dev and
          # fa-web-spa.zip must never drift onto different Flutter stables
          # (resolves to the same SDK the floating channel picked today).
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable

      # gh-1275 AC3 (web leg): fail fast before the web build — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      - name: Example app pub get
        # gh-1265 AC2: resolve against the committed lockfile.
=====
          cd office_addin/dart && dart pub get && cd ../..
          bash scripts/build_office_addin.sh

      # gh-1476 (PR #1479 owner directive): the static GEO layer is
      # generated ONLY here, straight into build/pages — the artifacts
      # (blog/docs pages, sitemap.xml, llms-full.txt) are gitignored
      # deploy-time products and never exist in the repo tree; sources
      # (blog/posts, docs/*.md, site/*.html|txt|css) are the single
      # source of truth. `--out` copies the static tree and overlays the
      # generated layer, so the Assemble step below picks up the freshly
      # built files, not repo paths. Dep-free pure Dart scripts — no
      # `dart pub get` needed.
      - name: Build the static GEO layer (gh-1476)
        run: |
          dart scripts/build_blog.dart
          dart scripts/build_site.dart --out build/pages/root

      - name: Assemble Pages artifact
        run: |
          # build/pages/root already holds the complete site: the GEO
          # step above built the generated layer AND the static tree
          # into it. Only the deploy-specific additions land here.
          mkdir -p build/pages/root
          # The App Store frames page (issue #691): the images are the
          # COMMITTED GOLDENS, copied at deploy — never hand-copied PNGs,
          # so the site assets cannot drift from the store assets (the
          # page↔golden set is pinned by test/site/appstore_assets_test.dart).
          mkdir -p build/pages/root/app-store/img
          cp flutter_app/test/goldens/store/en/ios/*.png build/pages/root/app-store/img/
          # Only copy the web app if it built successfully.
          if [ -d build/pages/app ]; then
            cp -R build/pages/app build/pages/root/app
          fi
          # The extension zip lives under /extension/ on fa1.dev.
          if [ -f build/fa-extension.zip ]; then
            mkdir -p build/pages/root/extension
            cp build/fa-extension.zip build/pages/root/extension/fa-extension.zip
          fi

      - name: Cache-bust static assets
        if: steps.web_build.outcome == 'success'
        env:
          BUILD_ID: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          # Bust the Flutter demo app's entry scripts so browsers never load a
          # stale flutter_bootstrap.js / helper bundle after a new deploy.
          sed -i -E 's|src="([^\"]+)"|src="\1?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/app/index.html
          # Bust the landing page's own CSS/JS and the demo-app iframe/link.
          sed -i -E 's|href="styles\.css"|href="styles.css?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="main\.js" defer|src="main.js?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" defer|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="\./app/"|src="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|href="\./app/" target="_blank"|href="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" target="_blank"|g' build/pages/root/index.html

      - name: Size manifest + budget gate (#1096 AC1)
        run: |
          # Per-entry uncompressed size table + +5% budget per line (issue
          # inventory format). First run seeds web-app.tsv/outlook-app.tsv
          # in the workspace (--init-if-missing) — the step below uploads
          # them as a ride-along artifact; commit them to arm the web
          # gates. The extension zip is gated against the committed
          # cut-shape baseline (same file the release gate in
          # build-macos.yml uses).
          python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/pages/app \
            --baseline scripts/size_budget/web-app.tsv --init-if-missing
          if [ -d build/pages/root/outlook/app ]; then
            python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/pages/root/outlook/app \
              --baseline scripts/size_budget/outlook-app.tsv --init-if-missing
          fi
          if [ -f build/fa-extension.zip ]; then
            python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/fa-extension.zip \
              --baseline scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv
          fi

      # The self-seeded baselines live only in this runner's workspace —
      # upload them so "commit it to arm the gate" is actually recoverable
      # (grab the artifact, commit the two TSVs).
      - name: Upload seeded size baselines (#1096 ratchet)
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: size-baselines

      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed a build containing /app/ (AC3 #1100)"

          # Red exit 2: no base tag to patch.

            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an unpatchable base tag (AC1 #1100)"

            exit 1

          # fa1.dev parity pin: both web builds must keep the identical

          for wf in .github/workflows/pages.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml; do

1. `--check` exits 2 with guidance.
2. In-tree default build keeps git tree clean (gitignored paths).
3. Look for NEW issues in the rework — this is the key value-add of re-review. Areas:

a) **pages.yml ordering issue**: "Build the static GEO layer" runs `dart scripts/build_blog.dart` which writes into `site/blog/posts/` in-tree — that's fine (committed sources). But then `build_site --out build/pages/root` copies statics. Wait — does the pages checkout have site/blog/posts committed? Yes. OK.

b) **The Assemble step no longer copies `site/`** — previously `cp -R site/. build/pages/root/` copied everything committed including e.g. `site/app-store/`, `site/widgets/`, `site/oauth/` — verified present in out tree above. Good. But what about files that are in site/ but skipped by _copyStaticSite incorrectly? The skip list: app/, generated page dirs (dirs under blog/ or docs/ containing index.html), sitemap.xml, llms-full.txt, blog/index.template.html. What about `site/blog/index.html` if present in-tree (from a local preview build committed accidentally)? It's gitignored so won't be in a fresh checkout. In the deploy checkout it won't exist. OK.

c) **The blog post legacy `post.html`** — committed, copied. Good.

d) **Concern: `dart scripts/build_site.dart --out build/pages/root` in pages.yml runs BEFORE "Assemble Pages artifact" mkdir** — emitSite creates dirs recursively, so build/pages/root exists. Fine.

e) **Cache-bust step** mutates `build/pages/root/index.html` and expects `href="styles.css"` and `src="main.js" defer` patterns — those are in the copied index.html, unaffected.

f) **`resolveSiteFile`** in the crawl test blocks paths containing '..' — fine for tests.

g) **test/site_test_support.dart `_repoRoot`** walks up from Directory.current — under `dart test`, cwd is the package root, fine.

h) **Potential issue — `_copyStaticSite` and stale generated dirs in-tree at deploy**: In the pages.yml deploy, checkout is clean (no in-tree generated), skipDirs empty. Fine.

i) **Potential issue — emitSite prune with `--out` when a generated dir contains extra files**: deletes whole dir recursively. In-tree, `site/blog/posts` — wait! `_generatedPageDirs` scans `site/blog` subdirs for dirs containing index.html. `site/blog/posts` has no index.html. But what about... `site/blog/2026-09-20-...` in-tree after preview build gets pruned correctly. OK.

But careful: **the in-tree default mode writes into gitignored paths, but does it also regenerate `site/blog/posts.json`?** No — build_blog does that. Fine.

j) **A subtle one**: In `_copyStaticSite`, `site/blog/index.template.html` is skipped, and the output writes `blog/index.html`. But in-tree mode, `index.template.html` stays. Good.

k) **`--out` to a dir inside repo? e.g. build/pages/root — `_repoRoot()` walks from cwd; pages.yml runs from repo root. Fine.

l) **Check `--check` exit code and stale references**: grep for `--check` across repo.

m) **The ci.yml GEO step**: `dart test/site/` runs the crawl tests which bind a loopback HttpServer — fine on ubuntu runner. Also note test/site has other tests (appstore_assets, asset_version_guard) that read committed site/ files directly — they run in the static job too (previously did they run there? They exist on main already, presumably run in test-core or somewhere; now they also run in static job — duplicate but harmless).

Wait — one thing: `dart test/site/` in the GEO step runs ALL test/site tests including appstore_assets_test, which reads `site/index.html` from the repo. That's fine.

n) **Duration**: static job timeout 8 min; building + 34 tests is fast. Fine.

o) **Edge: `resolveSiteRoot` fallback temp build inside tests** — builds on the fly when no FA_SITE_ROOT and no in-tree layer. In the static CI job, FA_SITE_ROOT is set. For local dev running `dart test/site/`, it builds to temp — good.

p) **The `--check` removal — is there any other caller?** grep.

q) **AGENTS.md references to build_site --check or committed artifacts?** grep AGENTS.md.

r) One more architectural check — the owner directive said "Add them to .gitignore". Done. But `site/blog/posts.json` is generated by build_blog.dart and still committed — pre-existing pattern, not in scope.

s) **blog/index.template.html rename** — old links to site/blog/index.html in tests/docs? The deployed URL /blog/ serves index.html which is generated. Fine.

t) Potential issue: **pages.yml builds `build_blog.dart` into `site/blog/posts` in-tree** — in the deploy runner that's a git checkout, writes fine.

u) **What about `widgets/`, `oauth/`, `app-store/` pages** — copied. Confirmed in ls output.

Now check for NEW bugs in emitSite/_copyStaticSite:

- `skipDirs` computed on the SOURCE site dir (`src.path`). In a fresh checkout, no generated dirs → nothing skipped except explicit rules. In `--out` from a dirty local tree (in-tree preview built), skipDirs includes generated page dirs so they're not copied stale. Good.
- BUT: `_generatedPageDirs(src.path)` returns paths relative like `blog/2026-09-20-...`. skip checks `rel == d || rel.startsWith('$d/')`. Files directly like `blog/2026-.../index.html` → rel = `blog/2026-.../index.html`, startsWith d+'/' → skipped. Good.
- In the OUT dir, after writing outputs, prune scans `_generatedPageDirs(siteDir)` where siteDir=outDir. It deletes dirs not in expectedPaths. But note: the prune runs on every emit — including in-tree local preview. If a user has `site/blog/posts` — no index.html, not touched. OK.

- **Windows path**: rel replaceAll('\\','/') handled.

- **Symlinks**: listSync follows links? Entity types could be Link — `entity is Directory` false for Link. Edge, ignore.

- **empty --out**: `--out` requires arg, exits 2. What if `--out` dir exists with content (e.g. redeploy)? Overwrites files; stale generated pruned. Good.

But note: in pages.yml, `build_blog.dart` runs at deploy and writes into the checkout's site/blog/posts — but the checkout already has committed copies, so it's a no-op refresh. And `_copyStaticSite` copies posts.json + posts/. Fine.

2. **`test/site_test_support.dart` imports `../scripts/build_site.dart`** — build_site.dart has a `main()` and calls exit() only within main; importing is safe. But `_repoRoot()` in build_site exits the process if not found — only called from main, not from buildSite. Fine.

3. **The crawl test's `resolveSiteFile` traversal guard**: `if (path.contains('..'))` — fine for tests.

4. **CI GEO step does not run `dart scripts/build_blog.dart`** — the builder reads committed `site/blog/posts`. But wait: is there a drift risk between `blog/posts/` and `site/blog/posts/`? If someone edits blog/posts but not the copy, CI passes but deploy... build_blog.dart runs at deploy and syncs. And pages.yml triggers on `blog/**` changes. There might be an existing guard checking blog/posts ↔ site/blog/posts sync. Not this PR's scope, but the new builder made site/blog/posts a build INPUT for sitemap/JSON-LD — is there a CI check that site/blog/posts is in sync with blog/posts? Let me check quickly. Actually this matters: the freshness gate was removed. If a post is added to blog/posts/ without running build_blog.dart, then site/blog/posts lacks it → builder doesn't see it → no page, no sitemap entry, and CI green. Previously --check would... no, --check only checked generated artifacts, not the posts copy. Let me check if there's a sync guard elsewhere.

5. **The llms-full budget guard error message says bytes** — fixed.

6. **`emitSite` stdout writes** — fine.

7. **`_copyStaticSite` copies `install.sh`, `setup.sh` etc. templates and generated install scripts** — those are committed generated (signed release artifacts per owner note). Fine.

8. **`CNAME` copied** — good, needed for Pages.

9. **`.gitignore` patterns**: `site/blog/*/index.html` — this also matches... site/blog/posts/index.html? doesn't exist. But `site/blog/*/index.html` would match `site/blog/posts/index.html` if it existed — harmless. Does it match anything committed that shouldn't be ignored? `site/blog/post.html` is not matched (no slash). `site/app-store/`? Not under blog. OK. What about `site/docs/*/index.html` — matches generated docs pages. But wait: does `site/blog/*/index.html` accidentally ignore a legit committed file? git ls-files showed committed: blog.css, index.template.html, post.html, posts.json, posts/. None match. Good.

10. **Deeper issue — `_generatedPageDirs` heuristic during `--out` static copy**: it detects generated dirs by the presence of `index.html`. Consider the out-dir static copy when the SOURCE tree has a stale in-tree generated page dir, e.g. `site/blog/old-post/index.html` from a local preview, whose source post was deleted. skipDirs includes it → not copied → good. And prune also handles out dir. Good.

11. **Race/idempotency**: emitSite with --out to an existing build/pages/root (redeploy same workspace?) — GitHub runners are fresh. Fine.

12. **`main()` arg parsing**: unknown args silently ignored, e.g. typo `--ou t`? If user passes `--out` without value → exit 2. OK. What if both `--check` and `--out`? --check wins, exits 2. Fine.

13. **The `dart test/site/` in CI runs from repo root; tests bind loopback** — integration-tagged? The ticket gh-1199 deterministic-gate: tests that look live need mocks. These tests serve local files over loopback with no credentials — compliant. There's a guard that detects integration-looking tests; test/site presumably tagged appropriately. Check dart_test.yaml tags for test/site? The CI step runs `dart test/site/` directly without --tags exclude... In ci.yml other jobs exclude integration tags. I independently verified every finding against the checked-out `ai/gh-1476` branch before writing the review artifacts.

Untested: the "exactly one h1" test covers blog posts only. This undercuts the PR's own GEO goal (headings are what agents index).
2. ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** (line 603) — The llms-full budget guard compares `text.length` (UTF-16 code units) against a 150 KB *byte* budget, but the file is written UTF-8. Confirmed live: 88,350 chars vs 89,026 bytes today. Fix: `utf8.encode(text).length`.
3. 💡 (line 141) — `lastmod` falls back to `blogIndexFloor` — a fabricated date that becomes `datePublished`/`dateModified` in JSON-LD and sitemap for dateless posts, contradicting the "real lastmod" discipline.
4. 💡 (line 467) — `docsLinkRewriter` leaks `..` into fallback GitHub URLs (`blob/main/docs/../x.md`) for parent-relative links. Latent today; none of the 5 curated docs hit it.
5. 💡 (line 243) — Front-matter `cover` interpolated unescaped into HTML attributes, unlike every sibling field (low risk — repo-controlled content).

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. name: Pages

# Builds the Flutter web demo (flutter_app) into site/app and
# deploys the static landing (site/) to GitHub Pages. Pages source must be
# set to "GitHub Actions" in the repo settings.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'site/**'
      - 'blog/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'flutter_app/**'
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'lib/**'
      - 'vendor/**'
      - 'browser_ext/**'
      - 'scripts/build_browser_ext.sh'
      - 'office_addin/**'
      - 'scripts/build_office_addin.sh'
      - 'scripts/build_site.dart'
      - 'scripts/site_markdown.dart'
      - '.github/workflows/pages.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# One deploy at a time; queued runs must not be cancelled mid-deploy.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build landing + web demo
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily website watcher's budget arithmetic (#351):
    # flutter web build + extension dart2js + add-in build + a Playwright
    # chromium boot smoke; historically ~15m, 45m is the slow-day bound.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          # Same pinned SDK as ci.yml web-spa (#1100): fa1.dev and
          # fa-web-spa.zip must never drift onto different Flutter stables
          # (resolves to the same SDK the floating channel picked today).
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable

      # gh-1275 AC3 (web leg): fail fast before the web build — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      - name: Example app pub get
        # gh-1265 AC2: resolve against the committed lockfile.
=====
          cd office_addin/dart && dart pub get && cd ../..
          bash scripts/build_office_addin.sh

      # gh-1476 (PR #1479 owner directive): the static GEO layer is
      # generated ONLY here, straight into build/pages — the artifacts
      # (blog/docs pages, sitemap.xml, llms-full.txt) are gitignored
      # deploy-time products and never exist in the repo tree; sources
      # (blog/posts, docs/*.md, site/*.html|txt|css) are the single
      # source of truth. `--out` copies the static tree and overlays the
      # generated layer, so the Assemble step below picks up the freshly
      # built files, not repo paths. Dep-free pure Dart scripts — no
      # `dart pub get` needed.
      - name: Build the static GEO layer (gh-1476)
        run: |
          dart scripts/build_blog.dart
          dart scripts/build_site.dart --out build/pages/root

      - name: Assemble Pages artifact
        run: |
          # build/pages/root already holds the complete site: the GEO
          # step above built the generated layer AND the static tree
          # into it. Only the deploy-specific additions land here.
          mkdir -p build/pages/root
          # The App Store frames page (issue #691): the images are the
          # COMMITTED GOLDENS, copied at deploy — never hand-copied PNGs,
          # so the site assets cannot drift from the store assets (the
          # page↔golden set is pinned by test/site/appstore_assets_test.dart).
          mkdir -p build/pages/root/app-store/img
          cp flutter_app/test/goldens/store/en/ios/*.png build/pages/root/app-store/img/
          # Only copy the web app if it built successfully.
          if [ -d build/pages/app ]; then
            cp -R build/pages/app build/pages/root/app
          fi
          # The extension zip lives under /extension/ on fa1.dev.
          if [ -f build/fa-extension.zip ]; then
            mkdir -p build/pages/root/extension
            cp build/fa-extension.zip build/pages/root/extension/fa-extension.zip
          fi

      - name: Cache-bust static assets
        if: steps.web_build.outcome == 'success'
        env:
          BUILD_ID: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          # Bust the Flutter demo app's entry scripts so browsers never load a
          # stale flutter_bootstrap.js / helper bundle after a new deploy.
          sed -i -E 's|src="([^\"]+)"|src="\1?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/app/index.html
          # Bust the landing page's own CSS/JS and the demo-app iframe/link.
          sed -i -E 's|href="styles\.css"|href="styles.css?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="main\.js" defer|src="main.js?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" defer|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="\./app/"|src="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|href="\./app/" target="_blank"|href="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" target="_blank"|g' build/pages/root/index.html

      - name: Size manifest + budget gate (#1096 AC1)
        run: |
          # Per-entry uncompressed size table + +5% budget per line (issue
          # inventory format). First run seeds web-app.tsv/outlook-app.tsv
          # in the workspace (--init-if-missing) — the step below uploads
          # them as a ride-along artifact; commit them to arm the web
          # gates. The extension zip is gated against the committed
          # cut-shape baseline (same file the release gate in
          # build-macos.yml uses).
          python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/pages/app \
            --baseline scripts/size_budget/web-app.tsv --init-if-missing
          if [ -d build/pages/root/outlook/app ]; then
            python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/pages/root/outlook/app \
              --baseline scripts/size_budget/outlook-app.tsv --init-if-missing
          fi
          if [ -f build/fa-extension.zip ]; then
            python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/fa-extension.zip \
              --baseline scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv
          fi

      # The self-seeded baselines live only in this runner's workspace —
      # upload them so "commit it to arm the gate" is actually recoverable
      # (grab the artifact, commit the two TSVs).
      - name: Upload seeded size baselines (#1096 ratchet)
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: size-baselines

      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed a build containing /app/ (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 2: no base tag to patch.
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          echo '<html></html>' > "$d/build/index.html"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad2.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an unpatchable base tag (AC1 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 3: a missing touchpoint file.
          rm "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad3.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an incomplete build (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # fa1.dev parity pin: both web builds must keep the identical
          # release flags AND the same pinned SDK — the bundle's only edit
          # stays the base tag.
          for wf in .github/workflows/pages.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml; do
            grep -q -- '--release' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost the --release web flag (#1100 parity)"; exit 1; }

      - name: CRAP badge/config sync guard

But then `build_site --out build/pages/root` copies statics. Wait — does the pages checkout have site/blog/posts committed? Yes. OK.

b) **The Assemble step no longer copies `site/`** — previously `cp -R site/. build/pages/root/` copied everything committed including e.g. `site/app-store/`, `site/widgets/`, `site/oauth/` — verified present in out tree above. Good. But what about files that are in site/ but skipped by _copyStaticSite incorrectly? The skip list: app/, generated page dirs (dirs under blog/ or docs/ containing index.html), sitemap.xml, llms-full.txt, blog/index.template.html. What about `site/blog/index.html` if present in-tree (from a local preview build committed accidentally)? It's gitignored so won't be in a fresh checkout. In the deploy checkout it won't exist. OK.

c) **The blog post legacy `post.html`** — committed, copied. Good.

d) **Concern: `dart scripts/build_site.dart --out build/pages/root` in pages.yml runs BEFORE "Assemble Pages artifact" mkdir** — emitSite creates dirs recursively, so build/pages/root exists. Fine.

e) **Cache-bust step** mutates `build/pages/root/index.html` and expects `href="styles.css"` and `src="main.js" defer` patterns — those are in the copied index.html, unaffected.

f) **`resolveSiteFile`** in the crawl test blocks paths containing '..' — fine for tests.

g) **test/site_test_support.dart `_repoRoot`** walks up from Directory.current — under `dart test`, cwd is the package root, fine.

h) **Potential issue — `_copyStaticSite` and stale generated dirs in-tree at deploy**: In the pages.yml deploy, checkout is clean (no in-tree generated), skipDirs empty. Fine.

i) **Potential issue — emitSite prune with `--out` when a generated dir contains extra files**: deletes whole dir recursively. In-tree, `site/blog/posts` — wait! `_generatedPageDirs` scans `site/blog` subdirs for dirs containing index.html. `site/blog/posts` has no index.html. But what about... `site/blog/2026-09-20-...` in-tree after preview build gets pruned correctly. OK.

But careful: **the in-tree default mode writes into gitignored paths, but does it also regenerate `site/blog/posts.json`?** No — build_blog does that. Fine.

j) **A subtle one**: In `_copyStaticSite`, `site/blog/index.template.html` is skipped, and the output writes `blog/index.html`. But in-tree mode, `index.template.html` stays. Good.

k) **`--out` to a dir inside repo? e.g. build/pages/root — `_repoRoot()` walks from cwd; pages.yml runs from repo root. Fine.

l) **Check `--check` exit code and stale references**: grep for `--check` across repo.

m) **The ci.yml GEO step**: `dart test/site/` runs the crawl tests which bind a loopback HttpServer — fine on ubuntu runner. Also note test/site has other tests (appstore_assets, asset_version_guard) that read committed site/ files directly — they run in the static job too (previously did they run there? They exist on main already, presumably run in test-core or somewhere; now they also run in static job — duplicate but harmless).

Wait — one thing: `dart test/site/` in the GEO step runs ALL test/site tests including appstore_assets_test, which reads `site/index.html` from the repo. That's fine.

n) **Duration**: static job timeout 8 min; building + 34 tests is fast. Fine.

o) **Edge: `resolveSiteRoot` fallback temp build inside tests** — builds on the fly when no FA_SITE_ROOT and no in-tree layer. In the static CI job, FA_SITE_ROOT is set. For local dev running `dart test/site/`, it builds to temp — good.

p) **The `--check` removal — is there any other caller?** grep.

q) **AGENTS.md references to build_site --check or committed artifacts?** grep AGENTS.md.

r) One more architectural check — the owner directive said "Add them to .gitignore". Done. But `site/blog/posts.json` is generated by build_blog.dart and still committed — pre-existing pattern, not in scope.

s) **blog/index.template.html rename** — old links to site/blog/index.html in tests/docs? The deployed URL /blog/ serves index.html which is generated. Fine.

t) Potential issue: **pages.yml builds `build_blog.dart` into `site/blog/posts` in-tree** — in the deploy runner that's a git checkout, writes fine.

u) **What about `widgets/`, `oauth/`, `app-store/` pages** — copied. Confirmed in ls output.

Now check for NEW bugs in emitSite/_copyStaticSite:

- `skipDirs` computed on the SOURCE site dir (`src.path`). In a fresh checkout, no generated dirs → nothing skipped except explicit rules. In `--out` from a dirty local tree (in-tree preview built), skipDirs includes generated page dirs so they're not copied stale. Good.
- BUT: `_generatedPageDirs(src.path)` returns paths relative like `blog/2026-09-20-...`. skip checks `rel == d || rel.startsWith('$d/')`. Files directly like `blog/2026-.../index.html` → rel = `blog/2026-.../index.html`, startsWith d+'/' → skipped. Good.
- In the OUT dir, after writing outputs, prune scans `_generatedPageDirs(siteDir)` where siteDir=outDir. It deletes dirs not in expectedPaths. But note: the prune runs on every emit — including in-tree local preview. If a user has `site/blog/posts` — no index.html, not touched. OK.

And `_copyStaticSite` copies posts.json + posts/. Fine.

2. **`test/site_test_support.dart` imports `../scripts/build_site.dart`** — build_site.dart has a `main()` and calls exit() only within main; importing is safe. But `_repoRoot()` in build_site exits the process if not found — only called from main, not from buildSite. Fine.

3. **The crawl test's `resolveSiteFile` traversal guard**: `if (path.contains('..'))` — fine for tests.

4. **CI GEO step does not run `dart scripts/build_blog.dart`** — the builder reads committed `site/blog/posts`. But wait: is there a drift risk between `blog/posts/` and `site/blog/posts/`? If someone edits blog/posts but not the copy, CI passes but deploy... build_blog.dart runs at deploy and syncs. And pages.yml triggers on `blog/**` changes. There might be an existing guard checking blog/posts ↔ site/blog/posts sync. Not this PR's scope, but the new builder made site/blog/posts a build INPUT for sitemap/JSON-LD — is there a CI check that site/blog/posts is in sync with blog/posts? Let me check quickly. Actually this matters: the freshness gate was removed. If a post is added to blog/posts/ without running build_blog.dart, then site/blog/posts lacks it → builder doesn't see it → no page, no sitemap entry, and CI green. Previously --check would... no, --check only checked generated artifacts, not the posts copy. Let me check if there's a sync guard elsewhere.

5. **The llms-full budget guard error message says bytes** — fixed.

6. **`emitSite` stdout writes** — fine.

7. **`_copyStaticSite` copies `install.sh`, `setup.sh` etc. templates and generated install scripts** — those are committed generated (signed release artifacts per owner note). Fine.

8. **`CNAME` copied** — good, needed for Pages.

9. **`.gitignore` patterns**: `site/blog/*/index.html` — this also matches... site/blog/posts/index.html? doesn't exist. But `site/blog/*/index.html` would match `site/blog/posts/index.html` if it existed — harmless. Does it match anything committed that shouldn't be ignored? `site/blog/post.html` is not matched (no slash). `site/app-store/`? Not under blog. OK. What about `site/docs/*/index.html` — matches generated docs pages. But wait: does `site/blog/*/index.html` accidentally ignore a legit committed file? git ls-files showed committed: blog.css, index.template.html, post.html, posts.json, posts/. None match. Good.

10. **Deeper issue — `_generatedPageDirs` heuristic during `--out` static copy**: it detects generated dirs by the presence of `index.html`. Consider the out-dir static copy when the SOURCE tree has a stale in-tree generated page dir, e.g. `site/blog/old-post/index.html` from a local preview, whose source post was deleted. skipDirs includes it → not copied → good. And prune also handles out dir. Good.

11. **Race/idempotency**: emitSite with --out to an existing build/pages/root (redeploy same workspace?) — GitHub runners are fresh. Fine.

12. **`main()` arg parsing**: unknown args silently ignored, e.g. typo `--ou t`? If user passes `--out` without value → exit 2. OK. What if both `--check` and `--out`? --check wins, exits 2. Fine.

13. **The `dart test/site/` in CI runs from repo root; tests bind loopback** — integration-tagged? The ticket gh-1199 deterministic-gate: tests that look live need mocks. These tests serve local files over loopback with no credentials — compliant. There's a guard that detects integration-looking tests; test/site presumably tagged appropriately. Check dart_test.yaml tags for test/site? The CI step runs `dart test/site/` directly without --tags exclude... In ci.yml other jobs exclude integration tags. Does `dart test/site/` run integration-tagged tests? Let me check dart_test.yaml and whether site tests carry tags.

14. **`resolveSiteRoot` fallback temp build in tests runs `builder.buildSite(root:)` then `emitSite(..., outDir: tmp.path)`** — emitSite with outDir copies statics → tmp is the site root; correct.

15. **Potential issue: `FA_SITE_ROOT` handling in `site_llms_guard_test`** — setUpAll resolves. Tests previously read files directly at main() time; now in setUpAll. Fine.

16. **`test/scripts/build_site_test.dart:538`** — asserts in-tree emit doesn't write sitemap... wait: "in-tree emit writes artifacts next to the sources (local preview)" — and line 538 checks `File('${root.path}/site/sitemap.xml').existsSync(), isFalse` in the --out test. Good coverage.

17. One more: **pages.yml — removing `cp -R site/.` also removed copying of any files that are NOT under site/ ... no, it only copied site/. Interesting — a real gap surfaces here. The crawl test reads the markdown source from `${siteRoot.path}/blog/posts/$slug.md` — i.e., from the BUILT site root (FA_SITE_ROOT temp dir). `_copyStaticSite` copies everything under `site/` — including `blog/posts/`? So the temp out dir DOES contain `blog/posts/*.md`. The test's fixture sanity relies on the copy.

But the deeper question I had: **the builder's input is `site/blog/posts/` (committed copy), synced from `blog/posts/` by build_blog.dart**. The new CI gate does NOT run build_blog.dart and has no sync check between `blog/posts/` and `site/blog/posts/`. So if an author adds a post to `blog/posts/` without running build_blog.dart:
- CI: green (builder reads the stale committed `site/blog/posts/`).
- Deploy: pages.yml runs build_blog.dart first → syncs → page appears.

So the site stays correct at deploy, but there's a latency hole: PR merge → pages deploy runs build_blog, fine. Actually deploy is the only generation point and it syncs first. But the CI "validation of the builder" validates against stale inputs — a missing post wouldn't fail CI, but deploy would still produce a correct site since build_blog runs there. Except: what if someone deletes a post from blog/posts? build_blog.dart copies but does it prune stale posts from site/blog/posts? Let me check — earlier grep showed it copies posts and assets but I should check for pruning. If build_blog doesn't prune, a deleted post lingers in site/blog/posts → gets rendered forever. Was that pre-existing? Yes — build_blog.dart is pre-existing (only the two scripts are new in this PR... actually build_blog.dart was referenced in the original PR too but pre-exists on main). Let me verify build_blog is NOT part of this PR's diff: the diff stat shows only build_site.dart and site_markdown.dart as new scripts. So the sync/prune semantics of build_blog are pre-existing. However, this PR made site/blog/posts a build input for the sitemap/JSON-LD, but that input relationship pre-existed for the JS blog too (posts.json). I'll note the missing sync-gate as a SUGGESTION at most... Actually, let me check whether build_blog prunes.

## Verdict: APPROVE — 0 blocking · 2 important · 3 suggestions

I independently verified every finding against the checked-out `ai/gh-1476` branch before writing the review artifacts.

**Findings (all in `scripts/build_site.dart`, a new file so all anchor lines are valid diff lines):**

1. ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** (line 206) — Every `/docs/` page ships with no visible `<h1>`. `loadDocs` strips the source H1 claiming "the page template renders it as the headline", but `renderDocsPage` never emits one — the title exists only in `<title>`/OG/JSON-LD. Untested: the "exactly one h1" test covers blog posts only. This undercuts the PR's own GEO goal (headings are what agents index).
2. ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** (line 603) — The llms-full budget guard compares `text.length` (UTF-16 code units) against a 150 KB *byte* budget, but the file is written UTF-8. Confirmed live: 88,350 chars vs 89,026 bytes today. Fix: `utf8.encode(text).length`.
3. 💡 (line 141) — `lastmod` falls back to `blogIndexFloor` — a fabricated date that becomes `datePublished`/`dateModified` in JSON-LD and sitemap for dateless posts, contradicting the "real lastmod" discipline.
4. 💡 (line 467) — `docsLinkRewriter` leaks `..` into fallback GitHub URLs (`blob/main/docs/../x.md`) for parent-relative links. Latent today; none of the 5 curated docs hit it.
5. 💡 (line 243) — Front-matter `cover` interpolated unescaped into HTML attributes, unlike every sibling field (low risk — repo-controlled content).

**What checked out clean:** no security issues (all dynamic output escaped, raw markdown HTML escaped, no secrets in the static layer); CI wiring is correct (freshness gate in the `static` job where Dart is available; `pages.yml` rebuilds at deploy with matching path triggers); ticket ACs 1–5 are satisfied by implementation + tests (AC6 is post-deploy manual); locally `dart scripts/build_site.dart --check` is fresh and 60/60 site/builder tests pass.

name: Pages

# Builds the Flutter web demo (flutter_app) into site/app and
# deploys the static landing (site/) to GitHub Pages. Pages source must be
# set to "GitHub Actions" in the repo settings.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'site/**'
      - 'blog/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'flutter_app/**'
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'lib/**'
      - 'vendor/**'
      - 'browser_ext/**'
      - 'scripts/build_browser_ext.sh'
      - 'office_addin/**'
      - 'scripts/build_office_addin.sh'
      - 'scripts/build_site.dart'
      - 'scripts/site_markdown.dart'
      - '.github/workflows/pages.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# One deploy at a time; queued runs must not be cancelled mid-deploy.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build landing + web demo
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily website watcher's budget arithmetic (#351):
    # flutter web build + extension dart2js + add-in build + a Playwright
    # chromium boot smoke; historically ~15m, 45m is the slow-day bound.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          # Same pinned SDK as ci.yml web-spa (#1100): fa1.dev and
          # fa-web-spa.zip must never drift onto different Flutter stables
          # (resolves to the same SDK the floating channel picked today).
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable

      # gh-1275 AC3 (web leg): fail fast before the web build — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      - name: Example app pub get
        # gh-1265 AC2: resolve against the committed lockfile.
=====
          cd office_addin/dart && dart pub get && cd ../..
          bash scripts/build_office_addin.sh

      # gh-1476 (PR #1479 owner directive): the static GEO layer is
      # generated ONLY here, straight into build/pages — the artifacts
      # (blog/docs pages, sitemap.xml, llms-full.txt) are gitignored
      # deploy-time products and never exist in the repo tree; sources
      # (blog/posts, docs/*.md, site/*.html|txt|css) are the single
      # source of truth. `--out` copies the static tree and overlays the
      # generated layer, so the Assemble step below picks up the freshly
      # built files, not repo paths. Dep-free pure Dart scripts — no
      # `dart pub get` needed.
      - name: Build the static GEO layer (gh-1476)
        run: |
          dart scripts/build_blog.dart
          dart scripts/build_site.dart --out build/pages/root

      - name: Assemble Pages artifact
        run: |
          # build/pages/root already holds the complete site: the GEO
          # step above built the generated layer AND the static tree
          # into it. Only the deploy-specific additions land here.
          mkdir -p build/pages/root
          # The App Store frames page (issue #691): the images are the
          # COMMITTED GOLDENS, copied at deploy — never hand-copied PNGs,
          # so the site assets cannot drift from the store assets (the
          # page↔golden set is pinned by test/site/appstore_assets_test.dart).
          mkdir -p build/pages/root/app-store/img
          cp flutter_app/test/goldens/store/en/ios/*.png build/pages/root/app-store/img/
          # Only copy the web app if it built successfully.
          if [ -d build/pages/app ]; then
            cp -R build/pages/app build/pages/root/app
          fi
          # The extension zip lives under /extension/ on fa1.dev.
          if [ -f build/fa-extension.zip ]; then
            mkdir -p build/pages/root/extension
            cp build/fa-extension.zip build/pages/root/extension/fa-extension.zip
          fi

      - name: Cache-bust static assets
        if: steps.web_build.outcome == 'success'
        env:
          BUILD_ID: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          # Bust the Flutter demo app's entry scripts so browsers never load a
          # stale flutter_bootstrap.js / helper bundle after a new deploy.
          sed -i -E 's|src="([^\"]+)"|src="\1?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/app/index.html
          # Bust the landing page's own CSS/JS and the demo-app iframe/link.
          sed -i -E 's|href="styles\.css"|href="styles.css?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="main\.js" defer|src="main.js?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" defer|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="\./app/"|src="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|href="\./app/" target="_blank"|href="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" target="_blank"|g' build/pages/root/index.html

      - name: Size manifest + budget gate (#1096 AC1)
        run: |
          # Per-entry uncompressed size table + +5% budget per line (issue
          # inventory format). First run seeds web-app.tsv/outlook-app.tsv
          # in the workspace (--init-if-missing) — the step below uploads
          # them as a ride-along artifact; commit them to arm the web
          # gates. The extension zip is gated against the committed
          # cut-shape baseline (same file the release gate in
          # build-macos.yml uses).
          python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/pages/app \
            --baseline scripts/size_budget/web-app.tsv --init-if-missing
          if [ -d build/pages/root/outlook/app ]; then
            python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/pages/root/outlook/app \
              --baseline scripts/size_budget/outlook-app.tsv --init-if-missing
          fi
          if [ -f build/fa-extension.zip ]; then
            python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/fa-extension.zip \
              --baseline scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv
          fi

      # The self-seeded baselines live only in this runner's workspace —
      # upload them so "commit it to arm the gate" is actually recoverable
      # (grab the artifact, commit the two TSVs).
      - name: Upload seeded size baselines (#1096 ratchet)
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: size-baselines

      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done

          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.

a) **pages.yml ordering issue**: "Build the static GEO layer" runs `dart scripts/build_blog.dart` which writes into `site/blog/posts/` in-tree — that's fine (committed sources). But then `build_site --out build/pages/root` copies statics. Wait — does the pages checkout have site/blog/posts committed? Yes. OK.

b) **The Assemble step no longer copies `site/`** — previously `cp -R site/. build/pages/root/` copied everything committed including e.g. `site/app-store/`, `site/widgets/`, `site/oauth/` — verified present in out tree above. Good. But what about files that are in site/ but skipped by _copyStaticSite incorrectly? The skip list: app/, generated page dirs (dirs under blog/ or docs/ containing index.html), sitemap.xml, llms-full.txt, blog/index.template.html. What about `site/blog/index.html` if present in-tree (from a local preview build committed accidentally)? It's gitignored so won't be in a fresh checkout. In the deploy checkout it won't exist. OK.

c) **The blog post legacy `post.html`** — committed, copied. Good.

d) **Concern: `dart scripts/build_site.dart --out build/pages/root` in pages.yml runs BEFORE "Assemble Pages artifact" mkdir** — emitSite creates dirs recursively, so build/pages/root exists. Fine.

e) **Cache-bust step** mutates `build/pages/root/index.html` and expects `href="styles.css"` and `src="main.js" defer` patterns — those are in the copied index.html, unaffected.

f) **`resolveSiteFile`** in the crawl test blocks paths containing '..' — fine for tests.

g) **test/site_test_support.dart `_repoRoot`** walks up from Directory.current — under `dart test`, cwd is the package root, fine.

h) **Potential issue — `_copyStaticSite` and stale generated dirs in-tree at deploy**: In the pages.yml deploy, checkout is clean (no in-tree generated), skipDirs empty. Fine.

i) **Potential issue — emitSite prune with `--out` when a generated dir contains extra files**: deletes whole dir recursively. In-tree, `site/blog/posts` — wait! `_generatedPageDirs` scans `site/blog` subdirs for dirs containing index.html. `site/blog/posts` has no index.html. But what about... `site/blog/2026-09-20-...` in-tree after preview build gets pruned correctly. OK.

But careful: **the in-tree default mode writes into gitignored paths, but does it also regenerate `site/blog/posts.json`?** No — build_blog does that. Fine.

j) **A subtle one**: In `_copyStaticSite`, `site/blog/index.template.html` is skipped, and the output writes `blog/index.html`. But in-tree mode, `index.template.html` stays. Good.

k) **`--out` to a dir inside repo? e.g. build/pages/root — `_repoRoot()` walks from cwd; pages.yml runs from repo root. Fine.

l) **Check `--check` exit code and stale references**: grep for `--check` across repo.

m) **The ci.yml GEO step**: `dart test/site/` runs the crawl tests which bind a loopback HttpServer — fine on ubuntu runner. Also note test/site has other tests (appstore_assets, asset_version_guard) that read committed site/ files directly — they run in the static job too (previously did they run there? They exist on main already, presumably run in test-core or somewhere; now they also run in static job — duplicate but harmless).

Wait — one thing: `dart test/site/` in the GEO step runs ALL test/site tests including appstore_assets_test, which reads `site/index.html` from the repo. That's fine.

n) **Duration**: static job timeout 8 min; building + 34 tests is fast. Fine.

o) **Edge: `resolveSiteRoot` fallback temp build inside tests** — builds on the fly when no FA_SITE_ROOT and no in-tree layer. In the static CI job, FA_SITE_ROOT is set. For local dev running `dart test/site/`, it builds to temp — good.

p) **The `--check` removal — is there any other caller?** grep.

q) **AGENTS.md references to build_site --check or committed artifacts?** grep AGENTS.md.

r) One more architectural check — the owner directive said "Add them to .gitignore". Done. But `site/blog/posts.json` is generated by build_blog.dart and still committed — pre-existing pattern, not in scope.

s) **blog/index.template.html rename** — old links to site/blog/index.html in tests/docs? The deployed URL /blog/ serves index.html which is generated. Fine.

In-tree build leaves the tree clean (all generated paths gitignored). 

Now the exhaustive hunt for new issues in the rework. Let me think hard about what's actually questionable:

1. **`site/blog/posts.json` still committed + `build_blog.dart` copies in-tree** — pre-existing pattern, out of scope. But note: in pages.yml, `build_blog.dart` runs at deploy and writes into the checkout's site/blog/posts — but the checkout already has committed copies, so it's a no-op refresh. And `_copyStaticSite` copies posts.json + posts/. Fine.

2. **`test/site_test_support.dart` imports `../scripts/build_site.dart`** — build_site.dart has a `main()` and calls exit() only within main; importing is safe. But `_repoRoot()` in build_site exits the process if not found — only called from main, not from buildSite. Fine.

3. **The crawl test's `resolveSiteFile` traversal guard**: `if (path.contains('..'))` — fine for tests.

4. **CI GEO step does not run `dart scripts/build_blog.dart`** — the builder reads committed `site/blog/posts`. But wait: is there a drift risk between `blog/posts/` and `site/blog/posts/`? If someone edits blog/posts but not the copy, CI passes but deploy... build_blog.dart runs at deploy and syncs. And pages.yml triggers on `blog/**` changes. There might be an existing guard checking blog/posts ↔ site/blog/posts sync. Not this PR's scope, but the new builder made site/blog/posts a build INPUT for sitemap/JSON-LD — is there a CI check that site/blog/posts is in sync with blog/posts? Let me check quickly. Actually this matters: the freshness gate was removed. If a post is added to blog/posts/ without running build_blog.dart, then site/blog/posts lacks it → builder doesn't see it → no page, no sitemap entry, and CI green. Previously --check would... no, --check only checked generated artifacts, not the posts copy. Let me check if there's a sync guard elsewhere.

5. **The llms-full budget guard error message says bytes** — fixed.

6. **`emitSite` stdout writes** — fine.

7. **`_copyStaticSite` copies `install.sh`, `setup.sh` etc. templates and generated install scripts** — those are committed generated (signed release artifacts per owner note). Fine.

8. **`CNAME` copied** — good, needed for Pages.

9. **`.gitignore` patterns**: `site/blog/*/index.html` — this also matches... site/blog/posts/index.html? doesn't exist. But `site/blog/*/index.html` would match `site/blog/posts/index.html` if it existed — harmless. Does it match anything committed that shouldn't be ignored? `site/blog/post.html` is not matched (no slash). `site/app-store/`? Not under blog. OK. What about `site/docs/*/index.html` — matches generated docs pages. But wait: does `site/blog/*/index.html` accidentally ignore a legit committed file? git ls-files showed committed: blog.css, index.template.html, post.html, posts.json, posts/. None match. Good.

10. **Deeper issue — `_generatedPageDirs` heuristic during `--out` static copy**: it detects generated dirs by the presence of `index.html`. changes:
    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      core: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.core || steps.filter.outputs.core }}
      app: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.app || steps.filter.outputs.app }}
      docs: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.docs || steps.filter.outputs.docs }}
      shared: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.shared || steps.filter.outputs.shared }}
      # PR-only (issue #303): a trajectory-touching diff flips this on so
      # the perf-gate leg below runs the #262 DoD gate per-merge.
      perf: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.perf }}
      # PR-only (gh-1241 REG-1): a trajectory/session/usage-touching diff
      # runs the usage-fold suite per-merge.
      usagefold: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.usagefold }}
      # Issue #1267 N1: the macOS exclusion-zone path set. Reserve only —
      # ci.yml has no pull_request trigger (dispatch-only CI); the
      # flutter-app-exzone leg gates on the SM validation dispatch itself
      # (gh-1280 idiom) and consults this output only if a real
      # pull_request trigger ever lands.
      exzone: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.exzone }}
      # PR-only (issue #551): test/integration/** changes run the no-key
      # mock-LLM integration legs per-PR instead of at tag time only.
      intmock: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.intmock }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # base...head diff for the classifier below
      # Non-PR events (main push, tags, schedule, dispatch): everything is
      # affected — the full gate always guards main and releases.
      - id: filter
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: |
          echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "shared=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      # PR classification runs through THE SAME classifier the pre-commit
      # hook uses (issue #194, AC7 + AC5/E2): one source of truth for path
      # rules, and the unknown-path safe default (full gate) — e.g. a new
      # dart_test.yaml at the repo root — now holds in CI, not only in the
      # hook. The selected stage set maps back to the same four groups the
      # old dorny filter emitted.
      - id: paths
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          stages=$(scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run |
            sed -n 's/^Fast gate scope: .*stages://p')
          echo "gate stages:[$stages]"
          # Empty output can only mean detection failure: full gate.
          [ -z "$(echo $stages)" ] && stages="size analyze test-core coverage crap dup dupx flutter integration-mock"
          case " $stages " in *"flutter"*) echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          case " $stages " in *"test-core"*) echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          case " $stages " in *"analyze"*) echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          # Issue #551: test/integration changes select the mock-LLM leg.
          case " $stages " in *"integration-mock"*) echo "intmock=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          # All nine stages selected = a shared/unknown path changed:
          if [ -z "$(echo $stages)" ]; then

## Verdict: APPROVE — 0 blocking · 2 important · 3 suggestions

I independently verified every finding against the checked-out `ai/gh-1476` branch before writing the review artifacts.

**Findings (all in `scripts/build_site.dart`, a new file so all anchor lines are valid diff lines):**

1. ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** (line 206) — Every `/docs/` page ships with no visible `<h1>`. `loadDocs` strips the source H1 claiming "the page template renders it as the headline", but `renderDocsPage` never emits one — the title exists only in `<title>`/OG/JSON-LD. Untested: the "exactly one h1" test covers blog posts only. This undercuts the PR's own GEO goal (headings are what agents index).
2. ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** (line 603) — The llms-full budget guard compares `text.length` (UTF-16 code units) against a 150 KB *byte* budget, but the file is written UTF-8. Confirmed live: 88,350 chars vs 89,026 bytes today. Fix: `utf8.encode(text).length`.
3. 💡 (line 141) — `lastmod` falls back to `blogIndexFloor` — a fabricated date that becomes `datePublished`/`dateModified` in JSON-LD and sitemap for dateless posts, contradicting the "real lastmod" discipline.
4. 💡 (line 467) — `docsLinkRewriter` leaks `..` into fallback GitHub URLs (`blob/main/docs/../x.md`) for parent-relative links. Latent today; none of the 5 curated docs hit it.
5. 💡 (line 243) — Front-matter `cover` interpolated unescaped into HTML attributes, unlike every sibling field (low risk — repo-controlled content).

**What checked out clean:** no security issues (all dynamic output escaped, raw markdown HTML escaped, no secrets in the static layer); CI wiring is correct (freshness gate in the `static` job where Dart is available; `pages.yml` rebuilds at deploy with matching path triggers); ticket ACs 1–5 are satisfied by implementation + tests (AC6 is post-deploy manual); locally `dart scripts/build_site.dart --check` is fresh and 60/60 site/builder tests pass.

**Outputs written:** `outputs/pr_review.json` (valid JSON, APPROVE), `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, `outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md` – `comment5.md`.

Do not edit or reply. --- ### Thread 19 **ai-teammate** (2026-10-10): ## Owner directive: sources-only, generate at deploy — drop the committed artifacts The implementation is solid, but the content-duplication model is rejected: right now every article lives 3× in the tree (markdown source + committed HTML + llms-full.txt excerpt). The repo should hold **sources only**; generated HTML/llms-full/sitemap get built **at deploy time**. Rework: 1. **Remove committed generated artifacts** from the tree: `site/blog//index.html`, `site/docs/*/index.html`, `site/llms-full.txt`, generated `sitemap.xml`, and the rendered blog-index list (keep a template/marker if the index needs one). Add them to `.gitignore`. 2. **pages.yml already rebuilds** (`build_blog.dart` + `build_site.dart` before Assemble) — keep that; it becomes the ONLY place artifacts exist, inside `build/pages`. 3. **Replace the `--check` drift gate** (CI ci.yml:344) with **build-to-temp + validate**: `dart scripts/build_site.dart --out `, then run the crawl/schema/llms guard tests (`test/site/*`) against the temp output. This validates the builder itself, not just drift, and nothing generated is ever committable. Hand-edited-HTML accidents become impossible by construction. 4. Keep everything else: D2 robots welcome-mat, D3 JSON-LD graph, deterministic lastmod (front-matter/registry — still the right call for reproducible builds), no-JS crawl tests. Note: the committed-artifact + drift-gate pattern has precedent in this repo (install.sh via gen_installers.dart), but that one is a *signed release artifact* where the bytes are the contract — blog HTML is pure render output, so the deploy-time model fits it better. --- ## General PR Comments **ai-teammate** (2026-10-10): ⚠️ **IMPORTANT: every /docs/ page ships with no visible `

`** `loadDocs` strips the leading H1 from each source doc with the comment "the page template renders it as the headline" — but `renderDocsPage` never renders any headline. The article opens with only the `post-meta` div followed by the body HTML, so the doc title appears in ``/OG/JSON-LD but not on the page itself. That hurts the GEO goal of this PR (headings are exactly what agents and crawlers index), and it's untested: the "exactly one h1" test in `test/scripts/build_site_test.dart:151` only exercises `renderBlogPostPage`. Fix — add the headline to the docs template: ```dart <article class="post-body" id="doc"> <h1>$title</h1> <div class="post-meta">Updated ${d.updated} · ${escapeHtml(orgName)}</div> ``` and add a matching "exactly one h1" assertion for the docs pages. --- **ai-teammate** (2026-10-10): ⚠️ **IMPORTANT: llms-full budget guard compares UTF-16 code units against a byte budget** The guard says "bytes" in both the constant docs and the error message: ```dart if (text.length > llmsFullBudgetBytes) { ``` but `String.length` in Dart is UTF-16 code units, while the file is written as UTF-8. Non-ASCII content (em-dashes, arrows, "—") inflates the byte count beyond the code-unit count — today the file is 88,350 chars but 89,026 bytes, so the guard already under-reports by ~0.8%. As more curated content lands, the guard can pass while the real file exceeds the 150 KB context-window budget it exists to enforce. Fix: ```dart if (utf8.encode(text).length > llmsFullBudgetBytes) { ``` (`dart:convert` is already imported.) --- **ai-teammate** (2026-10-10): 💡 **SUGGESTION: fabricated `lastmod` fallback leaks into JSON-LD and sitemap** When a post has neither `updated:`/`date:` front-matter nor a `YYYY-MM-DD-` filename prefix, `lastmod` falls back to `blogIndexFloor` ('2026-09-20') — a date unrelated to the post's actual publication. That fabricated date then becomes `datePublished` / `dateModified` in the BlogPosting JSON-LD and the sitemap `<lastmod>`, which is exactly the "real lastmod" discipline this PR's design section promises (and a wrong date is worse for search than none). Consider either failing the build for a dateless post (front-matter dates are already required convention — make the gate enforce it), or omitting `datePublished`/`lastmod` for that entry instead of inventing one. --- **ai-teammate** (2026-10-10): 💡 **SUGGESTION: `docsLinkRewriter` mangles parent-relative links** For a doc-internal relative link like `../foo.md` (or `../../x.md`) that isn't in the curated registry, the fallback builds: ```dart '$repoUrl/blob/main/docs/${href.replaceAll(RegExp(r'^\./'), '')}' ``` → `https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/blob/main/docs/../foo.md` — the `..` survives into the published URL, producing a broken or unexpected GitHub link. None of the current 5 curated docs hit this today, so it's latent, but it's cheap to normalize: ```dart final cleaned = href.replaceAll(RegExp(r'^\./'), ''); // resolve '.'/'..' segments before embedding, e.g. via Uri resolution return '$repoUrl/blob/main/docs/$cleaned'; ``` --- **ai-teammate** (2026-10-10): 💡 **SUGGESTION: front-matter `cover` interpolated unescaped into HTML attributes** Every other user-facing value in the templates goes through `escapeHtml` (title, description, author, meta), but the raw front-matter `cover` path is interpolated verbatim: ```dart '<img src="posts/$cover" alt="" loading="lazy">' ``` (and the same pattern in the OG/Twitter `og:image`/`twitter:image` meta and the `.post-cover` figure). Risk is low — the source is repo-controlled blog front-matter, not user input — but for consistency with the rest of the template (and defense if front-matter is ever sourced elsewhere), run it through `escapeHtml`/`Uri`-safe encoding like the sibling fields. --- **ai-teammate** (2026-10-10): Fixed. `renderDocsPage` now emits the headline as the first element of the article, exactly as proposed: ```dart <article class="post-body" id="doc"> <h1>$title</h1> <div class="post-meta">Updated ${d.updated} · ${escapeHtml(orgName)}</div> ``` New regression test `docs page renders exactly one visible h1 with the doc title` asserts a single `<h1>` (matching the blog-post coverage at `test/scripts/build_site_test.dart`) and that it opens the article ahead of the `post-meta` line.
